json.usageTitle: How the app uses this data
json.usage:
- The details lie with the person's role, each field separately, sealed with its key: only whoever has this person's key opens them (usually only you). The service only knows which fields are filled in.
- First and last name (or, without them, the nickname) are the person's name in the app: your roles and lists call them that, and the messages you send in conversations are signed that way.
- An area gets a field only when you share it (“My details”): the copy is sealed with the area's key and anyone with access to the area reads it — e.g. the area's list of people takes the first and last name from it.
- A form filled in for this person fills in the answers to questions about first name, last name, phone, date of birth, address, e-mail and nickname by itself. The import doesn't change submissions already sent.
- A share is withdrawn in “My details” (“Who got it”): the area loses the copy, but what someone has already read can't be undone.
json.title: My details as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
json.text:
Details of the persons this account runs: first name, last name, phone, date of birth, address, e-mail, nickname (Account, #/workspace/account → under “My details” → “My details as JSON”). Each field is sealed in the browser separately — with the person's key — and shared separately.
What the import does:
- First it shows a plan of changes; it saves only after “Import”.
- It changes only fields of this account's persons, named by "id" from the export. Persons without "id" or with someone else's "id" are skipped (warning) — it creates no persons or accounts and never changes someone else's details.
- A field with a new value is saved; the same value — no change. A change also refreshes the copies in areas this field was already shared with (the plan lists them); it shares nothing with new areas.
- Empty text ("") and null don't delete: the field stays as it was (it is deleted in “My details”, together with its shares).
- A value in the wrong shape (e.g. date, e-mail, phone) — warning, field skipped.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

snap.liturgy: Liturgy: canonical works, editions, texts, passages, observances, templates, assignments and explicit rules. Stable canonical IDs are in data.id; references name resources, never copied daily texts. Drafts and missing dependencies are not approved liturgical content.
snap.writing:
## Scriptorium — own texts
Texts ("text": title, plan, content, further information; the text type adds its fields), their deliveries ("delivery": when, where, what of the plan was said, what was left out), projects ("project") and text types ("texttype").

A project can be a work built from the whole down to its smallest unit: structure nodes ("node": parent, order, purpose, key thought, role, target, split by a dimension / variant, marks of the concepts that occur there, the text with its prose), rules of writing ("rule": with why and scope; without a project the own rulebook) and unit templates ("unittemplate"). The snapshot's "works" holds per work the rulebook, the tree, the dimensions and paths, the knowledge of the work (only from knowledge bases shared with this access), and per path the reading order, where each concept is first introduced, the check findings and the context of every node — read them with get_work_briefing, get_work_context and get_work_checks. In markup [[word|@id|intro]] marks how a concept occurs (intro, def, ex, use, recall).

{markup}
snap.base:
## Knowledge base entries (Cogita)
An entry has kinds ("kinds" — the first gives the name) and fields in "data" according to its kinds; what each field means — in "kinds" of this collection.
Field types: {types}.
A value may be uncertain: {"value", "state", "source": {"work": work id, "locator": "p. 23"}, "note"}; states: {states}.
A reference is the id of another entry (with its title in the entry's "refs"); a reference with a place: {"value": id, "locator": "Ps 110"}.
The field "blocks" is a statement: paragraphs {"type": "paragraph", "text"}, lists {"type": "ordered"|"unordered", "items"}, tables {"type": "table", "columns", "rows"}; a cell is a list of pieces {"text"} or {"ref": id, "locator"}. Thesis = the first sentence of the first paragraph.
Question: one kind "question"; "form" (question type) says how it asks: {questions}; a field with "when" belongs only to the given question types; "about" — entries the question tests; "needs" — what must be known before it.
Learning order: a reference field with "prerequisite": "up" — what it points to must be known EARLIER (concept → “Requires”); "down" — the entries pointed to build on this. From such fields the app computes levels from the basics (level 1 — nothing before it) and asks the general first, then the detailed.
Dates: "1999", "1999-05", "1999-05-03", "-1000" (BC); range: {"segments": [{"from", "to"}]}.
Structure (e.g. the argument of an article): a reference field with "structure": "up" — this entry lies UNDER what it points to (a step under a question, a reply under an objection); "structure": "down" — the entries pointed to lie under it. The root (no value in the "up" field) is usually the leading question. Its tree: via MCP get_related(root id, direction "in", fields: [key of the "up" field], depth 3), then again from every entry at depth 3 (at most 60 entries per call; with "truncated" the edges also name those that didn't fit — continue from them); via REST /entry/{id}: entries in "linkedFrom" with this field lie directly below — and so on from each of them (or, looking through all entries: under entry X lie those whose "up" field has value X). The order of steps is the order of their places in the work (a reference field with a place in a work from the library). Entries pointing to a step through a field without "structure" (e.g. a comment: "About") don't belong to the reconstruction — they are others' or own remarks.

format.intro:
Reservations in one document: resources (a priest's time, a hall, a house) with their rules and slots to choose, and in the export also the reservations the office sees.
What the import does (Reservations → “More” → “Import and export (JSON)”):
- First it shows the list of changes and the warnings; it saves only after “Import”.
- A resource or slot with an "id" from the export is changed in place — only the keys present in the document; what is absent stays. Empty text ("") clears a field. Without "id" a new one is created. An "id" that does not exist (or a slot already past) is skipped with a warning.
- It deletes nothing. It does not change reservations ("claims") — they are in the export for reading only.
- You can change and create only in areas you write in; the export only shows the rest.
- The title, place, note and link of a slot are sealed in this browser with the area's key — as when saving in the calendar.
- Whether someone may take a slot is decided by the service at each reservation, by the resource's rules — the import only saves rules and slots.
- Changing the time of a slot that already has reservations: the reservations move with it (the n-th day of the series to the n-th day of the new one), and those left without a day are declined; days cancelled or moved one by one return to the rhythm of the series. The preview warns about every such slot, about a number of places smaller than those taken, about a slot that stops being choosable, and about a new slot during an existing reservation.
- The export covers slots from yesterday {days} days ahead (also series running in that time) and reservations from that time.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

Document:
{top}
format.slotText:
A slot to choose is a meeting in the calendar of an "offered" resource — single or a series, as in the Calendar. The time is local (as in this browser's calendar).
{keys}
format.claimText:
A reservation — only in the export and only for reading: the import skips it. They are answered in Reservations or in the Calendar (“To confirm”).
{keys}
format.usage:
- An "offered" resource: its slots are meetings in the resource's calendar. On a page the module “Reservation” (field “What can be reserved”) shows them with the button “Choose this slot”. An "open" resource: the same module shows what is taken and asks for one's own time.
- A slot can be taken by a person with their own link or signed in (for whom — chosen at the top of the page). Anyone who sees the module sees what is free and what is taken — never who took it. "reserveArea" closes the slots to people outside that group (and the groups under it).
- Requests waiting for the office ("approval": "office") are seen by those who write in the resource's area: in Reservations (“Waiting for an answer”), in the Calendar (“To confirm”), in the bell and in “Waiting for you” (“Reservations to confirm”). Requests to join ("inviteHours") are seen by the host in the module “Reservation”.
- In the Calendar the slots to choose are ordinary appointments with the number of places taken (“2/3”); without a title they carry the resource's name. A signed-in person has their reservation in their own Calendar (“This is your reservation”).
- A form step completed “by itself — when the person chooses a slot” is done when the person has a request or reservation for this resource.
- There are no push notifications about reservations: the person sees the answer — also a cancelled slot — at their slot in the module “Reservation”.

occurrence.title: Series day ("occurrences[]")
occurrence.lead: A chosen day of an appointment — usually of a series. A day is named by its date: the day it falls on according to the series, also when it is moved. Days without an entry stay as they are.
occurrence.tail: The export lists the days of the range that are cancelled, moved or have values. An appointment that doesn’t repeat has one day — the day of its "start".

appointment.title: Appointment ("appointments[]", "points[]")
appointment.lead: An appointment has the same keys as the appointments of a page and an area ("title", "start", "end", "location", "points", "repeat" …) — plus "id", "kind", "scheme", "values" and "occurrences". For a changed appointment, a key that is missing stays unchanged.
appointment.retime: Changing the time of a series ("start", "end", "repeat", "every", "weekdays", "until", "count") changes all its days — including past ones. Cancelled and moved days not in "occurrences" then return to the series; those in "occurrences" the import writes again. Intentions and entries follow the day; when the day no longer exists, the appointment stays unchanged (the import says so). “Different from this day on” (“this and following”) is done in the appointment editor.
appointment.values: Values ("values"): "choice" and "colour" — a value or a name from the field’s list; "number" — a number; "bool" — "tak" (yes) or "nie" (no) (also true / false); "date" — "YYYY-MM-DD"; "time" — "HH:MM"; "link" — https://… or #/…; "person" — a role id. Public fields up to {max} characters. A required field ("required") must have a value — otherwise a new appointment is skipped and changes to an existing one are not saved.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- The appointments are seen by everyone who has the key of the area that sees the calendar (“Who sees” in the calendar settings) — also through an access link; when that area is public (“everyone reads”), by everyone, also without an account.
- Calendar (Day, Week, Month, List): program points stand in the grid next to their appointment; the appointment details show the place, note, link, scheme values and the day’s entry lists (intentions, sign-ups). “Now”: “Upcoming appointments” (today and tomorrow), and in “Waiting for you” — “Appointments today”.
- Page modules: “Calendar” (chosen calendars), “Event program” (an appointment with points — "points"), “Booking” (appointments to choose from); an appointment set as the area’s main appointment — in the modules “Events” and “Business card”, when everyone sees it. On a page everyone sees what they can open; a module of a public page can also be embedded as a widget on another website.
- Masses, confessions and devotions ("kind") are also in “Masses and services” (parish office). When the area that sees the calendar is public, their names and times (for a mass also the public scheme fields) go to the public plan — the page module “Masses and services” — and masses also to the notice-board printout; the place and notes are not there.
- "bookable" and "capacity" (a calendar with bookings): the appointment can be chosen in the module “Booking”; in the Calendar it shows the number of taken places, and requests wait in “To confirm”.
- Appointments have no reminders (tasks do), and the import notifies no one.

calendar.title: Calendar appointments ("{format}")
calendar.lead:
The appointments of ONE calendar: single and repeating (series — e.g. a weekly lesson plan or weekday masses), all-day, with a place, note and link, with a program (points under an appointment), with the calendar’s scheme and its values, and with chosen days of a series (cancelled, moved, with their own values). Masses, confessions and devotions are appointments here like any other ("kind").
Export (calendar settings → “Appointments as JSON”; whoever only sees the calendar: “Calendars” → “Export JSON”): the appointments of the chosen range (by default from today for a year) and the series that reach into it — each with "id".
The import changes IN PLACE: an appointment with "id" (from an export of this calendar) is changed, an appointment without "id" is added. A key that is missing stays unchanged — "id" and what changes are enough; "" or null clears a text. Nothing disappears unless the appointment has "remove": true. Before the import you see the list of changes and the warnings; the same document imported a second time changes nothing.
Titles, places, notes, links and non-public values are encrypted in the browser with the key of the area that sees the calendar — just as in the appointment editor. The export file holds them in plain text: it is your copy.
The import does not change: mass intentions (a separate format for masses and intentions), list entries (sign-ups), bookings, people at an appointment, or who sees an appointment (the calendar says that).
A document from another calendar ("calendar" with another "id") is a copy: its appointments will be added as new ones.
calendar.time: Time is local (the calendar’s time zone), without a zone: a moment "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", a day "YYYY-MM-DD", a time "HH:MM".
calendar.limits: Limits: {entries} appointments including points in one document, a program up to {depth} levels, {days} days per appointment in "occurrences".
calendar.update: Changes after an export — a new place, a removal, a cancelled series day and a new appointment:

universal.name: Universal
universal.giverSays: Who ordered it — not read out, stays in the parish office.
universal.offeringSays: Offering — stays in the parish office.
universal.listSays: Mass intentions: the text read at mass and on the notice board, the kind (single / collective), who celebrates.
universal.says: The scheme every older appointment has: all kinds and mass intentions.

calendarDataScheme.recordOutsidePublic: From outside only public fields can be given.

read.fieldType: {where}: “{label}” — unknown type “{type}”, it will be text.
read.nodeNotPlan: {where}: node {type} doesn’t fit a plan — skipped.
read.nodeNotRule: {where}: node {type} doesn’t fit a rule — skipped.
read.notObject: This is not a JSON object.
read.otherScheme: The scheme from the document doesn’t belong to this calendar — choose a scheme in the plan.

date.fixed: the same day every year (month 1 = January)
date.easter: days from Easter Sunday: −46 Ash Wednesday, +49 Pentecost, +60 Corpus Christi, +68 Most Sacred Heart of Jesus
date.advent: days from the first Sunday of Advent (−7 Christ the King)
date.christmasSunday: Holy Family: the Sunday in the octave of Christmas, and when there is none — 30 December
date.baptism: Baptism of the Lord: the Sunday after 6 January
date.nthWeekday: the n-th weekday of the month (n: 1–5, −1 — the last); with "month" only in that month, without it every month (e.g. the first Friday)
date.sundayAfter: the first Sunday AFTER the given day (not on it)

test.slot: mass time — a key from the "slots" node (only in the "mass" flow)
test.time: the mass starts in this range (one bound is enough)
test.rank: rank of the celebration (without one — of the day): 1 highest … 13 weekday
test.celebration: "any" — there is a celebration, "none" — there is none, "name" — the celebration’s name contains "name"
test.festive: Sunday or holy day of obligation
test.date: this day according to a date rule (below)
test.between: day of the year in the range "MM-DD" (also across New Year)
test.var: a variable set earlier by a "set" node; "op": "=", "!=" or "contains"
test.count: how many entries of this list are already at this appointment ("scope": "occurrence") or in the week from Monday ("week"); "mode" — only of this kind; "status": "live" (accepted and celebrated, default) or "all" (also waiting); "per": "occurrence" — at how many OTHER appointments of the week there are such entries
test.actor: who adds: "office" — those who run the calendar, "outside" — someone from outside (their entry waits anyway)
test.field: field of the entry: "set" — filled, "empty" — empty, "=" — equal to "value"

date.title: Date rule ("when", condition "date")
date.lead: A date computed anew for every year:

test.title: Condition ("if")
test.lead: The "if" node has the data {"test": …} and two outputs: "yes" and "no". Comparison "op": <, <=, =, >=, >, !=.

flow.title: Flow ("flow", "rule")
flow.lead: A flow is a graph as in the editor: {"v":1,"nodes":[…],"edges":[…]}.
flow.nodes: {"id", "type", "x", "y", "data"} — "id" unique in the flow; "x", "y" — place in the editor; "data" — the node’s settings
flow.edges: {"id", "from", "to", "out"} — from the output of node "from" to node "to"; "out": "out" (the only output, default), "yes" or "no" from an "if" node
flow.tail: A flow runs from the start node along the edges until it reaches an ending node. Unconnected nodes do nothing; nodes of another kind of flow the import skips with a word.

rule.title: List rule ("rule")
rule.lead: The rule runs in the browser when someone adds an entry or the office accepts a waiting one. Result: accept, wait or refuse (with a message — the entry is then not created). An entry by someone outside those who run the calendar always waits; the rule runs once more when the office accepts it.
rule.data: Data: "refuse" and "wait" — {"message": "…"} (what the person adding sees); "if" — a condition (below).

plan.title: Plan flow ("flow")
plan.lead: The "day" flow runs once for each day of the range and ends with a "slots" node (the day’s masses) or "skip" (no mass). Then the "mass" flow runs once for each mass of the day and ends with "end" (create) or "skip" (this time does not exist). The first matching path wins — that is how precedence is set.
plan.season: the colour of each season ({seasons}) and of special days; the node computes the season, week, rank of the day and colour
plan.feasts: celebrations: "when" — a date rule (below), "rank" 1–13, "festive": true — Sunday times, "title" — the mass title (without it the name), "moveIfImpeded": true — when displaced by a higher rank it moves to the next day; the highest rank wins
plan.set: the mass title, a scheme field (by key) or a variable (e.g. "colour")
plan.slots: masses on Sundays and holy days of obligation and on the other days; "key" stays forever — by it the preview recognises masses already planned
plan.record: a fixed entry of a scheme list at this mass
plan.texts: Texts ("value", "title", "text") may have places to fill: {celebration} {celebrationTitle} {title} {season} {seasonName} {week} {weekRoman} {sundayName} {dayName} {weekday} {colour} {date} {dateWords} {time} {slot} — and every variable from "set". Unknown ones stay as they are (the preview shows them).

field.title: Field ("fields[]")
field.key: a–z, 0–9, _ . - (missing: from the name); stays when the name changes — the values are under it
field.label: name (required)
field.level: "item" — the whole appointment (default) or "day" — one day of a series (appointment fields only)
field.public: true — the value is visible without a key: mass plan, notice board, printout; otherwise encrypted. For entry fields: only such fields are filled by someone outside those who run the calendar
field.required: true — it can’t be saved without a value
field.options: for "choice" and "colour": a list of names or {"value","label"}
field.onlyKinds: only for these kinds of appointments (e.g. ["mass"])
field.tail: Values are text. A liturgical colour is a word: {colours}.

list.title: List of entries ("lists[]")
list.lead: A list of entries at each appointment — e.g. mass intentions or sign-ups for a meeting.
list.key: as for a field; the list "intencje" is the mass intentions (also visible in “Masses and services”)
list.modes: kinds of entry: a list of names or {"value","label"} (e.g. [{"value":"single","label":"single"},{"value":"collective","label":"collective"}])
list.textLabel: the public text of an entry and its caption (e.g. “Intention text” — read at mass, in the plan and on the notice board)
list.person: caption of the pinned person (e.g. “Who celebrates”); someone from outside who signs up alone is that person
list.fields: fields of an entry (as above) — encrypted with the key of those who run the calendar
list.outside: true — people who don’t run the calendar also sign up (the entry waits for the office)
list.onlyKinds: the list only for these kinds of appointments
list.rule: the list rule — a flow (below); without it every entry by those who run the calendar is accepted

node.usageTitle: How the app uses this data
node.schemeUsage:
- A scheme saved in the calendar settings (“Appointment schemes”) works for the appointments that have it: the appointment editor shows its fields ("level": "day" fields — for the chosen day of a series), and the appointment details in the Calendar — values and lists.
- Public mass fields ("public": true) go to the public plan (the page module “Masses and services”, e.g. celebration and vestment colour) and to the notice-board printout — when the area that sees the calendar is public. The other values are opened only by the key of that area.
- Lists of entries stand at each day of an appointment. Those who run the calendar add entries; with "outside": true also those who only read it (“Submit”) — such an entry waits, and those who run the calendar see it in “Entries to accept” (bell, “Waiting for you”). Those who run it see all entries, readers — accepted, celebrated and their own.
- List rules are checked only by the browser — the server doesn’t know them, because the scheme is encrypted.
- The list "intencje" is the mass intentions: the parish office works with it (“Masses and services”), and its accepted and celebrated texts go to the public plan and the printout. Entries of other lists don’t reach the public plan.
- A calendar plan creates appointments with the chosen scheme and fills its fields and the fixed list entries right away.
node.planUsage:
- A saved plan creates nothing by itself. Only “Apply…” (calendar settings → “Plans”) computes the days of the chosen period in the browser and creates single appointments in this calendar.
- Each one gets: the kind from the plan (without it — from the scheme, and without both — "mass"), the plan’s scheme, the title from the flow, field values (also day fields) and a public title if the scheme says so; fixed entries from "record" nodes (e.g. the intention “For the parishioners”) are accepted right away.
- The created appointments are seen by everyone who has the key of the area that sees the calendar: in the Calendar, in “Now”, in “Masses and services” and in page modules; when that area is public — also in the public mass plan and on the notice-board printout.
- An appointment remembers the plan, the time ("key" from "slots") and the day: thanks to that the preview recognises masses already planned, and those who run the calendar get “Plans to extend” in “Waiting for you” when the last appointment of the plan falls within two weeks.
- The plan is encrypted with the key of the area that runs the calendar (the scheme — with the key of the area that sees the appointments).

scheme.title: Appointment scheme ("{format}")
scheme.lead: A scheme says what the calendar’s appointments are, which fields they have and which lists of entries (intentions, sign-ups). It is encrypted in the browser with the key of the area that sees the calendar’s appointments. The import loads the document into the editor; it is saved only by “Save scheme”. The keys of fields and lists stay — the appointments’ values are under them.
scheme.name: scheme name (required), e.g. “Mass”
scheme.kind: kind of appointments: {kinds} — "mass" puts the appointment in the mass plan and on the notice board
scheme.kinds: kinds to choose from for an appointment (instead of one "kind")
scheme.publicTitle: true — public title (plan, notice board), false — encrypted; missing: public for mass, confession and devotion

planRoot.title: Plan ("{format}")
planRoot.lead: A plan creates single appointments (e.g. masses) for a chosen period — “Apply…”. Once created, the appointments are not tied to the plan: they are changed like any other; applying the same plan again skips masses already planned. The import loads the document into the editor; it is saved only by “Save plan”.
planRoot.name: plan name (required)
planRoot.schemeId: the scheme of the created appointments — a scheme of THIS calendar; from another calendar it disappears on import (then choose it in the plan)
planRoot.weeks: how many weeks the “Apply…” window suggests (1–60)

kind.after: every so often after it is done

span.negative: "{unit}" is a number not less than 0
span.range: from a minute to a year

when.after: {every} after it is done, first time {from}

plan.idUnknown: it is not among your tasks
plan.idBad: "id" {id} is not an id from an export

doc.tasks: the list of tasks (at most {max} in one document)

task.who: who sees it: "me" — only you (the default for a new one); "@key" — a group from "groups"; or the id or name of a group. A change moves the task to another group
task.start: local time "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" (or "YYYY-MM-DD" — at 00:00; a time with a zone, e.g. "…Z" or "…+01:00", is converted to local): for "window" the start of the first window, for "period" the start of the first period, for "after" when the task is due for the first time (required for a new one)
task.end: only "window": the end of the first window — "HH:MM" the same day (a time before the start — the next day), "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" or "YYYY-MM-DD" (until the end of that day); a window lasts at most a year. Omitted for a new one — {minutes} minutes; omitted on a change — the window keeps its length (moves with "start"). Whoever changes "start" in an export should also change "end" or remove it
task.repeat: only "window": {repeats}; omitted for a new one — "none"
task.weekdays: only "window" with "repeat": "weekly": a list of days — {days}; omitted — the weekday of "start"
task.lasts: only "period": how much time to do it — a duration (below), e.g. {"days": 3}; from a minute to a year; omitted for a new one — 3 days
task.every: "period": how often it returns, from start to start — not shorter than "lasts", at most a year (omitted for a new one — 2 weeks); "after": how long after completion it is due again — from a minute to a year (omitted for a new one — 3 days). A duration like "lasts", e.g. {"weeks": 2}
task.remind: when to remind — a list: {kinds}; "end" — a quarter of an hour before the end, for a shorter window at the end; with "after" only "start" (when the time comes); [] — no reminders. They arrive on devices with notifications turned on
task.remove: true — remove this task (only with "id"; like “Delete” in the task window: it disappears from the lists, the history of completions stays in the archive); the other keys then don’t count
task.locked: only in an export: the title and note can’t be opened here (the task was saved with a key you don’t have) — the import won’t change such a task, it can only remove it

group.key: a short name (letters, digits, - and _) that "who": "@key" points to, e.g. "schola"
group.id: group id from an export — takes precedence over the name
group.name: the group name as in “Who sees”: alone (“Schola”) or with its path (“St Joseph’s Parish › Schola”); it must point to one group
group.readOnly: only in an export: true — in this group you can only read, so the import won’t change its tasks

node.intro:
Tasks (Calendar → tab “Tasks”) as one document: what is to be done and when, who sees it and when to remind. The export gives the tasks you see — all of them or those of one group.
What the import does:
- First it shows the list of changes — new, changed (what and how), removed, unchanged — and the warnings; it saves only after “Import tasks”.
- A task with "id" from an export is changed in place, and only what is in the document — an omitted key stays as it was. A task without "id" is added as new; the same document imported a second time adds it once more.
- By itself it removes nothing: a task disappears only with "remove": true.
- Completions (ticks and skips) are not part of the document: the export doesn’t contain them, the import doesn’t change them. A task created from a conversation stays with its message.
- The title and note are encrypted by the browser with the key of those who see the task (“Only me” or a group). You can add and change where you may write; tasks of groups you only read are skipped by the import with a warning.
- Time is the device’s local time, as in the task window: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM".
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.
Document keys:
node.kinds:
"window" — {window}: a window of time that can return ("repeat") — e.g. a prayer 21:00–21:15 daily. Each occurrence is ticked; one that passed unticked stays as missed until someone ticks or skips it.
"period" — {period}: time to do it ("lasts") that returns at a fixed interval ("every") — e.g. cleaning the church: 3 days to do it, every 2 weeks. It shows from the start of the period, and the closer to the end, the more urgent.
"after" — {after} ("every"): a counter from the last completion — e.g. water the flowers every 3 days; ticking starts the count anew.
A duration ("lasts", "every") is an object with a number at a unit: {units} — e.g. {"days": 3}, {"hours": 36}, {"weeks": 2}; several units add up ({"days": 1, "hours": 12}). A bare number, without a unit, is not enough.
A key of another kind (e.g. "lasts" with "window") the import skips with a warning. When "kind" changes, what is missing is taken as in the task window: a window of {minutes} minutes, 3 days to do it, every 2 weeks, every 3 days.
A task that starts in the past will show earlier occurrences as missed — the import warns about it.
node.groupsLead:
"who" says who sees the task: "me" — only you (a private task, encrypted with your key); a group — everyone in that group (encrypted with its key). A group is pointed to by an "@key" from "groups", its id or its name.
An entry in "groups":
node.groupsTail: The import creates no groups and doesn’t change who belongs to them. A task with a group that is not among yours, that matches several, or in which you only read, is skipped with a warning.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- Tasks stand in the Calendar: the tab “Tasks” (Now, Missed, Later today, In the coming days, Every so often, Done today, Skipped today) and the calendar grid (the bar and the “tasks” row at each day). The “Calendar” module on pages doesn’t show them.
- “Now”: the part “Tasks” — what is open now and what is overdue, with “Done”; in “Waiting for you” — how many tasks are to be done now.
- They are seen by whoever has the key of the area in "who": “Only me” — only you, a group — its people. Anyone who writes in the group can tick or skip; one tick counts for the whole group.
- Reminders ("remind") are planned by every device that sees the task — the server doesn’t send them. A phone with the app — with the system alarm, also when the app is closed (sometimes a few minutes later; the notification has “Done”); a browser — only while the page is open. They are turned off on the device: bell → “Settings” → “reminders about tasks”.
- A task created from a message is also visible in the conversation (“Tasks and appointments from this conversation”).
- Tasks from form steps (the page module “A person’s tasks”) are something else — this format doesn’t cover them.

desc.topic: An entry in "topics". The name is changed and the topic closed by whoever created it or a leader of the chat; there are no topics in Notes. At most {max} new ones in one import.
desc.message: The export describes every message as it is seen in the chat. From messages with "id" the import reads only "topic", "pinned" and "starred" — the rest is for reading: different content, sender or time give a warning and change nothing. Messages not in the document stay.

desc.newLater: A message for later, without sound: {"text": "Reminder: …", "sendAt": "2026-12-01T09:00:00+01:00", "silent": true}
desc.linked: An entry in "linked" — a task or appointment someone created from a message of this chat (message menu: “Create task”, “Add to calendar”). Read only: the import skips it.
desc.usage:
- A chat belongs to an area, and access to the chat is access to the area: whoever can read it reads the chat; whoever can write in it writes. So topics and messages from an import are seen by everyone who sees the chat — just like those written by hand.
- The service doesn't read messages: they lie sealed with the area key, and each is signed by the role you write through; the service only checks the signature. The first and last name under a message come from “My data”.
- A new message is unread for others (the bell, “Waiting for you”; the step “Read the messages” loses its tick until they read it) and wakes their phones — Firebase carries only a “check” signal, the content is opened by the phone itself. With "silent": true there is no such signal; it is unread all the same.
- A message with "sendAt" waits sealed in the service; at that time it goes out only if you can still write in this chat — and only then wakes the others.
- A topic is a filter and a place: whoever chooses it sees its messages, and what they write goes into it.
- Tasks and appointments are created from messages in the app (“Create task”, “Add to calendar”) and remember the chat, topic and message; the window “Tasks and appointments from this chat” collects them by topic.
- The import doesn't change who has access to the chat — that is set in the area.

says.prompt: The question text; for “True or false” — the statement, for a flashcard — its front, for a gap — the text with the gap [[word]] (several gaps: each on its own). Formulas: $…$ inline, $$…$$ on their own
says.hints: Hints before answering, from gentle to specific (1–3, with formulas $…$); each one revealed lowers the highest score of this answer by ¼
says.explanation: Explanation shown right after the answer, expanded (2–4 sentences, formulas $…$, sources [@work, p. 12])
says.answers: Accepted answers (text, number, date, gap) — the first is the model answer; typing never requires LaTeX
says.correct: Numbers of the correct options, from 0 (one, many)
says.feedback: One sentence for each option, in the same order as “Options” (empty: no sentence) — after the answer it stands under the chosen one and under the correct ones (one, many)
says.left: Left side of the pairs, e.g. years (match)
says.right: Right side of the pairs, in the same order, e.g. events (match)
says.leftLabel: Above the left column of the card, e.g. “Year” (match)
says.rightLabel: Above the right column of the card, e.g. “Event” (match)
says.show: Long list: this many pairs (match) or statements (many) on one card (2–{max}) — each pair / each statement then has its own card, and random others fill the remaining places; empty: everything on one card
says.share: Name of a set of parts: questions with the same name count an answer to the same part together — the same statement (many, truefalse), the same pair (match), the same word in a gap (gap), the same named fact (fact). E.g. several versions of “Which statements are theorems?”. Empty: parts of this question only
says.fact: Name of the one fact a question without parts asks about (text, number, date, one, flash, order…): questions about the same fact share answers — e.g. “When was Grunwald?” and “What happened in 1410?” with "fact": "Grunwald 1410". “True or false”: the statement it judges (without it — the question text), the same as a statement in “Several of several” with the same "share"
says.items: Items in the correct order (order); tiles of the correct answer in order (build)
says.extra: Tiles that need not be used (build); “Put in order” does not show them
says.alternatives: Other accepted answers from tiles: a list of lists, e.g. [["$B$", "$=$", "$A$"]] (build)
says.preview: math or text — how to show what has been arranged (build: formula by default; order: none — no preview)
says.join: What stands between the tiles in the preview — text, by default " " (build, order)
says.choices: For each gap [[…]] in turn, a list of WRONG options, e.g. [["Satz 2.1", "Lemma 3.4"], []] — a gap with a list is chosen from, one with an empty list is typed (gap)
says.back: What is on the back of the flashcard (flash)
says.tolerance: How far off the answer may be (number; date — in units of the precision)
says.relative: Tolerance as a fraction of the value (number)
says.quantity: Which quantity (number): Torque, Energy, Mass, Length … — then the answer may use another unit of this quantity (converted), and a unit of another quantity is wrong (12 J for a question about torque)
says.createInput: def create_input(seed): … — data to check with (code)
says.reference: def reference(x): … — the result the code is compared with (code)
says.cases: On how many inputs to check (code)
says.tests: Visible examples: [{"input": [3, 1, 2], "output": [1, 2, 3], "note": "…"}] — checked before the hidden cases (code); may be JSON text
says.radius: How close one must hit, in metres (point)
says.drawing: A drawing to move — the same JSON as in the page module “Animation”: vars, sim, controls, rules (with "goal": true — the goal), world (things to build, e.g. a balance), elements (interactive)
says.goal: When the answer is correct, e.g. "abs(x - cel) < 0.5 && y <= 0" — computed in the simulation to the end; empty: the drawing’s rules with "goal": true (interactive)
says.solution: Values that solve the task, e.g. "kat = 45; v0 = 12" or properties of things "w2.pos = 5" — shown after a wrong answer; empty: the drawing’s "task.solve" (interactive)
says.goals: Several goals (expressions) that must be reached IN ORDER, e.g. ["x > 3", "y < 1"] — instead of "goal" (interactive)
says.check: "live" (default) — the drawing shows a hit already while trying, judged after “Check”; "submit" — nothing gives the goal away, only “Check” judges (interactive)
says.explain: Entries shown after the answer, collapsed (e.g. a statement with content in blocks)
says.params: Values drawn for each question: [{"name": "a", "random": [2, 30], "step": 1}], {"name": "f", "values": [...]}, since 2026-11-03 also entries from the base: {"name": "kation", "entry": {"kind": "@rodzaj", "where": "it.ladunek > 0"}}, {"name": "zd", "entries": {"kind": "@rodzaj", "count": 4}}; in texts {a}, {kation.symbol}
says.let: Computed from the parameters, in order: [{"name": "r", "value": "mod(a, n)"}] — the expression language of drawings with lists and entries (filter, map, sortby, choose, gcd, lcm, sub, sup …); in texts {r}, {fmt(x, 2)}
says.require: Conditions the draw must meet, e.g. "a > 2*n" — drawn again (up to 60 times); if impossible, the card is not created
says.core: Key for the topics in “About”: “Check what you know” asks about it once, and how well it is known tells whether the topic is a “gap” (condition with rel "core")
says.about: Entries this question checks: its result counts towards how well they are known, and the question itself waits until you master what must be known before them
says.needs: Entries or questions that must be mastered before this question comes (e.g. “What is an atom?” before “What is an orbital?”)
says.form: How it is asked and answered — this decides which fields below are filled in: {list}
says.tags: One mistake tag for each option (one, many), pair (match), gap (gap) or position (order, build), in the same order (empty: no tag); for a passage (lines, label, span) one row per line range, "7: tag" — a flow can branch on it with the exit “wrong:<tag>”
says.use: When the question is played: in self-study and in lessons (default), only in self-study, or only in lessons. A step of a flow can say it differently with "use".
says.passage: The passage of a Library text: {"work": "<id or @name of the work>", "locator": "<place, e.g. XXII 136-213>"} — lines are numbered 1, 2, 3 … within the passage
says.lines: The lines of the passage that answer the task, e.g. "3-5, 9" (form lines)
says.roles: The roles to choose from, one per row, e.g. narrator, Hector, Achilles (form label)
says.labels: One row per marked line or range: "1: Hector", "3-4: Achilles" (form label)
says.spans: The ranges that count as found, e.g. "12-15; 30-31" (form span)

inverse.needs: Must be known before the question

text.label: Answer in words
text.says: The learner types the answer; similarity counts — a typo gives partial points. There can be several correct answers.

number.label: Number
number.says: The learner types a number, possibly with a unit; the tolerance says how far off it may be.

date.label: Date
date.says: The learner types a date — precise to the year, month or day.

gap.label: Gap in a text
gap.says: A text with a hidden word — [[word]] in the content (or “…” and the correct answers below); the learner types what is missing. Several gaps: each on its own; a gap with “Options” is a list to choose from (may contain formulas), without — a field to type into.

one.label: One of several
one.says: Several options, one is correct; the order is shuffled with every question. Each option can have a sentence the learner sees after answering.

many.label: Several of several
many.says: Several options, several may be correct — all must be marked. Each statement counts on its own (correctly marked or correctly left out), the result is their average; each is also a fact of its own, so it counts on every card it appears on. A long list with “How many at once” — each statement has its own card. Each option can have a sentence for after the answer.

truefalse.label: True or false
truefalse.says: One statement; the learner says whether it is true.

match.label: Match the pairs
match.says: Two columns (e.g. year — event); the learner connects them into pairs. A long list shows a few pairs at a time.

order.label: Put in order
order.says: Shuffled items; the learner puts them in order (drags). With “Preview” the arranged items are shown together above the list — as a formula or text.

build.label: Build from tiles
build.says: The learner assembles the answer from tiles (a formula, a negation, an expression, a line of a proof) and sees it assembled right away; there are extra tiles, and there may be several correct orders.

flash.label: Flashcard (you judge)
flash.says: Front and back; the learner turns the card and says whether they knew it.

point.label: Place on the map
point.says: The learner points to a spot on the map; what counts is whether it is within the radius.

code.label: Code (Python)
code.says: The learner writes a function transform(x) in Python; visible examples check it (input → output), then hidden cases compared with the reference solution. Each case has 2 seconds.

interactive.label: Drawing to move
interactive.says: The learner sets the drawing (sliders, dragging) and checks; correct when the simulation reaches the goal.

lines.label: Mark lines
lines.says: The learner reads a passage of a text from the Library (by work and place — the text is never copied into the base) and taps the lines that answer the task; partly right counts partly.

label.label: Label lines
label.says: The learner reads a passage from the Library and assigns a role (narrator, a character, a god …) to each marked line; every line counts for itself.

span.label: Find the device
span.says: The learner reads a passage from the Library and marks the first and the last line of a device (a simile, an epithet …); a partial overlap counts partly.

json.courseSummary: Course as JSON — export and import
json.courseLead: Kinds, entries (including statements and questions), card templates, revisions, flows, collections, looks, rules and values as one document. The import adds new things and changes existing ones in place; it deletes only what the document lists with “"remove": true”. Before saving you see every change: new items and deletions are selected (each can be unchecked), and changes to what already exists must be accepted — each can also be corrected.
json.readOnly: You can only read in this knowledge base.
json.aiTitle: Prepare from a text — in your own AI chat
json.aiHint: The app sends nothing to AI. Copy the prompt into your own chat and paste the reply (JSON) above under “Import” — you will see what will be created before anything is saved.

json.formLead: The form together with the kinds it needs (and card templates, if the document has them) — for another knowledge base or to correct as text. The same “ref” changes the existing form, a new one creates a form. Nothing is deleted.
json.progressLead: Your answers in this knowledge base — card, how well, when, how long and what was given — to keep or to analyse with AI. The import adds to your progress the answers that are not there yet; it changes and deletes nothing and never saves for anyone else.

balanced_duel.label: Balanced duel
balanced_duel.says: A minute per question; after the first answer 10 s for the rest; bonus for speed and streak.

first_strike.label: First come
first_strike.says: The first answer counts — right after it the game moves on; a mistake costs points.

sprint_race.label: Sprint
sprint_race.says: 12 s per question, then straight to the next; a big bonus for speed.

accuracy_focus.label: Accuracy
accuracy_focus.says: No rush: 35 s, no speed bonus; accuracy and streak count.

streak_master.label: Streak master
streak_master.says: Short rounds; a streak of right answers gives the most.

marathon_classic.label: Marathon
marathon_classic.says: Question after question, moving on by itself after 5 s.

async_challenge.label: Challenge at your own pace
async_challenge.says: Everyone answers whenever they like, until the session time ends (30 min).

sourceAll.label: Everything
sourceAll.says: Every entry of this knowledge base (and of the bases it uses).

sourceKind.label: Kind
sourceKind.says: Entries of one kind — also from a library or Scriptorium this base uses (e.g. quotes, sermons of one text kind); “From” narrows it to one source.

sourceCollection.label: Collection
sourceCollection.says: Entries of a saved collection — a filter or a list.

sourceFrom.label: From an entry
sourceFrom.says: What the chosen entry points to — e.g. a sermon: its quotes, comments, words, places from the plan.

follow.label: Follow a reference
follow.says: From the chosen entries onward: to what they point to (one field or all) — or backward: to what points to them.

structure.label: Follow the structure
structure.says: From the chosen entries down the structure — along the fields their kinds mark as “link in the structure” — to the very end or one level; or up, to the entries they lie under. In “Structure” it draws a tree in the order of places in the work.

filterRule.label: Filter
filterRule.says: Keeps entries that meet the rule: field, comparison, groups of conditions (AND / OR).

filterWhen.label: Knowness filter
filterWhen.says: Keeps entries for which the condition holds — also about how well they are known: this entry, its cards, what must be known earlier, what it lies under, what its field points to (e.g. facts of a period only once the period is known). Without a learner, the viewer’s knowness counts.

learning.label: Follow the learning order
learning.says: From the chosen entries to what must be known earlier (“Must know first”) — down to the very basics or one step; or onward: to what builds on them.

usage.s01: ## How the app uses this data
usage.s02Anchors: Knowledge: entries stand in “Entries” (table, tree, structure, matrix, canvas — by views), each with its own page (fields, references, learning order); kinds, templates, views and ways of adding — in “Schemas”; entry points ("anchors") add a button “In Knowledge” next to the work in the Library and in the reader.
usage.s03: Learning: templates turn entries into cards (with the key “template:entry”); revisions choose from the cards and ask; “Path” shows the learning order; views and revisions with a “Knowness filter” show what the learner is ready for.
usage.s04Landscape: Landscape (view "landscape", on a page "krajobraz"): from the learning order and knowness it computes a height for each entry (valley, ring, mountains), from the view’s grouping — the direction; there the learner chooses what to learn, sets a goal (saved privately like progress), and the lock asks to first revise weak cards on the way before the entry.
usage.s05About: Reading in Learning: before the first question about an entry from "about" comes “New topic” (title and lead, “Read more”, “Read text” to the place in the source), after the answer — the explanation; both according to its kind’s "reading", and without it — the summary or the first paragraph, then the text fields.
usage.s06: Answers: each is saved encrypted in the browser — for the learner and for the course’s intake area (Settings), where the teacher sees “Progress”; the knowness of cards and entries is computed from them. The service does not read answers; it only sees when the next revision is due and how many cards are waiting — per person and base (for reminders).
usage.s07: Pages: the modules “View” (table, tree, matrix, map), “Revision”, “Course / story”, “Entry card” read the base as the page’s reader sees it; the page’s person learns (signed in — they themselves, without an account — this browser).
usage.s08Rewards: Rewards ("rewards"): the modules “Points and streak” and “Live statistics” on a page and Learning (Motivation “Points and rewards”, tab “Rewards”) compute points, streak, daily goal, level and badges from the answers — live, with every answer; none of this is stored.
usage.s09: Other knowledge bases that use this one as a source see its kinds, entries, templates, revisions and flows read-only; the AI link and MCP read it unchanged.
usage.s10:
Other worlds ("@@name:…"): on the page of an entry and topic there is “In other worlds” — cards with the name of that base, one sentence and the learner’s state THERE; a link in the text opens such a card; a detour into another world plays that story with the bar “Physics › Newton’s laws › History: Glorious Revolution” and returns to its step; in the landscape a portal mark next to the field (close up) and a list in the topic panel — no lines between bases.
    Only those who can read that base see them (others see nothing; the owner sees “unavailable”); progress is saved in the base where it happens (answers in History belong to History); they do not affect the knowness, landscape, goals or revisions of this base.
    Broken ones (that entry deleted, name unknown) are hidden from learners, and the owner sees them in “To do”; when deleting an entry, the preview says which bases link to it.
usage.s11: Who reads: whoever reads its area (in a public area — everyone); entries are encrypted with the area key.
usage.s12Remove: The import deletes only what the document lists with "remove": true — or, with "wholeWorld": true in the head, everything of the base (or of its "part") that the file does not contain — the preview shows each, and does not touch answers or progress: a new card starts without history, and a card whose correct answer changed starts its history again (changing the "tests" weights does not change the history).
usage.s13Paths: Question paths ("paths"): the world map puts a signpost at each anchor (a status mark: not started / on the way / done), Start lists them all; the path panel shows the question, the promise, the steps with their state and "why", the length, „Go this way” (guided like „Lead me here”, known parts skipped), „Set as goal”, the closing check and „Deeper”; a chosen path is lit like any chosen route. Learner state: the value ~qpath.<id> (check passed). AI snapshot: the section "paths" in get_knowledge_setup and the signposts ("signs") in the world map.

rewards.s01Rewards: "rewards" — rewards (points, day streak, daily goal, levels, badges); several per base, each place chooses its own (module “Points and streak” / “Live statistics” on a page, Settings → Motivation → “Points and rewards” in Learning):
rewards.s02Ref:
{"ref": "@kurs/punkty", "name": "Points and streak",
   "points": {"correct": 10, "partial": 5, "wrong": 1, "first": 5, "known": 20, "fast": 0, "combo": 15, "goal": 50, "streak": 5},
   "known": {"days": 1}, "fast": {"seconds": 8}, "combo": {"every": 5}, "goal": {"amount": 20, "unit": "cards|answers|points|minutes"},
   "streak": {"counts": "goal|any", "grace": 0, "max": 10},
   "levels": [{"at": 0, "name": "Beginner"}, {"at": 100, "name": "Student"}],
   "badges": [{"id": "tydzien", "name": "A week in a row", "icon": "star|flame|target|book|bolt|crown|medal|leaf|check|rocket", "measure": "points|streak|best|known|cards|answers|correct|days|combo|goals|level|regions|map|clean", "atLeast": 7, "points": 0, "says": "…", "kind": "start|consistency|accuracy|volume|goals|exploration", "tier": 2}]}
rewards.s03Points: "points": "correct" × correctness for a correct answer (from 90%), "partial" × correctness for a partly correct one, "wrong" for a wrong one (for trying), "first" for the first answer to a card, "known" for a consolidated card (next revision at least "known.days" days away), "fast" for a correct one within "fast.seconds" s, "combo" every "combo.every" correct in a row (a break over 30 min starts again), "goal" for the daily goal, "streak" × day of the streak (up to "streak.max")
rewards.s04Goal: "goal": the daily goal — "cards" different cards, "answers" answers, "points" points (without bonuses for goal and streak), "minutes" minutes of learning; "streak": a streak day is a day with the goal ("goal") or with any learning ("any"), "grace" — this many days of break do not break the streak
rewards.s05Badges: "badges": "regions" (map regions fully known), "map" (percentage of map topics, 0–100) and "clean" (days in a row without overdue cards) are computed by the landscape — such a badge arrives when the learner opens it, and its date is saved in their progress; "kind" (optional) is the category on the page “Badges and levels” — without it, it follows from the measure; badges of one category with the same measure are the steps of one ladder: from the lowest threshold wood, bronze, silver, gold, diamond (a ladder of up to 5 steps: one each; a longer one spreads the five materials evenly, with a number within the material — “Silver II”), "tier" 1–5 (optional) sets the material directly; the built-in rules have 5 categories of 12 steps each, roughly exponential (the first easy, the highest after months), and 12 levels, each roughly twice as far
rewards.s06: points are not stored: the app computes them from the learner’s answers — changing the rules changes everyone’s points; whatever is missing is taken from the built-in rules; there are no rankings (only in live sessions)

anchors.s01Anchors: "anchors" — entry points from the Library: {"ref", "name", "work": "@work key or identifier", "locator": "p. 45–60" | "p. 1–3; 27–30" | "I q. 2 a. 3; a. 4" | "" (whole work), "entry": "@entry of this base (not a work)", "view": "@view or its name", "note"}
anchors.s02: next to the work in the Library a button with the entry point’s name appears — only for those who can read this base (the Library saves nothing); several entry points of one work may concern the whole, the beginning, the end, also several parts at once
anchors.s03: parts are separated by “;”; a part that starts at a lower level than the previous one belongs to its frame (“I q. 2 a. 3; a. 4” — article 4 of the same question; “vol. 2, ch. 1; ch. 9” — chapter 9 of the same volume)

main.s03Quote: a template may concern a kind from the library ("quote", "work", "person") or from the Scriptorium ("text", "delivery", "project") that this base uses: then the cards come from their entries, e.g. {"name": "Place of the quote", "kinds": ["quote"], "direction": "locator", "graph": …}
main.s06Random: computing nodes: "random" ({"min", "max", "step"} or {"list": ["3", "5"]}, or a list from the input "items"; "count": 4 — this many DIFFERENT at once) — draws for every card; "calc" (“Compute”): {"expr": "p0 * p1; p0 + 1", "inputs": 2, "decimals": 2} — expressions in the drawing language (mod, round, fmt, sqrt …), one per line or after “;”, each gives a value (a list — several); p0…p7 — the first number from the input, n0…n7 — how many values came, l0…l7 — all input values as a list (entries as records: sum(l0, it.masa)); "aggregate" (“Collect”): {"op": "sum"|"count"|"min"|"max"|"avg", "decimals"} — input "values" (e.g. "follow" → numeric "field"); the output "value" connects to "pattern", "answer.number" ("expected") and "answer.one" ("expected" or "distractors", e.g. "p0 + 1; p0 - 1; p0 * 2")
main.s08Card: node "card" also takes "hints" (hints — texts, from gentle to specific) and "solution" (the solution — a text with the task’s values, after the answer)
main.s09: Knowness — computed by the app, the same everywhere (it is not set in JSON):
main.s10: every answer is saved; a card remembers only a few values: when it was last answered, how much time really passed before that answer, the interval until next time and the best interval before the last mistake;
main.s11:
right (from 90%): interval = the time that really passed × 3 (answering before the due date does not shorten it); partly: a third of that time, at least a day if days have passed; wrong (below 25%): 5 minutes; right just after a mistake: 0.4 × the best interval before the mistake
    — e.g. wrong after 5 days: comes back after 5 minutes; right right after: in 2 days; right again after 2 days: in 6 days;
main.s12: card knowness: correctness of the last answer × √(10 ÷ (1 + 9 · time since the answer ÷ interval)) — right after a correct one 3.16, on the revision day 1, then it falls more and more slowly (10 % only after 111 intervals, never 0); after a wrong one 0;
main.s13: three bands (fixed): “known” from 1 (100 %) — not time yet; “due” from 0.1 to 1 — you know it, and now (or soon) it needs revising: a due date does NOT mean “I don’t know”; “unknown” below 0.1 — never asked, recently wrong or forgotten (111 intervals past due);
main.s14Weight: entry knowness: the average knowness of its cards WITH AN ANSWER, weighted by "weight" from "tests" (a card not yet asked is no evidence); what builds on it (fields with "prerequisite" — half — and dependencies from Settings, with their weight) raises it at least to that share of the best of them — never to their sum
main.s16EndWhenDone:
LESSON — an ordinary revision with "endWhenDone": true, "pick": "next", "order": "general": during it a bar “x of y cards”, at the end a summary (done, right the first time, time, cards with a wrong answer and “Practise these again”);
    "next": "@kurs/lekcja-2" — the lasting name (or identifier) of the revision that comes after this one: at the end a button “Next lesson”
main.s17Type: also steps shared with views: {"type": "follow", "config": {"field": "authors", "back": false}} — cards of the entries the reference leads to (or, "back": true, that point to these entries); {"type": "filter.rule", "config": {"rule": {"op": "and", "items": [{"field", "cmp", "value"}]}}} — cards of entries meeting the rule; {"type": "structure", "config": {"dir": "down|up", "one": true}} — cards of entries that lie in the structure under these entries (or above them); "follow" and "structure" with "keep": true also keep the cards they started from
main.s18Type: source “kind from the library”: {"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "quote", "from": "<library identifier>"}} — "from" empty: from this base and all sources
main.s19Type:
source “view”: {"type": "source.view", "config": {"view": "@widok"}} — cards of the entries a saved view shows: the view decides what is in play, the revision chooses from it; changing the view changes the revision, and its “Knowness filters” at the end work during the revision
    e.g. {"name": "From general to specific", "graph": {"nodes": [{"id": "w", "type": "source.view", "config": {"view": "@fakty/w-ogolne"}}, {"id": "p", "type": "strategy", "config": {"mode": "temporal", "order": "general"}}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "w", "out": "cards", "to": "p", "in": "cards"}]}}
main.s21Type: “Follow the learning order”: {"type": "learning", "config": {"dir": "before" | "after", "one": true, "keep": true}} — cards of what must be known earlier (or, "after", what builds on it), down to the basics or ("one") one step; "keep": true adds them to the starting cards
main.s22Type: “Sample from each topic”: {"type": "sample", "config": {"perTopic": 2}} — from each topic (the first of the card’s "about", otherwise its entry) up to "perTopic" random cards stay; a different sample every day; together with “Together” ("union") e.g. all gap cards + a sample of the rest — a spot check
main.s23Strategy:
“Way of asking” ("strategy"): {"mode": "temporal" (by what I know) | "levels" | "once" | "random", "order", "pick", "perTopic", "stackSize", "count", "levels", "minCorrectness", "endWhenDone", "rule"}
    "once" (“Whole stack, each once”): every card of the stack exactly once, in "order"; a wrong answer does NOT come back in this run; a card whose condition starts to hold during it joins the queue; at the end each topic as “you know it” or “gap” (gap: one of its cards was not fully right) with “Topic”, “See in the story” and “Fill the gaps” — this is how “Check what you know” works
    "random": like "once", but only the first "count" cards (default 20) by "order" (without "order": random)
    "levels" (“Levels”): a stack of "stackSize" cards; a right answer raises the card one level (up to "levels", default 5, 1–20), a wrong one goes back to level 1, and a right one after a wrong one also goes to 1; a card at the highest level does not come back in this run — the run ends by itself
    "minCorrectness" (0–1, default 1) — from which correctness an answer counts as right (for the stack and levels); "stackSize" (default 20) — how many cards at once in the stack ("temporal", "levels"); "rule" — what the revision changes in the strictness of the template’s checking, e.g. {"caseSensitive": false}
    "temporal": a stack of "stackSize" cards; a card leaves the stack only after a fully right answer ("minCorrectness", default 1); a free place takes first what is due (weakest first), then unknown ones (new, recently wrong, forgotten — in "order"), and when there are neither — known ones that are known least (“in reserve”: the revision does not end by itself); "endWhenDone": true — the end when nothing is waiting and there is nothing new
    "order" — order: "general" (general first — by levels of the learning order) | "text" (as in the source text — place in the work) | "date" (by the earliest date of the entry) | "random" | "given" (as they come) | "due" (overdue first); without "order": "general" in a stack, "random" in a fixed queue
    "pick" — the choice from the stack: "next" (strictly the next by order) | "weighted" (random, more often what is known less and has waited longer; default) | "sample" (a sample: from each topic only "perTopic" random cards, default 2 — e.g. "mode": "once", "pick": "sample", "perTopic": 2 spot-checks every topic; then strictly the next); another value — the import warns, works like the default; at every card the learner sees why it came
main.s24Name: “Check what you know — the whole book”: {"name": "Check what you know — the whole book", "graph": {"nodes": [{"id": "q", "type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "question"}}, {"id": "k", "type": "filter.rule", "config": {"rule": {"op": "and", "items": [{"field": "core", "cmp": "eq", "value": "true"}]}}}, {"id": "p", "type": "strategy", "config": {"mode": "once", "order": "general", "pick": "next"}}], "edges": [{"id": "e1", "from": "q", "out": "cards", "to": "k", "in": "cards"}, {"id": "e2", "from": "k", "out": "cards", "to": "p", "in": "cards"}]}} — every key question once (without a ready-made revision: the button “Check what you know” above the landscape does the same for the region in view)
main.s25Type: “Fill the gaps”: source → {"type": "filter.when", "config": {"when": {"type": "knowness", "rel": "core", "each": "any", "band": "unknown"}}} → “Together” ← (the same source → {"type": "sample", "config": {"perTopic": 1}}) → “Way of asking” {"mode": "once"}: all gap cards and one spot check each from the rest ("band": "unknown" also covers never-asked ones — first “Check what you know”)
main.s26Type: “Basics first” is ordinary steps: {"type": "learning", "config": {"dir": "before", "keep": true}} → {"type": "filter.when", "config": {"when": {"type": "knowness", "rel": "before", "band": "learned"}}} → “Way of asking” with "order": "general"; the old step "gate" is converted to them by import and export
main.s28Graph: "graph": {"nodes": [{"id", "type", "x", "y", "config"}], "edges": [{"id", "from", "out", "to", "in": "in"}]} — steps and transitions ("out" — the step’s output; a transition’s "id" and "in" may be omitted);"start": id of the first step (omitted — the only step nothing leads to);
main.s29End: THE PATH MUST BE LOGICAL: exactly one beginning and one end (a step "end", "return" or "handoff"), every step reachable from the beginning, from every step the end can be reached, every output ("right" AND "wrong" of a question, every choice option) leads to a step; the import preview names every step that breaks this (a second beginning, an unreachable step, a dead end, a loop without exit), and a flow without a beginning or without an end is not saved;
main.s31Goals: "goals": [{"id", "title", "condition"}] — goals (a flow with goals is a task); reached ones are saved with the learner’s place and stay reached; a flow with goals lets its unit sink into the valley only when it is completed AND every goal is reached (without goals: when completed);
main.s32Id: REVIEW IN ONE STEP (since 2026-11-05 — instead of several steps per question): {"id": "przeglad", "type": "review", "config": {"of": "story", "threshold": 0.9}} → "passed" | "notyet"; asks again the questions of THIS flow ("question" steps; "of": "@other-flow" — its questions) that the learner does not know yet — each once per round (wrong ones do not come back in this round; known ones are skipped as always), then shows the result (“You know 9 of 10 (90 %)”): at least "threshold" (0–1, default 0.9) → "passed", otherwise "notyet" (unconnected: the story ends with the review not yet passed, and at the end stands “Repeat the review”; or connect it to a choice “Try again” / “Stop for now” — not to itself); stores the value "value" (default “<story name without @>.przeglad”: 1 passed, 0 not); a flow WITHOUT "goals" gets the goal “Review passed” by itself ("goal" — another name for the goal, e.g. “Durchsicht bestanden”) with the condition on this value, and “Repeat the review” returns to this step (unless "review" points elsewhere); on the path it is one node “Review”; example: {"nodes": [… {"id": "q9", "type": "question", "config": {"of": "@kurs/q/opady"}}, {"id": "przeglad", "type": "review", "config": {"of": "story", "threshold": 0.9, "goal": "Review passed"}}, {"id": "koniec", "type": "end"}], "edges": [… {"from": "q9", "out": "right", "to": "przeglad"}, {"from": "q9", "out": "wrong", "to": "przeglad"}, {"from": "przeglad", "out": "passed", "to": "koniec"}]} ("notyet" unconnected)
main.s33DeszczPrzeglad:
REVIEW FROM SEPARATE STEPS (the old way, still works) AT THE END OF A STORY (in the same flow, the same questions as in the story — the same card history, never copies): a counter with the story’s name at the start ("deszcz.przeglad" — values belong to the learner, not to one story); a "set" step resets it at the start of the review, and "review": "<id of this step>" says where “Repeat the review” leads (without "review": to the beginning); each question "right" → step "set" {"actions": [{"type": "add", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "by": 1}]} → next question, "wrong" → straight to the next question; at the end "condition" {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3} — "yes" → end, "no" → back to the start of the review (or to a choice “Try again” / “Stop for now”: a story finished without a passed review stays on the plain as “review not yet passed”); a goal with THE SAME condition: "goals": [{"id": "przeglad", "title": "Review passed", "condition": {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3}}]
    {"ref": "@kurs/deszcz", "name": "Where rain comes from", "look": "dialogue", "unit": "@kurs/lekcja/deszcz", "review": "p0", "goals": [{"id": "przeglad", "title": "Review passed", "condition": {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3}}],
     "graph": {"nodes": [{"id": "p0", "type": "set", "config": {"actions": [{"type": "set", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "to": 0}]}}, {"id": "p1", "type": "question", "config": {"of": "@kurs/q/parowanie"}}, {"id": "p1ok", "type": "set", "config": {"actions": [{"type": "add", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "by": 1}]}}, …, {"id": "pz", "type": "condition", "config": {"condition": {"type": "value", "value": "deszcz.przeglad", "op": "ge", "than": 3}}}, {"id": "koniec", "type": "end"}],
      "edges": [{"from": "p0", "out": "next", "to": "p1"}, {"from": "p1", "out": "right", "to": "p1ok"}, {"from": "p1", "out": "wrong", "to": "p2"}, {"from": "p1ok", "out": "next", "to": "p2"}, …, {"from": "pz", "out": "yes", "to": "koniec"}, {"from": "pz", "out": "no", "to": "p0"}]}}
main.s34About: QUESTIONS ABOUT TOPICS, NEVER ABOUT THE UNIT: the "about" of a story’s questions lists topics; the unit ("unit") has no cards of its own — otherwise it would sink after a few right answers without the story, and its button would practise cards instead of playing the story;
main.s35Narrators: "narrators" — who narrates, depending on values: [{"character": "@piotr", "condition": {"type": "value", "value": "przewodnik", "op": "eq", "than": 1}}, {"character": "@maria"}] — the first whose condition holds narrates (without a condition: always); their portrait and name stand above the step and introduce its title
main.s36Unit: "unit": "@wpis" — the UNIT this story is: one field in the landscape (also when it has no cards itself), “Show path” shows the story’s path, and when the story is finished (with goals: and the review passed), the field sinks into the valley; a reference field of the unit with "prerequisite": "up" (e.g. “Requires” → topics) locks the story until you know that — in the landscape it stands as a mountain with a road to it
main.s37Path: the story button (a field in the landscape, a node in Learning → Path and in the module "path"): “Start the story” (new), “Continue the story” (on the way — from where they stopped), “Repeat the review” (completed, goal not reached — from "review"), “Open the story” (passed); it never practises the unit’s cards
main.s38: the locked screen (the player before a story, the same logic as the landscape): something is missing before the unit — a list from the basics with links and “Learn” at each, plus “Set as goal” (a goal in the landscape); everything learned, but there are weak cards in the chain — “Revise first (N)” with exactly those cards, then straight into the story; whoever writes in the base has “Preview anyway”
main.s39Name: a flow from a presentation (ONE story = presentation page + this flow, no copies): {"name": "The way", "look": "scenes", "presentation": "parafia/droga", "unit": "@lekcja", "narrators": […]} — without its own "graph": its map is the page’s storyboard (scenes, buttons, questions, gates, values — "story" in the page JSON, with "base": id of this base); in Learning it plays that presentation, and answers, values and the place where someone stopped count in this base (the same place as on the page); only those who can see the page see it; a question on a scene with "question": "@pytanie" counts like a "question" step here, and the scene’s "about" says what the scene is about (for the path); a review on the page: a value in "story.values", "set" gates (zero, +1 on "right") and a "condition" gate with the result, "review": "<key of the scene where the review starts>", the flow’s "goals" as above (counted from the page’s values); the page opens at the scene from the address "?scena=<klucz>"
main.s40Type: the learner’s place (private, like progress; never in an export or in MCP): step, visited, walked chapter paths, “completed” (end reached — stays also after “from the beginning”), reached goals — the condition {"type": "flow", "flow": "@przebieg", "state": "done" | "started" | "goal", "goal": "goal id"} reads them in views ("filter.when"), revisions and steps of a landscape view (e.g. topics only after a completed story)
main.s41Show: the path next to a story (2026-11-04): a map of the flow’s PARTS, computed from the graph alone — beginning and end as their own marks; “slides to read” (consecutive steps "show"/"line"/"expand"/"opening"/scene without questions), “questions to answer” (consecutive "question"/scene with questions; a step with both — both counters), “review” (a loop returning to the questions until you know them all, and a step with "review"; a single slide right before it belongs to it), “choice of path” ("choice", "chapters" and a scene with several buttons — drawn as a fork with the counter “choose 1 of 3” / “chosen 1 of 3” / “completed 2 of 3 paths”); "condition"/"set" steps are transparent; always from the bottom (beginning) to the top (end), all in a frame (scaled down; “+”, “−”, “Fit”, “Full screen”), the current part larger, outlined and with its name beside it, other names on pointing (first touch — a popup, second — opens), the legend always under the map; “X of Y” counts exactly the hexagons drawn; a part is completed when walked (questions: and learned, review: and everything known); old description: a small path map follows the step; a pointed choice option highlights its path; a click on a free step moves the story to it; on a page it also stands separately as the module "path" ({"library", "flow": "<flow id>"} — also for a flow from a presentation)
main.s42RecreatioCogitaFlow: "recreatio.cogita.flow" — ONE flow together with what it shows (export from the flow editor): {"format": "recreatio.cogita.flow", "version": 1, "flow": {flow as above}, "entities": [the entries it shows — also characters and the unit "unit"]} — imported in the same place as a course; entries with "ref" merge with existing ones
main.s44Views: "views" — views (the same steps as a revision, over entries): {"name", "mode": "table|tree|matrix|map|canvas|outline|quilt|landscape", "steps": [step, …], "query", "group", "matrix", "columns": ["field key" | "#axis:@axis"], "sort": {"key", "dir": 1|-1}, "landscape": {"nest": "field"}}
main.s45SourceAll: sources at the start — several in a row add up (e.g. sermons and comments): "source.all" | "source.kind" {"kind": "@rodzaj" or "text" from the Scriptorium, "from"} | "source.collection" {"collection": "@zbiór"} | "source.list" {"ids": ["@wpis"]};
main.s46SourceFrom: also "source.from" {"entry": "@kazanie"} — what an entry points to (a sermon: its quotes, statements, dictionary words, places from the plan; in a revision: “From entry” — a revision from the sermon);
main.s47Follow: then "follow" {"field", "back"}, "structure" {"dir": "down|up", "one": true} (along the structure fields — without "one": to the very end; "one": true — one level) and "filter.rule" {"rule"} (a source after another step starts anew);
main.s48FilterWhen:
also "filter.when" {"when": condition} and "learning" {"dir", "one", "keep"} — the same as in a revision; in a view the knowness of whoever is looking counts (the learner on this account; on a page — the page’s person or this browser),
    e.g. facts of a period only once the period is known: {"type": "filter.when", "config": {"when": {"type": "knowness", "rel": "okres", "op": "ge", "than": 1}}}; only entries whose basics are known: "rel": "before";
main.s49Sort: columns and "sort" from knowness: "#knowness" (knowness of the entry), "#due" (when to revise), "#level" (level in the learning order), e.g. "sort": {"key": "#knowness", "dir": 1} — weakest first;
main.s50Mode: "mode": "quilt" (Progress map) — a tile per entry in the colour of how well the learner knows it (new, learning, due, known), grouped like "group" (e.g. ideas by lesson under chapters: {"by": "axis", "kind": "@lekcja", "via": ["lekcja"], "sort": {"field": "nr"}, "group": "rozdzial"}); click: text, questions, “Practise this”, “Open in source”; visible in Learning → Progress (also to the teacher) and in the module “View”
main.s51World: "landscape": {"style": "world"} — the WORLD MAP instead of hexagons: topics (places) as round pillars, stories (flows) as railway lines between them, branchings as interchange stations, the unit's "Requires", the condition of a choice option and a "condition" step as tickets of sections; pillar height = cards still missing; the app computes positions (never in an import); conquest levels in the settings: {"settings": {"levelsSetup": {"levels": 0–5, "rules": [{"pct", "attempts": "any|one|first"}], "knownShare", "pillarWidth", "locked"}}} (recommended for every world and the start of every new base — guide-good-world §1.3: {"levels": 2, "rules": [{"pct": 75, "attempts": "any"}, {"pct": 90, "attempts": "one"}], "knownShare": 1, "openAt": 1}; "one" = a question may be wrong once and right at the next attempt; without the setting: 0 — nothing changes; a change of levels is explained in the import preview); blocks with parts through a field with "part" — guide "guide-world-map"; PART OF THE WORLD (2026-11-24): {"style": "world", "only": {"tags": ["@…tag"], "places": ["@…tower"], "withBase": true}} — the map shows only the towers of these tags (with subtags), these towers and (withBase, default yes) everything they require; ways, goals, reviews and counts stay inside, flows reaching a tower outside disappear; 2026-11-24 — EXCEPTIONS chosen on the map (also "only" without tags/places = the whole world with exceptions): "hidePlaces": ["@…tower"] (hidden wins over chosen), "hideFlows": ["@…flow"] (a whole story), "hideSections": [{"flow": "@…flow", "step": "<step id>"}] (from this step on: a branch of a fork disappears — the choice loses that option, the others stay;
