on the trunk the story ends there; the id of the first step of the section, stable across re-imports), "hideSigns": ["@…question path"]; hiding a tower cuts only the sections to it, the story keeps its other branches; a view with "forClass": "<class area id>" is the part of the world of a class (set by the teacher, not by an import);
main.s52Mode:
"mode": "outline" (Structure) draws the sources as roots, and under them what the steps lead to; "outline": {"chip": "field key above each step (e.g. role)", "order": "tree|text" (without "order": the reader’s last choice, and initially text order for Thomas and a tree in other works), "by": "field key by which the steps of one level are arranged first (e.g. time — story time; without "by": by place in the work)", "tie": "field key at the same place (e.g. nr)"};
    a view opened from an entry (an entry point from the Library) replaces everything before the first “Follow…” with this entry; e.g. {"name": "Argument", "mode": "outline", "steps": [{"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "@krok"}}, {"type": "filter.rule", "config": {"rule": {"op": "and", "items": [{"field": "nalezy", "cmp": "empty"}]}}}, {"type": "structure", "config": {"dir": "down"}}], "outline": {"chip": "rola", "order": "tree", "tie": "nr"}}
main.s53Group:
grouping (tree "group", rows and columns "matrix": {"rows": grouping, "cols": grouping}): {"by": "kind"} | {"by": "field", "field": "key"} | {"by": "axis", "kind": "@rodzaj", "via", "through", "depth", "sort", "group"} — AXIS: its values are entries of a kind
    "via": ["pole"] — through which reference fields an entry belongs to a value (empty: through any); "through": "pole" or "*" — also one step further (entry → through this field → another entry → through "via" → value); "depth": "all" or a number — "through" across all (or n) levels: on each way up the value of the nearest entry that has one, and an entry with its own value has only that (e.g. {"by": "axis", "kind": "@obszar", "via": ["obszar"], "through": "wymaga", "depth": "all", "sort": {"field": "nr"}}; in the landscape an upward structure field works the same without "depth")
    "sort": {"field": "numer"} — order by a numeric field of the value, or {"list": "@rozaniec", "field": "tajemnice"} — by the order in a reference field of another entry; without "sort" — by name
    "group": "czesc" — headings: a reference field of the value (e.g. part of the mysteries); in a matrix above the columns and between the rows
main.s54: column "#axis:@rodzaj" — the values of this axis (entries of the kind) the entry points to
main.s56Name:
e.g. a 20 × 12 matrix — Mystery × Area: {"name": "Mystery × Area", "mode": "matrix", "steps": [{"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "text"}}, {"type": "source.kind", "config": {"kind": "@komentarz"}}], "matrix": {"rows": {"by": "axis", "kind": "@tajemnica", "sort": {"field": "numer"}, "group": "czesc"}, "cols": {"by": "axis", "kind": "@obszar", "group": "grupa"}}}
    — 20 mysteries of the rosary (in four parts) × 12 Marian areas (in groups); in a cell: sermons from the Scriptorium (text kind “Marian sermon” with fields "tajemnica" and "obszar") and comments whose "about" points to the mystery and the area; empty cells are visible too
main.s57View: on a page: module "view" {"library": "<base id>", "view": "<view id>", "mode": "tabela|drzewo|macierz|mapa|postepy|krajobraz", "answers": "<course area id>", "rewards": "<rewards id>"} — a matrix cell (click) and an entry open below, the path in the address separately for each module; in the landscape the page’s person learns: "answers" and "rewards" as in the module “Revision”, learning counts for the modules “Points and streak” and “Live statistics” of this page
main.s30PathsFor:
PATHS FOR SELF-STUDY AND FOR TEACHING (2026-11-26) — the towers are shared, the paths are not. A story (flow) may say at its top for whom it is:
    no "use" — a path in both modes (default); "use": "self" — only for learning alone (not on the map while the teacher teaches); "use": "lesson" — only for teaching: visible only to the teacher in the mode “I lead” on the world map (Learning → World map) and to the class following them live, never to a student alone (map and list of paths).
    The map has two modes (a switch above it for the teacher): the same towers at the same places, different lines. Every tower needs a path in self-study. The import warns about an unknown "use".
main.s30Graphics:
GRAPHICS FOR SEVERAL SLIDES (2026-11-26) — "graphics": [{"ref": "@course/g/atom", "name": "Atom", "drawing": {size, elements, vars …}}] (the same JSON as "drawing"); give the parts that slides change an "id".
    In a "show" (or "choice" with "of") step: "drawing": "@course/g/atom" — the graphic as it is; or {"graphic": "@course/g/atom", "add": [parts on top], "change": {"<id>": {…}}, "hide": ["<id>"], "set": {"vars": {…}}} — the graphic plus what THIS slide adds.
    Between two slides with the same graphic the picture stays, only the text comes in anew: a part with the same "id" stays (its one-time entrance does not play again, loops go on), a part in another place, size, turn or colour glides from the old state to the new (0.7 s), a new part plays its own "motion" or fades in, a missing part fades out; parts with expressions move by themselves. A step without a graphic in between breaks the chain.
    "transition" (in a step's "config", or at the top of the flow for all its steps): "fade" (default), "slide", "zoom", "none" — how the slide's text comes in; with “less motion” always at once. The import warns about unknown values and about "@…" that do not exist.

entities.s04Blocks:
statement — an entry of a kind with a "blocks" field, e.g. a comment from templates/cogita/komentarz.json:
    "kinds": ["Komentarz"], "data": {"about": [{"value": "@bt", "locator": "Łk 1,35"}], "content": [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Holy Spirit descends on Mary as on the Apostles. Luke describes both events with the same words."}, {"type": "table", "columns": ["Annunciation", "Pentecost"], "rows": [[[{"ref": "@bt", "locator": "Łk 1,35"}], [{"ref": "@bt", "locator": "Dz 1,8"}]]]}]}
    the kind “knowledge” ("knowledge") no longer exists — old entries of it stand in Knowledge under “Old entries”
    there are no topics or perspectives — order comes from your own kinds (e.g. "Mystery" with fields "numer" and "czesc" → kind "Part"; "Area" with a field "grupa"), and entries point to them with reference fields (comment: "about"; sermon: fields of its text kind, e.g. "tajemnica", "obszar")
    a text kind from a Scriptorium the base uses is a kind here: the text has its fields next to the fixed ones (title, date, plan…) — views group and matrices arrange texts by them
    cards from statements: a template with "kinds": ["@kind with a blocks field"] and nodes "statement.thesis" (thesis), "statement.part" ({"n": 2} — the second piece; empty: paragraphs), "statement.table" ({"table": 1, "left": 1, "right": 2} — pairs from columns), "statement.subjects" (about what: values of reference fields, with place)
    text markup in a paragraph and in "markup" fields (the same as in the Scriptorium): paragraphs are separated by an empty line, "## subheading", **bold**, *italic*, [description](https://…), ^[footnote], "> quote", "- item";
    [[word|@wpis]] — a link to an entry (of this base, another base or the library) with these words; never a footnote;
    [@dzielo, p. 23] — source: a work, quote or person from the library becomes a footnote; the same markup pointing to a statement, entry or text gives a link “(see label)” in the text
    QUOTE — a separate paragraph, every line starting with "> "; words in quotation marks, the source as a footnote at the end of the words; the last line starting with "> — " is the attribution (who speaks) under the quote:
      "> “All the following years were deeply marked by this dream.” [@bosco-biografia, p. 5]\n> — Teresio Bosco"
      — shown as a highlighted block with attribution; NEVER “**Quote (T. Bosco):** “…”” in an ordinary paragraph (then it is plain text); footnotes collect themselves under the text — do not write them by hand or a “Footnotes” list
    EXPANDABLE BLOCK (long proof, details): in markup "::: details Beweisidee" on its own line, then the content (paragraphs, formulas, lists), at the end ":::" on its own line — shown collapsed, with this heading; in a "blocks" field also as a block {"type": "details", "summary": "Beweisidee", "text": "content markup"} (saved as a paragraph with this markup)
    TABLES AND GRAPHICS (2026-11-16) in any markup: a table as lines starting with "|" (a second line "|---|" makes the first the header); a graphic as a fenced block on its own: "```chart Title" (type: bar|hbar|line|stacked|share|scatter, then a table: header row, rows of values), "```plot" (y = sin(x), x: -3..3, point: 1, 2 label), "```diagram" (A -> B: label, A ..> B, direction: right), "```tree" (indented lines), "```timeline" (1815: what happened), closed by "```" — drawn everywhere the text is shown, with a data table; details: guide "guide-visuals"
entities.s04Colors: COLOURED TEXT (2026-11-21) in every text with markup (slide paragraphs in "blocks", "markup" fields, explanations and hints of questions, step texts): [these words]{.red} — the words in brackets, then the colour as a class in braces (Pandoc's "bracketed span"); colours: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink, gray, mark ("mark" — a yellow highlighter behind the text); a fixed palette, never a hex value: each colour has its own shade for the light and the dark look, always readable on the slide; it can hold other markup ([**important**]{.blue}, [$x^2$]{.green}) and stand inside it (**[bold red]{.red}**); several classes — the first known one counts; an unknown colour shows the text without colour and the import preview warns; printed (LaTeX) without colour; use colour sparingly and with meaning (e.g. the same colour for the same thing on all slides), never as the only carrier of meaning — the words must say it too

head.s03: "{courseFormat}" — the whole course: kinds, entries, card templates, revisions, flows, collections, looks, rules, values
head.s06: "{flowFormat}" — a flow together with what it shows
head.s09Ref: "ref" — the entry’s own name, e.g. "@dawid"; other fields refer to it the same way: "@dawid".
head.s10Pole: Existing entries are recognised by identifier (from an export) or by lasting name; the import COMPLETES them in place: fields the document does not mention stay, and "field": null removes a field; a list field given in the document replaces the whole previous list. Before saving, every change to what already exists must be accepted (and can be corrected).
head.s11Ref: CHANGE BY IDENTIFIER: {"ref": "<identyfikator>", "data": {"nazwa": "New name"}} — "kinds" may be omitted (the entry keeps its kinds); "id" works the same as "ref".
head.s12Ref:
DELETING: {"ref": "<identifier or @lasting/name>", "remove": true} — in "entities" (an entry) and in the document lists ("flows", "views", "revisions", "templates", "collections", "forms", "anchors", "looks", "rules", "values", "rewards", "paths"); the import does not delete kinds (Schemas → “Delete kind”).
    The preview lists every deletion by name with what points to it; each can be unchecked; nothing disappears silently.
    References to the deleted entry in reference fields of other entries (e.g. "wymaga", "pole", a question’s "about") and in collections are removed from them in the same save — the preview says from which. If something else points to it (a step or the "unit" of a flow, a view, a revision, a template, an entry point, a statement cell), the save fails: fix it in the same document, delete it too, or uncheck the deletion.
    Learners’ answers and history stay: cards of deleted entries simply do not count (progress, statistics, landscape); the entry can be restored from the version history, and then its answers count again.
    The same entry changed and deleted in one document — it is only deleted (with a warning).
head.s13: There is ONE save: new kinds (with lasting names), kind changes, new entries, entry changes, views and the rest, and deletions — all or nothing. The identifiers of new things in the preview are the ones that will be saved.
head.s14: Size: at most 20 000 items including deletions (one entry up to 4 MB, all of them sealed together up to about 150 MB). Up to 2000 items and 16 MB go in one request; a larger save is sent in parts and still written in ONE transaction — all or nothing (a 4 MB file is one preview and one save, about 6 MB transferred).
head.s12Whole:
WHOLE WORLD: "wholeWorld": true in the head of a course document (next to "format") makes the file the whole knowledge base. What the file contains keeps its identifiers (as always); everything else of this base is deleted in the same save — entries, and structures of the kinds a course carries ("templates", "revisions", "flows", "looks", "rules", "values", "collections", "views", "forms", "anchors", "rewards", "paths"). Never deleted: kinds, "settings", feedback, learners' answers and progress.
    The preview starts with the line "WHOLE WORLD: … will be deleted" and lists every deletion by name; each can be unchecked. References work as with "remove": true (reference fields and collections lose them; a flow step, a view, … that still points at a deleted item stops the save). What the file does not contain but points at (an identifier or a lasting name in a value) stays, with a warning. An export of the base, imported again with "wholeWorld": true, deletes nothing.
    PARTS: "part": "<name>" in the head (e.g. "mechanics", also without "wholeWorld") marks everything the file creates or changes as belonging to that part. With "wholeWorld": true only items of THAT part are deleted; other parts and items that never came with a part stay (the preview counts the latter). An item belongs to the part it last came with — import a part once with "part" to give its existing items the part.
head.s15To: The save fails if something would point to a kind or entry that does not exist (e.g. a "to" field with an unknown kind, a value with a nonexistent identifier, a reference to a new thing unchecked in the review) — the list says which item and which field.
head.s16Kinds: A kind can be given by its lasting name ("kinds": ["@wywod/krok"]) — it is found even after it is renamed.
head.s17:
A name with “/” is LASTING: it stays with the entry (also with a view, entry point, template, form, kind), and the same document imported a second time changes the same things instead of creating new ones; letter case does not matter.
    Reconstruction steps: "@<work key>/<rekonstrukcja>/<krok>", e.g. "@kowalski2020/calosc/pytanie", "@kowalski2020/wstep/arg1" — each reconstruction of one work has its own middle part.
    Lasting names are shared by the whole base: a document that hits entry names from another document changes them (the preview says so) — another reconstruction needs another middle part (e.g. "calosc-2").
    Names without “/” work only within their document. Kinds and entries share names, each document kind (views, entry points, templates…) has its own: an entry point "@q" does not change the entry "@q".
    In a reference field and in a cell reference ("ref") a name that leads nowhere is dropped (with a warning naming the entry and field); in a text field "@author/year" is text and stays.
head.s18: A work, person or quote from the library is given by its key or identifier ("@kowalski2020") — only from libraries this base uses (More → Settings → Sources); they are not created here.
head.s20: The export writes lasting names, and the identifiers of its own entries, kinds and documents in views, templates, revisions, flows, collections and forms as "@name" — it can be imported into another base.
head.s21: Who reads: the base is read by whoever reads its area. In a public area (when the base is open: Settings → Who reads) everyone, without an account — the whole base, including question answers and drafts.
head.s22: Single entries are not published: what is to be public goes into a separate base in a public area (entry → Who sees → Move; the identifier stays). Page modules (revision, flow, entry card) read the base as the page’s reader sees it.
head.s12Feedback: FEEDBACK DONE (2026-11-22): "feedback": [{"id": "<feedback id from get_feedback>", "state": "done", "note": "what was changed"}] in the head of a course document marks feedback items as done in the same all-or-nothing save as the rest of the file. The preview lists each (accepted by default, can be unticked); nothing is marked until the owner confirms the import. The note is shown in the app and by get_feedback. An unknown id is a warning, not an error. "state": "open" reopens an item. Feedback items are never created, changed in their text or deleted by an import.

usage.s01: ## How the app uses this data
usage.s02: The form appears in Knowledge → “Add” next to the other ways of adding; row by row (or pasted text) it creates entries of its kinds — before saving you see what will be created and what was skipped.
usage.s03: Saved entries are ordinary entries of the base: they appear in “Entries” and in views, and card templates turn them into cards for Learning; new kinds and templates from the document work as if added by hand.
usage.s04: Who sees it: whoever reads the base; whoever can write in it adds. Importing a form does not add any entries by itself.

head.s02: Format: "{schemaFormat}" (the same as the schema), version 1:
head.s04Kinds: "kinds" — the kinds the forms need; without them they must already exist in this knowledge base (recognised by "ref", name or built-in identifier).
head.s05Templates: "templates" — card templates for these kinds (optional): {"ref", "name", "kinds": ["@rodzaj"], "direction", "graph", "tests", "asks"} ("tests" — what their cards check and how strongly, "asks" — which fact they ask about, as in a course).
head.s06Ref: A form with the same "ref" as an existing one changes it in place; a different one creates a new form. Nothing is deleted.
head.s07Ref: "ref" — your own name, e.g. "@miejsce"; within the same document it refers to the kind ("kind": "@miejsce", "to": ["@miejsce"]).

kinds.s02Name: "name" — name, "label" — label pattern, e.g. "{givenNames} {surname}", "tells" — the field that tells namesakes apart,
kinds.s04Builtin:
"builtin" — a change to a built-in kind (person, work, quote — from the library; text, delivery, project — from the Scriptorium; question);
    there is no other built-in content: the base owner writes the kinds or imports a ready-made schema (below)
kinds.s06Structure:
"structure" (reference) — a link in the STRUCTURE (e.g. the argument of an article): "up" — this entry lies UNDER what it points to (step → step above: “Belongs to”); "down" — the entries pointed to lie under it (“Arguments for”);
    the view “Structure” with a "structure" step draws a tree from this in the order of places in the work; such a field does not make a statement an “interpretation”
kinds.s07Part: "part" (reference) — BLOCK WITH PARTS (world map): "up" — the entry is a part of the block it points to; "down" — the block points to its parts; never together with "prerequisite" on the same field (then it counts only as a prerequisite); a part belongs to one block; without such a field there are no blocks — guide "guide-world-map";
kinds.s07Tag: "tag": "up" (reference) — TAGS (world map, 2026-11-22): what the field points to are tags of this entry; a tag is any entry (usually of an own kind "Tag"), and the tag fields of a TAG name its PARENT tags — a network with levels where a subtag may belong to two or more parents (not a strict tree); a tower carries the tags of its entry and of its block ("part": "up"); a parent tag shows all towers below it across all levels, the learner chooses a tag on the map and refines with a subtag (only that slice is drawn), "Check what you know" and an "explore" step with a tag in "scope" check only the towers below it; no circles (the import warns and the circle is cut); read the existing tags first (MCP get_knowledge_setup, section "tags"); not the same as the mistake "tags" of a question; example: {"key": "nad", "label": "Belongs to", "type": "ref", "multi": true, "tag": "up", "to": ["@k/tag"]} — guide "guide-world-map" §5b;
kinds.s08External:
"external": true (reference) — the field may also point to entries and stories of ANOTHER knowledge base ("@@historia:@historia/rewolucja-1688", see “OTHER WORLDS” above) — as an offer “In other worlds”, never as a requirement (no "prerequisite" and no "structure"); the editor shows “Link to another world” next to it;
    e.g. {"key": "swiaty", "label": "In other worlds", "type": "ref", "multi": true, "external": true}
kinds.s09When: "when" — a field only for some values of a choice field of the same kind: {"field": "typ", "values": ["bitwa", "traktat"]} — ONE kind with a field “type” instead of a separate kind for each type; the editor shows the field only for these values
kinds.s11Form: a question with a number and quantity: {"form": "number", "prompt": "What torque…?", "answers": ["12"], "unit": "N·m", "quantity": "Torque", "tolerance": 0.1} — “12 N·m” and “0.012 kN·m” are correct, “12 J” is not (energy, although the dimension is the same)
kinds.s14To: "to" (reference) — which kinds it points to: ["@ref of a kind from this document", "Kind name", "work"]; empty — any
kinds.s15Locator:
"locator": true (reference with a place) — each value is {"value": "@dzielo", "locator": "Ps 110"}: a psalm is the Bible from the library + the place, a dictionary entry is the lexicon + “p. 23”; the app reads places in Scripture (Ps 110 · Lk 1:46-55) and searches by them; the text of the Bible is not stored
    e.g. {"key": "miejsce", "label": "Place in Scripture", "type": "ref", "to": ["work"], "locator": true}, and in the entry: "miejsce": {"value": "@bt", "locator": "Ps 110,1-7"}
kinds.s17:
ready-made schemas are files in the repository, imported like any schema (Knowledge → Schemas → Entry kinds → “Schema as JSON” → Import): templates/cogita/komentarz.json (Comment: “About” — references with a place to any entry, “Content” — blocks; with card templates “Thesis” and “Table from content”),
    templates/cogita/slownik.json (Language, Word, Translation, Synonyms, Antonyms — with “Vocabulary” templates), templates/cogita/psalterz.json (psalm with its place in Scripture, breviary places),
    templates/cogita/komentarz-biblijny.json (Comment with arguments for and objections, biblical Comment on a passage of Scripture),
    templates/cogita/pytania.json (one question schema: the built-in kind “Question” with its question types and fields, ways of adding many questions at once — true/false, answer in words, flashcards — and the view “Questions by type”),
    templates/cogita/podstawy.json (learning order: “Concept” with the field “Requires” — "prerequisite": "up" —, “what is it” cards, the view “From the basics” and a way to add concepts with what they require; an atom example to import as a course: templates/cogita/przyklad-atom.json),
    templates/cogita/fakty.json (facts and sources — from any source: a novel about a real person, a textbook, reportage, memoirs, a recording: “Fact” — one claim about the world with a keyword, kind, when, where, about whom, period, source with place, how the source presents it, an assessment after checking (confirmed, disputed, simplified, false, fiction…) and other sources; “Period” — an era or stage with its duration; cards “When?”, “What is known?”, “Is it right?”; views by period, timeline, by assessment and kind, from the basics),
    templates/cogita/zbior.json (a set of items to recognise and tell apart — prefaces and prayers, hymns, psalms, articles of a law, pieces, pictures: “Item” with number, designation, beginning, what it is about, distinguishing marks, image or sound, group, place in works, items easily confused with it and the difference, use; “Group” — a section with what distinguishes it; cards “Which one is it?” by beginning or image, beginnings ↔ designations, “How does it differ?”; views by number, groups, similar items and differences),
    templates/cogita/ksiazka-AI.md (how to prepare any book with AI in two steps: the Library with the full text, then a selection menu — scope, layers, questions, learning order, revisions — and a Cogita course),
    templates/cogita/wywod.json (description of a work: “Argument step” — role (question, thesis, argument, objection… or thread, part of a piece, event, stage, description), place in the work, content, key passage, “Belongs to” — a link in the structure, also in several structures at once, story time; “Stable element” — concept, character, place, motif… in the work or across works (“General”); Comment — one’s own remark; views “Argument” (tree, text order, story time), “Stable elements”; cards with strict checking: passages ↔ theses, thesis for a passage, work of a thesis, meaning of an element; how to prepare the text and structure of a work for AI in two steps: templates/cogita/wywod-AI.md)

forms.s01Forms: "forms" — add forms (they belong to the schema): {"ref", "name", "says", "graph", "keys", "paste", "order"}
forms.s02Pick: node "pick" — a choice made at the start, kept for all rows: "config": {"label", "kinds": ["@rodzaj"], "many", "optional", "value": ["@wpis"]}
forms.s03Entry:
node "entry" — an entry from each row: "config": {"kind": "@rodzaj", "also": ["@inny rodzaj"] (kind chosen for each value; in a list the prefix “Kind name: …”), "label", "many" (several in a row), "optional": true (may stay empty — the entries it leads to are created without it), "reuse": "same|never", "identity": ["pole"],
    "fields": {"pole": {"from": "type|ask|fixed", "value": "text"}}} — type: typed in the row, ask: set at the start ("value" — default), fixed: a fixed value
forms.s04Id:
edge {"id", "from": node, "out": "out", "to": node "entry", "in": key of a reference field} — fills this field with the entry from the node "from";
    several edges to a field that takes several values: values in order by the position of the nodes (top to bottom); an entry is created when all connected values are in the row
forms.s05Order: "order": ["id of an entry node"] — the order of fields in a row (Enter, columns of a pasted list); without it as on the canvas

body.s02Show: pairs: left and right side in the same order; a long list with "show" (2–{showMax}) — that many pairs on a card, each pair has its own card, the ones the learner does not know yet come back
body.s03Show: parts (2026-11-01): every question asks about parts, and each part is a fact counted separately — a pair (match), a statement (many: correctly marked or correctly left out, the result is the average; with "show" each statement has its own card), a word in a gap (gap with several gaps); a question without parts (text, number, date, one, truefalse, flash, order…) has one part, only with "fact" (the fact’s name; "#strona" = that side of the entry from "about", the same fact as a template card with "asks"); "share" (a name) makes questions with the same name share the same parts — one answer counts for every card that asks about it; "truefalse" with "share" is a statement, the same as in "many" with the same "share"
body.s04Ref: e.g. {"ref": "@q-lata", "kinds": ["question"], "data": {"form": "match", "prompt": "Match the year with the event", "left": ["1410", "1569", "1791", "1918"], "right": ["Battle of Grunwald", "Union of Lublin", "Constitution of 3 May", "Regaining independence"], "leftLabel": "Year", "rightLabel": "Event", "show": 3}}
body.s05Ref: e.g. {"ref": "@q-atom", "kinds": ["question"], "data": {"form": "one", "prompt": "What is in the nucleus of an atom?", "options": ["Electrons", "Protons and neutrons", "Only neutrons"], "correct": [1], "about": ["@atom"]}}
body.s06Ref: e.g. {"ref": "@q-orbital", "kinds": ["question"], "data": {"form": "truefalse", "prompt": "One orbital can hold at most two electrons.", "value": true, "about": ["@orbital"], "needs": ["@q-atom"]}}
body.s07Gap:
"gap" — [[word]] in the content is a gap (the learner sees “…”), and without "answers" the correct answer is that word; several gaps — each on its own (result: the share of correct gaps);
      "choices" — for each gap in turn a list of WRONG options: a gap with a list is chosen from (the correct word is added automatically, formulas allowed), one with an empty [] — typed
body.s08: FORMULAS: $…$ inline, $$…$$ on their own — in the question, options, pairs, items, tiles, hints, explanation; \$ is a plain dollar; typing an answer never requires LaTeX
body.s09Hints: "hints" — hints before answering (1–3, from gentle to specific): each one revealed lowers the highest score of this answer by 0.25 (one — at most 0.75);
body.s10Explanation:
"explanation" — explanation (markup, 2–4 sentences, formulas, sources [@dzieło, p. 12]) right after the answer, expanded; "explain" — entries after it, collapsed;
      story slides at the start of "explain" (entries of a kind with the field “Content in blocks”, shown by a flow’s "show" step) come FIRST after the answer, drawn as in the player (title, text, quotes with “> — Author”, formulas, footnotes), collapsed; under an expanded one: “See in the story” (a preview of the story at this slide: saves nothing; first a story already started, then a deeper one before the review, with the detour ladder “Stage 1 › The nine-year-old’s dream”) and “Questions on this slide (N)” with “Practise”; questions about the same starting slides are one map field “Questions” next to “Stories”; "explain" pointing to the UNIT of a story (“Part of the story”, when the question covers the whole story, e.g. a timeline) — the field “Whole story” of that story, and “See in the story” opens it from the start; do not put a [@klucz] citation into "prompt" (the import warns) — the source belongs in "explanation";
body.s11Feedback: "feedback" (one, many) — one sentence for each option, in the order of "options" ("" — no sentence): after the answer it stands under the chosen one and under the correct ones
body.s13Code: "code" — "tests": visible examples [{"input": …, "output": …, "note": "…"}] (JSON values or JSON text), checked before the hidden cases from "createInput"/"reference"; each case has 2 s; result: the share passed
body.s15: EXPRESSION LANGUAGE in generators (let, require, where, {…}, “Compute”):

question.head: question — ONE kind "question"; "form" (the question type) says how it is asked, and it decides which fields are filled in (in knowledge worlds the app grades every answer — do not use "flash", which the learner grades alone: guide-good-world §1.4):

questionExample.right: ["Battle of Grunwald", "Union of Lublin", "Constitution of 3 May"]
questionExample.feedback: ["Too few — count the empty set too.", "", "Yes: 2^3 = 8.", "Too many."]

aiPrompt.entities: List the people, places, works and other things in the text as entries.
aiPrompt.statements: Split the text into statements — entries of a kind with a "blocks" field ({kinds}). Each begins with a thesis — one short sentence; then paragraphs, lists, tables; references to entries as {"ref": "@…", "locator": "…"} in cells or [[word|@ref]] in a paragraph.
aiPrompt.statementsMissing: this base does not have one yet: add to "kinds" {"ref": "@komentarz", "name": "Comment", "label": "{content}", "fields": [{"key": "about", "label": "About", "type": "ref", "multi": true, "locator": true}, {"key": "content", "label": "Content", "type": "blocks"}]}
aiPrompt.questions: Write questions from the text that check knowledge (one kind "question"), using different question types ("form": text, one, many, truefalse, match, order, gap, number…; every answer graded by the app — no "flash", which the learner grades alone) — pick the type that fits what you ask (dates and their events: "match" with "show"; a statement to judge: "truefalse"). First questions about general things, then specific ones: a question that requires knowing the answer to another has "needs": ["@that-one"]; "about" points to the entries the question checks.
aiPrompt.flow: Build a flow (format {flowFormat}): steps showing statements and questions; all texts are statements (entries with a "blocks" field), not text of the flow.
aiPrompt.schema: Propose kinds (kinds) with fields that describe such entries.
aiPrompt.answerOnly: Reply ONLY with a JSON document in the format "{format}" (version 1), without comments.
aiPrompt.useRefs: Use your own "ref" names (e.g. "@david") and refer to entries with them.

top.library: the knowledge base the answers come from: {"id", "name"} — the import refuses another base; omitted — import into the base open here
top.answers: answers (below), at most {max} in one import

library.name: name of the knowledge base (information only)

answer.id: identifier of the answer from the export — an answer already in your progress is skipped; without "id" the answer is new (unless there is already an answer to the same card "key" at the same moment "at")
answer.key: card: question and direction ("question|direction" or just the question) — required, up to {max} characters; only such a card of this base counts the answer
answer.question: the card’s question (the part of "key" before "|"); omitted — from "key"
answer.direction: the card’s direction (the part of "key" after "|", e.g. "a-b"); omitted — from "key"
answer.fingerprint: a fingerprint of what was the correct answer at the time — when the card’s content changes, old answers stop counting; omitted — the answer always counts
answer.at: when: ISO date and time ("2026-10-28T18:03:11Z") or milliseconds since 1970 — from 2020 until today
answer.correctness: how well: a number from 0 (wrong) to 1 (right), fractions for partly correct answers; true/false also
answer.ms: how long the answer took, in milliseconds (at most a day)
answer.given: what was given, briefly (up to {max} characters — longer is cut)
answer.via: where from: a revision, session or flow (e.g. "revision:<id>") — information only, for analysis
answer.hints: how many hints the learner revealed before answering (each lowers the highest score by 0.25) — information only
answer.params: a task from a generator: the drawn values, e.g. {"a": 37, "n": 5}, drawn entries as "@identifier", short lists ["…", "…"] — which version came up; information only
answer.seed: the draw number of a generator task — with it exactly the same task is created (the same values and entries); information only
answer.text: information only, from the export: what the card asked, in words — the import does not read it

usage.title: How the app uses this data

progress.title: My progress as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
progress.text:
Your answers in one knowledge base: to which card, how well, when, how long and what was given — to keep or to analyse (e.g. with AI: what is difficult, how answer times change). In the app: Learning → knowledge base → “Progress” → “My progress as JSON”, #/workspace/learn/<baza>/postepy.
What the import does:
- It first shows a plan; it saves only after “Import”.
- It adds answers only to YOUR progress in the base open here — never to anyone else’s (the document does not say whose they are: it is always the progress of the person importing). It rejects a document from another base ("library.id").
- It skips an answer whose "id" is already in your progress — the same export imported a second time changes nothing. An answer without "id" is new (unless there is already an answer to the same card at the same moment "at").
- It changes and deletes nothing: an answer has happened.
- It saves new answers as new batches of {perBatch}, sealed in the browser for you (and for the course’s intake area, if the base names one — leaders see them in “Learners’ progress”), like every answer from learning. Without internet they wait on this device.
- An answer to a card that does not exist in this base is saved with a warning — it counts only once such a card exists. An answer in the wrong shape — a warning, skipped.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

paths.s01Paths: "paths" — QUESTION PATHS (2026-11-12): a learner often arrives with a question, not with a place („Who was Don Bosco?”, „Why did he found the Salesians?”). A path is an OFFER on the world map: it never changes prerequisites, order, tower heights, knowness or levels; a learner who skips it loses nothing (progress stays in the places and cards).
paths.s02Shape: {"ref": "@…/p/…", "name": "<the question>", "promise": "<one sentence: „After this you can say …”>", "anchors": [...], "steps": [...], "check": {...}, "deeper": "@…/p/…"} — "title" = "name".
paths.s03Steps: "steps" (in order): {"place": "@place", "level": <n>?, "why": "<why this step>"} — a place (topic); without "level" the step is done when the tower is passable ("openAt"), with "level" when it has that level (SPIRAL: the same place again, higher) · {"flow": "@story", "from": "<step id>"?, "why"} — a story (from that step); done when its sections are travelled (or the whole story is done).
paths.s04Anchors: "anchors" — where the path is offered (no coordinates — the app puts a signpost next to the anchor): "home" (Start), "@place" (a place or an interchange station), {"flow": "@story", "step": "<step id>"} (a fork — a "choice" step — or a step on a track). Several paths at one anchor share one signpost; Start lists all paths („What do you want to find out?”).
paths.s05Check: "check" — the closing check: {"questions": ["@question", …]} (1–3 questions; passed when each was last answered fully right) or {"slide": "@slide"} („Now you can answer…”). A path is done when its steps are done and its check is passed (per learner); without "check" when its steps are done. "deeper" — a deeper path, offered after this one („Deeper”).
paths.s06Checks: The import warns with the path's name: an unknown place, story or "from" step, an anchor that does not exist, a loop ("deeper" back to this path; the same step twice in a row), more than 3 questions; on the map the author also sees a step that is not on the world map. Removal: {"ref", "remove": true} in "paths". Full description: guide-world-map §10.
paths.s07Example: e.g. {"ref": "@bosko/p/dlaczego-salezjanie", "name": "Dlaczego ksiądz Bosko założył salezjanów?", "promise": "Potem powiesz, dlaczego powstało Zgromadzenie i kto do niego należał.", "anchors": ["@bosko/t/1855", {"flow": "@bosko/f/glowna", "step": "w5"}], "steps": [{"place": "@bosko/t/1854", "why": "Tu pada nazwa „salezjanie”."}, {"flow": "@bosko/f/zgromadzenie", "from": "s3", "why": "Wątek Zgromadzenia aż do 18 grudnia 1859."}, {"place": "@bosko/t/1854", "level": 2, "why": "Druga runda: szczegóły."}], "check": {"questions": ["@bosko/q/zgromadzenie-1", "@bosko/q/zgromadzenie-2"]}, "deeper": "@bosko/p/najwazniejsze"}

subject.label: Entry from a knowledge base
subject.use: At the top of the page, a choice of one entry of a knowledge base (◀ ▶ along the list); “Entry card” modules without their own entry show this one. One page for all characters, places, concepts. The entries are seen by whoever can read the base (public area: everyone).
subject.keyLibrary: id of the knowledge base — its entries are to choose from
subject.keyOf: optional: the name of a kind (e.g. “Postać”) — only entries of this kind
subject.none: No entries to choose — the base is empty or you can't read it.
subject.hint: The entries of this knowledge base are to choose from. Whoever can read the base sees them: if its area is public (and the base open), everyone — then the whole base is public, also question answers and drafts. “Entry card” modules without their own entry will show the chosen one.

fromEntry.noBaseWriting: There is no knowledge base that uses this scriptorium, nor one in its area — create it in Knowledge.
fromEntry.noBaseBooks: There is no knowledge base that uses this library, nor one in its area — create it in Knowledge.

entity.missing: This entry doesn't exist (or was merged with another one).
entity.outsideHint: These values remained after the kind changed — the field was removed or its type changed. They stay until you decide.
entity.askDelete: Delete this entry? It stays in the version history.
entity.linksChanged: What this entry is about has changed
entity.outline: The project plan is edited in the Scriptorium ({n} items).
entity.sourceWork: a work from the library (this base's sources)
entity.listPh: one item per line, in order
entity.noCards: No card is made from this entry yet — add a template for its kind or write a question.
entity.mergeHint: All references to the duplicate will move to this entry; the duplicate will disappear (it stays in the history).
entity.noVersions: There are no earlier versions yet.
entity.searchEntry: Search for an entry (Scripture, quote, another statement…)
entity.thesisQuestion: — this is a question; the answer will be a statement that refers to it.
entity.thesisMissing: Start with the sentence that says the most important thing — that is the thesis (the entry's name, the front of the card in learning).
entity.thesisLong: The first sentence has over {n} characters — shorten the thesis, leave the development for the following sentences.

kind.name: Kind name
kind.label: Label pattern
kind.noFieldUsed: — the pattern doesn't use any field yet.
kind.baseHint: The fields of a built-in kind stay (built-in tools use them: footnotes, cards, answer checking) — you can rename them and add your own.
kind.readingHint: This is how a learner sees an entry of this kind: “New topic” before the first question and the explanation after the answer. Fields in braces, notation as in a text (**bold**, *italic*, ## subheading, footnote [@work, p. 12]). The first paragraph is the lead, the rest after “Read on”; a list on its own line under a bold subheading is folded; a part up to an empty line in which all fields are empty disappears. Empty pattern: the summary or the first paragraph, then the text fields.
kind.badKey: Key “{key}”: letters, digits and _, starting with a letter.
kind.removeHint: When you remove a field or change its type, the entries' values stay as “outside the scheme” until someone decides about them.
kind.says: What it means (for JSON and AI)
kind.targets: To which kinds (empty — any; also from libraries this base refers to)
kind.structUp: ↑ points to the entry above (this entry lies under it)
kind.structDown: ↓ points to entries below (they lie under this entry)
kind.orderUp: ↑ what it points to must be known first (e.g. “Requires”)
kind.orderDown: ↓ what it points to builds on this entry (e.g. “Leads to”)
kind.tag: Tag field: what it points to are tags of the entry (on a tag: its parent tags) — the world map filters by them

field.label: Field
field.says: The values of one field — of this entry or of the entries coming in from the left.

statementThesis.label: Thesis
statementThesis.says: The first sentence of block content — the thesis (of this entry or of the entries coming in from the left; any kind with a “Block content” field).

statementPart.label: Content part
statementPart.says: Block number n (1, 2, …) of block content: a paragraph as text, a list — each point separately, a table — each row (“Lk 1:35 — Acts 1:8”). Empty: all paragraphs.

statementTable.label: Table from content
statementTable.says: Table rows from block content as two sides: column A on the left, column B on the right (the same positions form a pair) — for “match pairs” or questions about a column.

statementSubjects.label: What it is about
statementSubjects.says: The entries the statement's reference fields point to (e.g. “About”) — with the place (e.g. “Lk 1:35”).

media.label: Image or sound
media.says: A file from a field — as a question: show the image, play the recording.

follow.label: Through references
follow.says: Follows references step by step (e.g. author, then their birthplace) and gives the entries at the end of the path.

list.label: List
list.says: A fixed list typed in by the author — e.g. extra correct answers or your own distractors.

entity.label: This entry
entity.says: The entry the card is made for — with its label.

filter.label: Filter
filter.says: Splits entries by a field: those whose field has a value from “Compare with” (or typed in), and the others — e.g. words in this card's language and words in other languages. Without a field it compares the entries themselves.

unique.label: No repeats
unique.says: Each entry (or text) only once — e.g. the languages of all words of a translation, each one once.

entries.label: Entries of a kind
entries.says: Entries of the chosen kind — all of them, or those whose field has a value from “Where field has” (or typed in): words with the same spelling, translations with this word, words in a given language. Can skip this entry and take a few at random.

pattern.label: Text pattern
pattern.says: Builds a text from the inputs: “Who wrote {0}?”. Several values on one input are joined with a comma.

mask.label: Mask
mask.says: Hides part of a text: the end, the beginning or random words. Gives the text with a gap, the hidden part and the whole.

fragments.label: Quote fragments
fragments.says: Splits a quote into pieces (7–13 characters) and arranges them in a tree: first the pieces, then what they make together. Connect “For each value”.

pick.label: Pick one
pick.says: Takes one value from a list (random, first or last) and gives it and the rest separately.

distractors.label: Distractors
distractors.says: Wrong answers to choose from: the same field of other entries of this kind, only from the current set, the author's list, or the values closest to the correct one.

each.label: For each value
each.says: Makes a separate card for each value from the left — each translation, each fragment of a quote.

pairs.label: Pairs
pairs.says: A pair from each entry: the field values matching the left side and those matching the right (without a right side: all the others) — e.g. from each translation the English and the Polish word. An entry without one of the sides is dropped.

pairsFields.label: Pairs from two fields
pairsFields.says: A pair from each entry: the field on the left (e.g. a text fragment) and the field on the right (empty: the entry's thesis) — for “match pairs”, e.g. five fragments of one work and their five theses. An entry without one of the sides is dropped.

random.label: Random value
random.says: Draws a number from a range (with a step) or one item from a list (typed here or coming from the left) — one template gives a different question every time (a “random” card: its history does not start over with each draw). “How many” > 1: that many different ones (no repeats) — e.g. 4 entries to put in order.

math.label: Operation
math.says: Calculates: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, power, logarithm, rounding, remainder.

calc.label: Calculate
calc.says: Calculates expressions in the drawing language — e.g. p0 * p1, mod(p0, 7), round(p0 / 3, 2), sqrt(p0), fmt(p0, 2) — each on its own line or after “;”, each gives one value (e.g. distractors “p0 + 1; p0 - 1; p0 * 2” for “Answer: single choice”). p0, p1, … are the first number of an input, n0, n1, … — how many values came, l0, l1, … — all values of the input as a list (entries as entries: sum(l0, it.masa), map(l0, it.label)). A result that is a list gives several values; a result that is not a number (division by zero) is dropped; when an input an expression uses gave no number, or no expression gave anything — the step fails and no card is made from this entry.

generate.label: Generator
generate.says: Draws a task: numbers from ranges ("params": [{"name": "s", "random": [20, 500], "step": 10}]), items from lists ({"name": "f", "values": ["sin", "cos"]}), entries from the base ({"name": "kation", "entry": {"kind": "@chem/jon", "where": "it.ladunek > 0"}}, several different ones: "entries" with "count"), calculates values ("let": [{"name": "v", "value": "s / t"}]) and checks conditions ("require": ["isint(v)"] — draws again, at most 60 times); "texts": [{"name": "pytanie", "value": "What is {a} + {b}?"}] — texts with values. In expressions "this" is this card's entry (this.pole); "only": "this.ladunek > 0" — only such entries of the kind get a card (others without a warning). Each name has its own output. When the task cannot be drawn, no card is made from this entry — with the reason in the preview.

aggregate.label: Aggregate
aggregate.says: Combines many values into one: sum, how many there are, smallest, largest, average — e.g. the sum of protons of a compound's components (a number field read through a reference to many entries: the same component twice counts twice). “Count” counts every value, also non-numeric ones (0 when nothing came); the others only numbers — without any number they give nothing, and no card is made from this entry.

compare.label: Comparison
compare.says: True or false from comparing two numbers or dates: “born before …?”.

when.label: Condition
when.says: The card is made only when the condition holds — e.g. when the field is filled in.

python.label: Python
python.says: Calculates in Python, in the browser (Pyodide): the function run(*inputs) returns a value or a list of values.

prompt.label: Question
prompt.says: What the learner sees: texts, images, recordings — in the order of the connections from top to bottom.

answerText.label: Answer: text
answerText.says: The learner types a text. The first value is the model answer; the next ones and “other correct” count too.

answerGap.label: Answer: gap in a quote
answerGap.says: The learner fills the gap. Takes the text with a gap and the hidden part (from a mask), a fragment of a quote, or marked gaps (from “Gaps in the text”) — then every gap stands in its place and is checked on its own.

answerNumber.label: Answer: number
answerNumber.says: The learner types a number; tolerance absolute or in percent, a unit to type beside it; with a quantity (e.g. torque) the answer's unit counts: another unit of the same quantity is converted, a unit of another quantity is an error.

answerDate.label: Answer: date
answerDate.says: The learner types a date with the required precision (year, month, day); tolerance in these units.

answerOne.label: Answer: single choice
answerOne.says: The learner picks one answer from the correct one and the distractors, in random order.

answerMany.label: Answer: multiple choice
answerMany.says: The learner marks all correct ones among the correct ones and the distractors.

answerTruefalse.label: Answer: true or false
answerTruefalse.says: The learner says “true” or “false”; the value comes e.g. from a comparison.

answerOrder.label: Answer: order
answerOrder.says: The learner puts the items in order — the order in which they come in.

answerMatch.label: Answer: match pairs
answerMatch.says: The learner joins pairs: items on the left with items on the right (the same positions on the lists form a pair).

answerFlash.label: Answer: flashcard
answerFlash.says: The learner turns the card over and rates themselves: knew it, partly, didn't know.

answerCode.label: Answer: code (Python)
answerCode.says: The learner writes a function in Python; Pyodide checks it in the browser on random cases.

answerPoint.label: Answer: point
answerPoint.says: The learner points to a place on a map (from a “place” field) or a point on an image.

card.label: Card
card.says: Assembles a card: question, answer and (after answering) an explanation from the connected entries. For generator tasks: “Hints” (texts, from gentle to specific) and “Solution” (a text with the drawn values and intermediate results — after answering).

gaps.label: Gaps in the text
gaps.says: Gaps where the text marks them with [[word]] (also several). Gives one item with all gaps, one item per gap (for “For each value”), the hidden words and the whole text. When reading the entry, only the word shows.

error.filterNothing: The filter has nothing to compare with: connect “Compare with” or type a value.
error.entriesNothing: “Entries of a kind” with a field have nothing to compare with: connect “Where field has” or type a value.
error.pairsFields: Pairs need a field with the values (e.g. words) and a field to split them by (e.g. language).
error.pairsLeft: Pairs don't know what goes on the left: connect “Left: compare with” or type a value.
error.randomItems: “Random value”: {count} different items needed, there are {have}.
error.randomRange: “Random value”: the range has only {have} numbers, but {count} different ones are needed.
error.cannotCompute: This cannot be calculated (no number or division by zero).
error.calcEmpty: “Calculate” has no expression — type e.g. p0 + 1.
error.noExprNumber: No expression gave a number (e.g. division by zero).
error.generatorEmpty: The generator has nothing to draw — add "params", "let" or "texts".
error.noTask: The task could not be drawn.
error.compareNeeds: A comparison needs two numbers or dates.

stepSays.show: Shows an entry or a statement ("of"), or a file ("media"); "title" — the screen heading.
stepSays.question: Asks a question ("of": a question or a card key); exits "right" and "wrong".
stepSays.choice: Offers a choice: "options" [{"label", "condition"?}]; exit "o0", "o1", … for each option.
stepSays.condition: Checks a condition ("condition" — one logic); exits "yes" and "no". Whoever knows the entry goes on: {"type": "knowness", "of": "@wpis", "op": "ge", "than": 1} (the old step “Basics first”, "prerequisite", is read as such a condition: "known" → "yes", "explain" → "no").
stepSays.chapters: Chapters ("chapters": [{"title"}]); exit "c0", "c1", … — the start of a chapter; "done" when all are finished.
stepSays.chapterEnd: End of chapter — goes back to the chapter choice.
stepSays.subflow: Enters another flow ("flow"); after it exit "next".
stepSays.each: For each entry of a collection ("collection") or kind ("kind") — another flow ("flow") with {item}; then "next".
stepSays.expand: Explains the concept "of" in place when it is not known yet; then "next".
stepSays.line: A character ("character") says a sentence ("of": a statement — an entry with a “Block content” field); "mood" — the mood; "next".
stepSays.handoff: Hands over to another flow ("flow") — that one starts from the beginning.
stepSays.detour: Offers a detour into another story ("flow", "label" — “Want to know more: …”): “Enter” plays it and comes back through exit "done", “Continue without it” goes through exit "skip"; "optional": false — only “Enter”.
stepSays.review: A review of the story in one step: asks once more the questions of this story ("of": "story" — or @przebieg) that the learner doesn't know yet — each once per round; when they know at least "threshold" (e.g. 0.9) of them, exit "passed", otherwise "notyet". Saves the value "value" (by default <story name>.przeglad: 1 passed, 0 not); without "goals" the flow gets the goal “Review passed” ("goal" — its name) and “Repeat the review” goes back to this step.
stepSays.scene: A presentation scene ("page" — the page address, "scene" — the scene key, "title"); exit "next", with a question on the scene "right" and "wrong", buttons "b0", "b1", … ("buttons": [{"exit", "label", "target"}]).
stepSays.return: Returns from an inner flow to the place it entered from.
stepSays.explore: Checks with real questions which towers of a scope the learner already masters and moves on to what builds on them (adaptive or up to a target level).

segmentQuestions.one: The segment “{name}” asks {count} question — it is practice only and does not count for the hexagon; put required questions into the shared checkpoint.
segmentQuestions.other: The segment “{name}” asks {count} questions — they are practice only and do not count for the hexagon; put required questions into the shared checkpoint.

mountain.branchQuestion: The question “{name}” lies on only some paths — it does not count for completing the hexagon; move it to the shared part.
mountain.reviewBranch: This review lies on only some paths — put the review into the shared part after the paths meet.
mountain.reviewEmpty: This review has no required questions (none on every path) — it would pass at once.
mountain.noAssessment: The hexagon has no shared assessment: no question and no review lies on every path.
mountain.noAssessmentBranch: The branch “{route}” has no assessment: no question and no review lies on every path through it.
mountain.tooManyRoutes: More than {count} paths — only the first {count} were checked.
mountain.uncheckable: The question “{name}” names neither a topic (“about”) nor explaining slides (“explain”) — its coverage cannot be checked.
mountain.routeNoEnd: The path “{route}” never reaches an end.
mountain.notCovered: The path “{route}” does not prepare the question “{name}”: it shows neither its topic nor one of its explaining slides.

editor.intro: A flow says how to tell something: steps show knowledge, entries and questions; headings and choice captions are data of the flow, and all content comes from the knowledge base (and its sources).
editor.usesTemplate: This flow is a use of the template
editor.slotHint: In a template step a field can point to a slot: in the step's JSON {json}. A change of the template reaches every use.
editor.proposedDeps: {n} dependencies proposed — confirm them in Settings.
editor.showFailed: The presentation could not be loaded.
editor.storyboard: Storyboard of the presentation ({n} scenes) — the map is view-only; it is changed in the presentation (Transitions).
editor.narrators: Narrators — the first whose condition holds tells the story (e.g. value “przewodnik” = 1 → Piotr, no condition → Maria). Their portrait and name stand above the step, also above a presentation.
editor.slots: Slots to fill (this flow as a template):
editor.goals: Goals — a flow with goals is a task (quest):
editor.lines: Character lines that are spoken by themselves when the condition holds (values, knowledge, visited steps). Any entry can speak.
editor.pageHint: The course on the page is read by those who can read this knowledge base (see “Who sees” above).
editor.makePage: Create a page with this course
editor.pathOk: The path is fine: one start, one end, the end can be reached from every step.
editor.pathError: This flow has an error (no start or end, detours in a loop) — it won't be saved like this from an import and the learner will get stuck:
editor.pathWarn: The path has places where the learner will get stuck or that they will never see:
editor.pathForSays: The towers are the same for everyone. A path for self-study is not shown while teaching; a teaching path only while you teach (and to the class that follows you).

adaptive.title: After the answer (adaptive)
adaptive.hint: What each question does after the answer: help after a wrong answer (slides, an easier check, then continue or try again), partly right answers, branches for the mistake tags of the question. Help steps never count toward progress.
adaptive.tags: Branch on these mistake tags (one exit each in the graph):

sumRetry.one: try again up to {max}× after {slides} slide
sumRetry.other: try again up to {max}× after {slides} slides

modes.title: Lesson or self-study
modes.hint: One content, two orders: in self-study first explain, then ask; in a lesson first let the class predict, then explain. Mark what only one of them plays — a step the mode does not play is skipped, and a choice with only one fitting branch takes it by itself. A prediction is asked and branches, but it never counts.
modes.tryLessonSays: The same story in the order of a lesson: steps for self-study only are skipped, predictions do not count.

cogitaEditRevision.intro: A review picks cards (all, from a kind, a collection, a list or a view), can narrow them down — also by what you already know (e.g. details only once the general is known) — and asks in the chosen way, in the chosen order.

sourceAll.label: All cards
sourceAll.says: Every card of this knowledge base (and of the bases it uses).

sourceKind.label: Kind
sourceKind.says: Cards of the entries of one kind — also from a library this base uses (e.g. quotes); “From where” narrows it to one library or base.

sourceCollection.label: Collection
sourceCollection.says: Cards of the entries of a saved collection — a filter or a list.

sourceList.label: List
sourceList.says: Cards of chosen entries or questions.

sourceView.label: View
sourceView.says: Cards of the entries shown by a saved way of displaying (a view) — it decides what comes into play, the review picks from it. Its knowledge filters at the end are checked during the review, at each card.

filter.label: Filter
filter.says: Keeps the cards of chosen templates, directions, answer forms, states (not yet / learning / known) or only those that are due.

sample.label: Sample from each topic
sample.says: Keeps a few random cards from each topic ("perTopic", 2 by default) — a spot check; a different sample every day.

union.label: Together
union.says: Joins several sources into one stack, without repeats.

strategy.label: Way of asking
strategy.says: How to ask: a given number at random, the whole stack once, in levels or by what I already know — in what order (general first, as in the text, by date, at random, as they come, overdue first) and how to pick from the stack (strictly the next one or at random, weaker ones more often).

sourceFrom.says: {step} Gives the cards of these entries.

through.says: {step} Gives the cards of those entries.

learning.says: {step} Gives the cards of those entries; “Also keep the starting ones” adds them to the cards it started from (e.g. a review about orbitals starts with the atom).

filterRule.label: Entry filter
filterRule.says: {step} The cards of these entries stay.

filterWhen.says: {step} In a review it is checked as it goes, at each card: what waited before comes in once the condition starts to hold; a card already in the stack stays.

cogitaEditRevision.noTemplate: No cards are made from this kind yet — add a template for it in “Cards” (e.g. “Gaps in a quote”).
cogitaEditRevision.migrated: This review had a “Basics first” step — now those are ordinary steps: “Follow the learning order”, “Knowledge filter” and the order “general first”. It works the same; save it to keep it in the new form.
cogitaEditRevision.storage: Where the answers are saved (for this review)
cogitaEditRevision.storageHint: A module on a page (course, group) can point to its own area — then they go there. Without it: the area chosen here, then the one from the base Settings, and without them they stay with the learner. Progress is seen by whoever leads the chosen area; a learner who can't read it keeps the answers to themselves.
cogitaEditRevision.askDelete: Delete the review? The answers stay.
cogitaEditRevision.pageHint: Those who can read this knowledge base review on it (see “Who sees” above) — without an account their progress stays in their browser.
cogitaEditRevision.makePage: Create a page with this review
cogitaEditRevision.taskAdded: A daily task with a link to the review was added.

error.noStrategy: The review has no “Way of asking” step.
error.oneStrategy: A review can have only one “Way of asking”.

welcome.title: The knowledge map
welcome.text: Knowledge is not a list of chapters but a landscape: topics depend on each other, and to understand one you need others. This map shows those dependencies. So at any moment you can see what you already know, what you can start now and how far it is to your goal. The guide walks you through your own map: you click what it shows, then read what it is and why it works this way.

home.title: Start
home.do: Click the house — the pulsing spot on the map.
home.text: The house is the starting point. Stories leaving it assume nothing — you can begin with them without any knowledge. The house is also where you come back. From here you review everything you have seen at once (you choose how well known something may be and still be skipped), see the ways that bring something new, and open this guide again.

tower.title: Tower = topic
tower.text: A tower is one topic: a dozen or so questions that together check whether you understand it. The colour is the field. The height is how many cards stand between you and conquering the tower — including the towers it requires — so it honestly shows how much work is ahead. A pale tower is a topic nothing of which has come up yet. With every card you learn, it gains colour and shrinks. Once clicked, only the buttons that make sense right now stand above it.

path.title: Path = story
path.do: Click the highlighted path (or its marker).
path.text: A path is a story: slides and questions that explain the topic before it is checked. Towers and paths are separate on purpose. The tower says WHAT you need to know; the path says HOW you can learn it. Several stories can lead to one tower, and one story can introduce cards of several towers, so the same knowledge can be reached in different ways. A solid line means you can go. Dashed with a lock: the story assumes knowledge you do not have yet. The arrow shows the direction, and on a chosen path the dots are slides (●) and questions (◆).

started.title: On the way
started.text: This is a story half done: the path is coloured up to the last slide seen, and the tower has gained colour and shrunk by the cards that already came up. You can stop anywhere — the map remembers where you left off, and you come back from there.

level.title: Conquering
level.text: Having seen the cards is not the same as mastering the topic. That is why a tower is conquered in a run: each card once, in random order, without the story's explanations. Each of the {levels} levels asks more and lights another arc on top of the tower. You do not need the highest level to go on: the ways out of a tower open from the level the course author set, and higher levels only show how firmly the topic sits. The star (everything right the first time) is not a requirement either — it is a distinction that shows what else can be achieved.

conquered.title: Conquered
conquered.text: A conquered tower is flat: there is nothing left to learn in it, so it does not hide the topics further on. The flag marks the conquest, the star a run without a single mistake the first time. The dot in the middle says how fresh the knowledge is: green — fresh, yellow — review soon. Only a conquered tower opens the ways that build on it, because the next topics assume this one is mastered.
conquered.text0: When you know all its cards, the tower is conquered and flat: there is nothing left to learn in it, so it does not hide the topics further on. The dot in the middle says how fresh the knowledge is: green — fresh, yellow — review soon, orange — time to review (then "Review" stands above the tower). Only a conquered tower opens the ways that build on it.

due.title: Due for review
due.text: Memory fades over time — that is normal, not a failure. A review helps most just when knowledge starts to blur: then the dot turns orange and "Review" appears above the tower. Each good review lengthens the time to the next. Only conquered towers are reviewed, so reviews do not flood topics still being learned. One more thing: when you choose a longer way and there are cards along it that the system thinks may have faded, the way starts with a short review of them — before building something new on them, you check whether you still remember them.

onward.title: Ways on
onward.text: Above a conquered tower stand the ways that leave it and bring something new — new cards or a tower still missing. Ways already travelled or bringing nothing are left out, so the choice stays simple. Pointing at a way lights it on the map. When something is due, "Review" stands next to them, coloured by how much it is needed.

locked.title: A tower that waits
locked.do: Click the tall tower standing on discs.
locked.text: This tower requires other topics. The discs under it are the towers still missing — the bottom one comes first. Requirements are not there for their own sake: this tower's questions assume that knowledge, and without it they would be guesswork. "Explore" lays out the shortest way through the missing topics and guides you step by step. "Conquer directly" lets you try without that way — if you already know it from elsewhere, you do not have to prove it twice.

fork.title: Fork
fork.text: Here the story splits: the branches tell the same thing differently or lead to different topics. You choose one; you can come back to the others later — nothing is lost.

sign.title: Signpost
sign.text: A signpost is a question answered by several steps of the map at once, for example "Who was…?". It stands where that way begins. Clicking it guides you through all the stories and towers needed, in order, and at the end you can check whether the answer is clear now.

way.title: Guidance
way.do: Click the tall tower again, then “Explore” above it.
way.text: “Explore” (or a double click on a tower) chooses the tower as your goal and turns on guidance. Now you see the whole way to it: the bright paths are what is still ahead, the arcs in the air show which topics it needs, and the camera shows the whole map so nothing of the way is hidden. At the bottom the same way appears as a bar of steps; each step says what will happen and gives a choice — go, skip, or restore a skipped one. Skipping is allowed on purpose: sometimes you want to get to a particular place straight away and fill in the rest later. A double click on empty ground ends the guidance; the progress stays.

views.title: Views
views.text: At the top, views narrow the map: what I know, to discover (what you can start now), to review, gaps. "Check what you know" asks the key questions of every topic and shows the gaps — a good start if you already know something. Open this guide again by clicking the house.

steps.title: Steps of a way
steps.do: Click one of the steps in the bar at the bottom.
steps.text: Every way is laid out in steps: a story (reading the slides), learning (cards no story brings), a review, and conquering a tower. "Go to step" stands above the current step. A clicked step shows on the map where it lies and gives a choice: "Go here" starts it at once, even before earlier ones, and "Skip" greys it out — it stays in its place and can be restored with the same click ("Restore"). Try it in the bar: skip a step and restore it. "≡" shows the whole way with its forks, and "End" stops the way without losing progress.

placement.title: Checking what you already know
placement.do: Click the tower with the dashed ring.
placement.text: Not everyone starts from zero. The check ("Check how much you already know", at the start of a course or a story) asks real questions from the towers that can be passed right now — on the map they are in colour, the rest grey. A tower passed this way has a dashed ring: it counts as passable, opens everything built on it, and its cards that were not asked come later in reviews. There are two ways. Adaptive: a few questions per tower — a few right answers in a row pass it, a few mistakes end it; quick and many towers at once, but an estimate. Up to a level: each tower is asked like a real conquest of the chosen level — slower, but the tower is truly conquered and nothing needs redoing.

arcs.title: Arcs in the air
arcs.text: The grey arcs above the map are not ways but dependencies: they show where the knowledge comes from that this tower needs, or that is needed to enter a path. An arc runs from the tower you must know to the tower (or the gate on a path) that requires it; the arrow at its end shows the direction. A dashed arc means this knowledge is still missing; a solid one that the requirement is met. The arcs are in the air on purpose: you walk on the ground (the paths), and in the air you only see what you must know beforehand. They appear when you click a tower or a fork, or choose a goal.

full.title: Conquer fully: {name}
full.says: This tower is already conquered and opens the ways on — higher levels and the star are not needed for that. They only show how firmly the topic sits. Each run asks every card once, in random order.
full.star: Masterly — every card right the first time (all levels at once)
full.how: A run raises you by every level whose rule it meets. One mistake does not undo your learning: every answer counts for your knowledge.

desc.title: Community as JSON ("{format}", version 1)

section.usage: How the app uses this data

desc.intro:
One document describes a whole community: a tree of units (e.g. diocese → districts → circles, school → classes, retreat session → groups), positions with their rights, blueprints for similar units, people with their positions and the settings of the five steps of the guided setup. It is the same document that “Communities” → “New community” creates and that the community's JSON tab shows.
What the import does:
- First it shows a plan (a list of changes): new and moved units, roles, access, people's links, parts of areas. It saves only after “Import”.
- Unit = an area in Recreatio (under the area of the unit above). Position in a unit = a role of that area (“Animator couple · Circle 3”). Person = one personal link that holds all of their roles (a member in the circle, a leader in the district). The unit's tools (chats, calendar, pages, sign-ups) are created as an area document (“recreatio/area”) and go through the same import.
- Everything is named by keys. The community remembers what was created under which key: the same document imported again CHANGES the same things (names, place in the tree, staffing, settings) instead of duplicating them. A document from another community creates everything here anew.
- Nothing is deleted silently: a unit with "remove": true is no longer managed (the area and its content stay), a person with "remove": true loses their link. A unit or person missing from the document stays unchanged.
- Changing a person's roles (a new position, a position given up) gives them a NEW link and the old one stops working. Content stays with the position — the successor takes it over.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

top.name: name of the community (omitted — name of the top unit)
top.positions: positions — each described once, used in many units (below: Positions)
top.fields: person fields from step 4 (below: Person fields)
top.unit: the top unit, with its units in "units" (below: Units)
top.persons: people with their places (below: People); people can also be entered as a group in a unit's "people"

positions.key: short name (lowercase letters, digits, - and _, up to 32 characters), e.g. "para-animatorska"
positions.name: name, e.g. "Para animatorska"
