describe.mathExample: ### A textbook with formulas (theorems, a proof, matrices, a figure, a table, code)
describe.useHead: ## How the app uses this data
describe.mathAsk: Transcribe formulas, matrices and mathematical symbols in LaTeX ($…$ in a sentence, $$…$$ on their own, with the number \tag{…} as printed), reading them from the page image; definitions, theorems, lemmas, proofs and examples — as "statement" blocks with a label; references to them and to formulas — {{ref …}}; figures — a "figure" block with a caption and a description. In JSON double every LaTeX backslash ("\\frac").
describe.use:
- On the work's page the “Source text” box shows which texts there are (parts, words, in which library) and opens the reader (“Read”).
- The reader (#/workspace/library/<biblioteka>/<dzieło>/tekst/<miejsce>): list of parts, places in the margin, page breaks, footnotes; “Go to” a place, search in the whole text, “Beside” — another edition or translation of this work, aligned by places in the structure.
- A selected passage can be added as a quote (with the work and the place) or copied with its place.
- Every place already quoted somewhere (a footnote, a quote, a reference in a knowledge-base entry, a field with a place) gets “show in text” if it is in this text: the passage opens at the place, also on a page. Nothing is saved — the link is made while reading.
- A place in the structure (verse, number, article) also leads to the text of another edition of this work ("editionOf"); a page — only to the text of this edition.
- “In Knowledge” on the work and in the reader: entries of knowledge bases the reader may open that point to this work or its places.
- The text is sealed with the area key of the library in which it was saved — this can be a different (e.g. private) library than the one with the work. Whoever does not read it does not see the text: not in the reader, not in search, not on a page.
- “AI access” (an area link, MCP server), if it covers the library with the text, gives it to the assistant to read: list_texts, read_text (by place), search_text.
- The text is not in the library JSON ("recreatio/library"); the export in the “Source text” box gives it out — in this format.
- The reader typesets formulas ($…$, $$…$$) as in print (KaTeX), including matrices, systems and formula numbers; a formula that cannot be typeset stays visible as LaTeX code. The import checks every formula and says which do not pass.
- Theorems, definitions, proofs, examples stand in labelled boxes; a proof ends with ∎. “Go to” also accepts labels (“Twierdzenie 2.3”, “(2.4)”, “Rys. 1.2”), and a reference {{ref …}} in the text leads to its target — also in another part.
- Search in the text also finds formulas: by words and symbols (“α”, “∫”, “sin”) and by LaTeX (“\frac”, “x^2”). A selected passage with a formula goes into a quote and the clipboard as LaTeX ($…$).
- “AI access” gives formulas as LaTeX in $…$ and $$…$$; read_text also accepts a label (“Twierdzenie 2.3”, “(2.4)”).
describe.rules:
## Rules
- Do not invent text or numbers: what is not visible in the source is not in the JSON. Mark what is uncertain with {{? …}} or "uncertain": true.
- Page numbers: as printed, as in the book (also roman: "xii"); the page number of the PDF file in "pdf", if it differs.
- Footnotes and endnotes: a "note" block (after the paragraph or at the end of the part) and {{note …}} at the place of the reference mark.
- One part — at most about 2 million characters.
- Every page has its break — also an empty one or one taken up entirely by a figure ({{page …}} or a "page" block); the import checks that none is missing.

## The whole text
- Divide the text by its own division: books of the Bible (key: the book's abbreviation, e.g. "J"), chapters of a book ("rozdz-1", "rozdz-2"), questions of the Summa ("I-q2"), chapters of a document; a short article or document can be one part.
- Keys short and stable; "order" — the order in the work (1, 2, 3…). Introduction, preface, table of contents, bibliography, index — separate parts only if they are in the source.
- Every chapter is a separate part, with its number and title as headings ("heading") — check at the end that the number of parts matches the table of contents and that no chapter was left in the middle of the previous one.
- Every part starts with a "page" block with the page on which it starts — also when the previous part ends on the same page (a chapter starting mid-page). This shared page does not duplicate text.
- Put endnotes (at the end of the book or chapter) in the part they refer to.
- When the text does not fit into one answer: transcribe the following parts in following documents (with the same "work", "scheme" and "edition"), starting exactly where you stopped. Never break off a part in the middle — finish it, or start the next document with it (the same part a second time replaces the previous one).
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.
describe.head:
# Source text as JSON ("{format}", version {version})

The text of a work consists of PARTS (e.g. a book of the Bible, a chapter of a book, a whole short document or article). A JSON document holds one part ("portion" + "blocks") or several at once ("portions": [ … ] — also the whole text). A part with the same "portion.key" replaces the previous one, others stay — so a long work can be sent in several documents one after another, and a repeated document duplicates nothing.

{
  "format": "{format}",
  "version": {version},
  "work": "@work-key",              — key (or identifier) of the work's entry in the Library; the text belongs to THIS edition/translation
  "scheme": "{scheme}",                — the work's place layout (below); must match the work
  "edition": {                       — optional
    "pdfPageOffset": 12,            — printed page = PDF page − 12 (when constant)
    "language": "pl",
    "psalms": "hebrew" | "greek",   — Holy Scripture only: psalm numbering (most modern translations: hebrew; Vulgate: greek)
    "macros": { "\\R": "\\mathbb{R}" }  — the author's own macros in formulas (below: Formulas)
  },
  "portion": { "key": "rozdz-1", "label": "Chapter 1", "order": 1 },
  "blocks": [ … ]                    — blocks in the order of the original
}

Or several parts (e.g. the whole text) in one document — instead of "portion" and "blocks":
  "portions": [
    { "portion": { "key": "wstep", "label": "Introduction", "order": 1 }, "blocks": [ … ] },
    { "portion": { "key": "rozdz-1", "label": "Chapter 1", "order": 2 }, "blocks": [ … ] }
  ]

## Blocks
  {"type": "heading", "level": 1-4, "text": "…", "loc": "…"}    heading
  {"type": "paragraph", "text": "…", "loc": "…"}               paragraph (also a verse, a point of a document, a theorem)
  {"type": "quote", "text": "…", "loc": "…"}                   block quote in the source
  {"type": "list", "items": ["…", "…"], "ordered": true, "loc": "…"}
  {"type": "table", "columns": ["…"], "rows": [["…", "…"]], "loc": "…"}
  {"type": "note", "id": "1", "text": "…"}                     footnote (the footnote text); in the text the reference {{note 1}}
  {"type": "page", "page": "46", "pdf": 52}                   page 46 (printed) starts here = page 52 of the PDF file;
                                                              the page as printed — also with series marks: "12*", "3'", "(7)", "A12", "xii"
  {"type": "statement", "kind": "theorem", "label": "Theorem 2.3", "title": "…", "text": "…"}
                                                              definition, theorem, lemma, proof, example… (below); longer content: "blocks": [ … ] instead of "text"
  {"type": "figure", "label": "Fig. 2.1", "text": "caption", "alt": "what the figure shows"}
                                                              figure, chart, diagram — the caption from the book, and in "alt" a short description of what is visible
  {"type": "code", "lang": "python", "text": "…"}             code or pseudocode — character for character, with indentation and line breaks
  {"type": "table", "label": "Table 2.1", "text": "caption", "columns": […], "rows": […]}   a table with a label and caption (both optional)
  "uncertain": true                                           on any block: uncertain reading

## Marks in the text
  {{page 46}}  or  {{page 46 pdf 52}}      page break in the middle of a paragraph (exactly where it falls)
  {{note 3}}                               reference to footnote "3"
  {{? word}}                               uncertain reading of this word;  {{?}} — illegible
  {{gap}}                                  omitted / missing passage
  {{ref theorem 2.3}}  {{ref (2.4)}}       reference to a theorem, formula, figure, table of the same work — written as in the text
  $x^2$   $$\\int_0^1 f(x)\\,dx$$         a formula in a sentence and a displayed formula (on its own) — LaTeX (below)
Everything else is plain text. Keep the exact wording, order, paragraphs and punctuation of the original. Do not correct, do not summarise, do not translate.

## Formulas (LaTeX)
- Write every formula, symbol and mathematical notation (also a single variable letter, an index, a unit in an expression) in LaTeX: in a sentence between $ … $, a displayed formula (on its own line) between $$ … $$ — in the paragraph exactly where it stands in the source; a paragraph can have several displayed formulas and continue after them.
- There is no space after the opening $ and before the closing $. A literal dollar sign in the text: \\$.
- In JSON every LaTeX backslash is doubled: "$\\frac{a}{b}$", "$$\\sum_{k=1}^{n} k = \\frac{n(n+1)}{2}$$". A single backslash breaks the formula (in JSON "\f", "\t", "\n" are control characters).
- The formula number as printed: $$ … \\tag{2.4}$$ (in a multi-line layout \\tag on its line). A formula without a number — without \\tag. Do not number on your own.
- Step-by-step derivations and systems: \\begin{aligned} … \\end{aligned} (or align*, gather*), cases: cases; matrices: pmatrix, bmatrix, vmatrix, array (with rules: {cc|c}, \\hline); commutative diagrams: \\begin{CD}; chemistry: \\ce{H2O}, units: \\pu{9,81 m/s^2}.
- Do not turn formulas into plain text or Unicode characters (x², α, √) — always LaTeX ($x^2$, $\\alpha$, $\\sqrt{x}$). Do not simplify, transform or correct — transcribe what is printed, in the same form.
- Give the author's own macros (e.g. \\R, \\norm{x}) once in "edition.macros" ({"\\norm": "\\left\\lVert #1 \\right\\rVert"}) and use them in formulas; an ordinary \\newcommand in a formula works too.
- Formulas are read by KaTeX. It does not have: \\label and \\ref (references use {{ref …}}), tabular and \\multicolumn (a table is a "table" block), tikz, \\includegraphics (a figure is a "figure" block), \\sideset.
- A page break never in the middle of a formula — {{page …}} before the formula or after it.
- Read formulas from the page image, not from the PDF text layer: the text layer usually loses indices, fractions and symbols.

## Theorems, definitions, proofs ("statement")
  {"type": "statement", "kind": "definition", "label": "Definition 2.1", "text": "A sequence $(a_n)$ converges if …"}
  {"type": "statement", "kind": "theorem", "label": "Theorem 2.2", "title": "squeeze theorem", "text": "…"}
  {"type": "statement", "kind": "proof", "label": "Proof", "blocks": [ {"type": "paragraph", "text": "…"}, … ]}
- "kind": {kinds}, other (other — then "label" counts).
- "label" — exactly as printed, with its number ("Lemma 4.1", "Exercise 7*"); "title" — the name in brackets after the label, if there is one (without the brackets).
- Content as one paragraph: "text". Longer (several paragraphs, displayed formulas, lists, cases, page breaks): "blocks" — ordinary blocks, also nested statements (e.g. a lemma inside a proof).
- A proof, solution, answer — a separate "statement" right after what it is about. Do not transcribe the end-of-proof sign (□, ∎, Q.E.D.): the app adds it itself.

## References and labels
- In the text write a reference to a theorem, formula, figure or table of the same work as {{ref …}} — in the words of the source: "by {{ref theorem 2.3}}", "from {{ref (2.4)}}", "cf. {{ref Fig. 1.2}}". The reader turns them into links.
- Labels (label, \\tag) must be unique in the whole work — as in the book.

## "loc" — the place in the structure of the work
Give "loc" on every block that has its own number in the structure of the work (verse, point, article, theorem, paragraph, chapter). Blocks without their own number (e.g. a paragraph in the middle of a chapter) have no "loc" — they belong to the place given earlier. Pages do NOT go into "loc": pages are "page" blocks and {{page …}} marks, because they belong to this one edition.

prompt.intro: Turn the attached source text (PDF, scan or file) into a JSON document for import into the Recreatio Library.
prompt.faithful: Transcribe the text faithfully — word for word, in the order of the original, divided into paragraphs, with headings, lists, tables and footnotes, with page breaks exactly where they fall (also in the middle of a paragraph). Do not correct, do not summarise, do not add anything that is not in the source. Mark whatever is illegible or uncertain.

withWork.workInvalid: The work from "work" cannot be saved — check its fields.
withWork.workUnknown: There is no work “{work}” in the library — describe it in "work" as an object (the work's fields) and it will be created together with the text.
withWork.workMissing: "work" — the work: an object with the fields of a new work (e.g. {"key": "kowalski2020", "data": {"workType": "article", "title": "…"}}) or the key of an existing one ("@kowalski2020").
withWork.noText: The document has no text ("portions" or "portion" and "blocks") — only the work will be saved.

withWork.use:
## How the app uses this data
- The work and the entries from "entries" go into the library in which the document is imported; the text — into the library chosen at import. After saving, the work's page opens.
- The work, the authors and the periodical are ordinary Library entries (whoever sees its area sees them): they have their pages and are cited by key — [@kowalski2020, s. 47] in a Scriptorium text, in a knowledge-base entry or in a page's “Text” module becomes a footnote.
withWork.prompt:
Turn the attached source (a PDF, scan or file with a book or article) into ONE JSON document for import into the Recreatio Library: the description of the work (bibliographic data from the title page or the article's header), its authors and — if it is an article or chapter — the periodical or book it is in, and the whole text divided into parts.

Transcribe the text faithfully — word for word, in the order of the original, divided into paragraphs, with headings, lists, tables and footnotes, with page breaks exactly where they fall (also in the middle of a paragraph). Do not correct, do not summarise, do not add anything that is not in the source. Mark whatever is illegible or uncertain. If the whole does not fit into one answer, give "work", "entries" and the first parts in the first one, and in the following ones — "work": "@work-key" and the next parts.
withWork.head:
# A work with its full text as JSON ("{format}", version {version})

One document creates in the Library the entry of a work (a book, article, chapter, document…), the entries it points to (authors, periodical, edited volume) and its full text. A work with a key that is already in the library is completed (the given fields), not duplicated; the same goes for an author or periodical with an existing key.

{
  "format": "{format}",
  "version": {version},
  "work": { "key": "surname2020", "data": { … fields of the work … } },   — or the "@key" of a work that already exists
  "entries": [ { "kind": "person", "key": "…", "data": { … } }, { "kind": "work", "key": "…", "data": { "workType": "periodical", … } } ],
  "scheme": "pages",          — how places in this work are referred to (below)
  "edition": { … },           — optional: PDF page offset, language
  "portions": [ { "portion": { "key", "label", "order" }, "blocks": [ … ] }, … ]
}

- References in the work's fields ("authors", "editors", "translators", "container") are keys with "@": to entries from "entries" or to ones that are already in the library.
- Take the description of the work from the title page, the imprint or the article's header; do not enter what is not there.

## Fields of the work and the person

box.title: Source text
box.none: No full text — the work works without it too. When a text appears, quotes and footnotes with a place lead to it by themselves.
box.inLibraryApart: in the library “{name}” (apart from the work)
box.apart: The text will be in the library “{target}”, the work is in “{work}”. Whoever reads only “{work}” sees the work and the quotes, but not the text.
box.publicNote: The library “{name}” is public — anyone will read the text, even without an account.
box.publicBody: The library “{name}” is in a public area — anyone will read the full text, even without an account. Share only texts that may be published (copyright).
box.otherWork: This text is for another work (“{key}”) — import it in Sources as “Work with text” or open the right work.
box.workSkipped: The work's data from the document was skipped — this work already exists; change its fields on this page.
box.removeBody: Deletes the full text from the library “{name}” ({parts}). The work, quotes and footnotes stay — they just stop leading to the text.
box.lead: One part of the text, several or the whole text (“portions”) — e.g. transcribed by AI from a PDF. A part with the same key replaces the previous one, others stay; the same part a second time changes nothing. Beside it are the format description and a prompt to copy.
box.withWorkModal: Work with full text — JSON import
box.workElsewhere: The work is in another library — add the text on its page.
box.withWorkLead: One document: the description of the work (a book, article, chapter, document), its authors and — when needed — the periodical or book it is in, and its text in parts. The work goes to “{name}”; one with an existing key is completed, not duplicated. Beside it are the format description and the prompt for AI.
box.aiSays: Off: the text stays in the Library but is left out of the snapshot for AI assistants. Every text is stored for AI on its own — a large one never hides the others — so switch it off only for huge reference works you do not want read.

reader.noWork: This work does not exist (or you have no access to it).
reader.noText: This work has no text you can read yet. You add it on the work's page (“Source text”).
reader.noParts: This text has no parts yet.
reader.partFailed: This part cannot be opened right now.
reader.texMissing: Formulas shown as LaTeX code — the module that typesets them did not load (no network?).
reader.otherMissing: The other edition does not have this part (or has no places of this structure in it — pages do not carry over).

blocks.refMissing: This place is not in the saved text
blocks.pageStartPdf: Start of page {page} (page {pdf} of the PDF file)
blocks.gap: Missing in the source or omitted

jump.failed: This passage cannot be opened right now.
jump.notInPart: This place cannot be seen in this part of the text.

pages.label: Pages of the edition
pages.says: Only the pages of this particular edition (books, articles without their own numbering). When a book numbers its parts separately (introduction “xii” or “12*”, appendix “3'”, inserts “(7)”, “A12”), the page carries the marks of its series as printed — any marks — and the work says in the field “Page series” in what order the series stand in the book.

bible.label: Holy Scripture
bible.says: Book, chapter, verse — shared by all translations (psalm numbering: Hebrew, Greek in brackets).

numbered.label: Numbers (documents)
numbered.says: Numbered points of Church documents, the catechism, codes; a paragraph within a number after “§”.

aquinas.label: Thomas Aquinas
aquinas.says: Part, question, article; objection (arg.), sed contra, answer (co.), reply to an objection (ad).

decimal.label: Decimal numbering
decimal.says: Propositions numbered decimally, as in the Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus: each digit after the point is one level lower.

sections.label: Sections of the work
sections.says: Sections (remarks) numbered through the whole work, with parts, as in the Philosophical Investigations.

outline.label: Division of the work
outline.says: Volume, part, book, chapter, section, paragraph — as many levels as the work has.

time.label: Recording time
time.says: Minutes and seconds of a recording — like the pages of an edition they belong to this one performance, not to the piece.

read.label: Reads
read.says: sees what is in the area

levelSays.read: reads (sees what is in the area)

error.incomplete: This link is incomplete — copy it again in full.
error.pickRole: Choose the role the link gives.
error.cannotAdmit: In one of the chosen areas you can't let anyone in.
error.notYourRole: A link can only give a role you have.
error.notLeader: Only someone who leads a role can give leading it.
error.mismatch: This link doesn't match the invitation — copy it again in full.

aim.notOurs: The target must be an address on recreatio.pl.
aim.badChars: The target address contains characters that are not allowed.
aim.pageBound: access-only page for the chosen area
aim.label: Where the link opens
aim.placeholder: e.g. parish/grzegorzki/oaza — or paste a page address
aim.empty: Empty: the link opens the join page. With a target: it opens that page and gives access on it right away — also without an account, in this browser.
aim.needsAccount: this part of the workspace needs an account: whoever opens the link signs in and adds it to their account. Without an account, pages and the calendar work.
aim.noAccount: with access right away, also without an account.

progress.areas: Opening the areas for the link…
progress.role: Connecting the link with the role…

new.noPerson: The account doesn't lead any person yet.
new.pickRole: Choose the role the link gives — or create a new one.

new.nameLink: Name the link — e.g. „Parish council" or the person's name.
new.title: New access link
new.label: For whom / what for

new.lead: can also invite others to this role

new.once: Single-use — once one person adds it to their account, the link stops working (before that it works in every browser where it was opened)

item.cannotShow: This link can no longer be shown — create a new one.
item.revokeAsk: The link will stop working — also in the browsers where it was opened. What about those who added it to their account?
item.revokeAskCount: The link will stop working — also in the browsers where it was opened. What about those who added it to their account ({count})?
item.aimHint: The link stays the same — one sent earlier still works and leads where it led. Addresses shown from now on have the new target.

held.title: Links opened in this browser
held.lede: They work here without signing in and add up. On an account they work on every device and allow writing.

share.title: Invitation to recreatio.pl
share.warn: Whoever has this link has access. Send it only to those it is meant for.

shareDialog.needPassword: Enter your password first — the keys are not open in this tab.
shareDialog.title: Share: {title}
shareDialog.public: This is public — this address is enough. Whoever opens it sees it without signing in.
shareDialog.ready: Link ready. Whoever opens it has access right away.
shareDialog.lede: The link gives a role — and the role gives access to its areas. It opens right here.
shareDialog.ledeAim: The link gives a role — and the role gives access to its areas. It opens right here: {aim}.
shareDialog.name: Link name (seen by whoever opens it)

bar.label: Access link
bar.unjoinedLabel: Access link that is not on the account
bar.unjoined: There is an access link in this browser — {access}. Your account doesn't have it, and in the workspace only what the account has works.
bar.unjoinedNamed: There is an access link „{label}” in this browser — {access}. Your account doesn't have it, and in the workspace only what the account has works.
bar.dead: This access link no longer works — it was turned off, has expired, or was single-use and already used.
bar.owned: You also have this access on your account.
bar.signedIn: It works in this browser, together with other links opened here.
bar.guest: It works in this browser, without signing in.
bar.guestWrites: It works in this browser, without signing in — in the calendar, adding entries too.
bar.signedInHint: You are signed in — in the workspace and when adding entries, what the account has works. On the account, access also works on every device.

state.revoked: This link was turned off by the person who created it.
state.used: This link was single-use and someone has already joined through it.

join.noInvite: This link is missing the invitation.
join.title: Invitation
join.joinedLede: You now have access: {access}. It works on every device where you sign in.
join.unlockWhy: To join, enter your password — the keys open only on your side.
join.noPerson: The account doesn't lead any person yet — create one in Roles, then come back to this link.

json.title: Liturgy — the whole collection ({format}, version {version})
json.intro: A liturgical collection of the Library: works, editions, texts, passages, templates of the hours and Mass, observances, assignments, rules and calendar profiles — nine kinds of entity that refer to each other by "id". Each text has ONE full wording in its edition and language ("text"); everything that belongs to its performance — verse numbers, pauses (* and †), lines and stanzas, V./R., headings, rubrics, repetitions — is structure next to it, never inside it. The same wording gives two views: continuous (as read, with punctuation and paragraphs) and liturgical (with that structure).
json.rules:
- An "id" that exists (in this collection or built in) changes that entity in place: only the fields named change, a field set to null is cleared, the rest stays. A changed built-in entity becomes this collection's own.
- An unknown "id" creates an entity: then "entity_type" and every field marked required are needed.
- {"id": "…", "remove": true} deletes the entity; a built-in one changed here returns to its default. Nothing else is deleted — entities the document leaves out stay.
- References are ids of this collection or built-in ones; the order in the document does not matter. An id merged into another text still works.
- A division is written as pieces of the wording ("layout": [{"text": "…"}, …]): the pieces must follow the wording in order, with only spaces between them. A piece that does not match stops the import and the preview says where. A division always belongs to one version of its wording: change the "text" and send the division again.
- Identical wordings of the same edition and kind become one text; the other ids remain as "aliases", their sources and divisions are kept. Texts that only begin alike, or where one is the beginning of the other, are listed in the preview as candidates to compare — never merged; a shorter one is marked "possibly_truncated".
- Before saving, everything is checked together: a reference to nothing, a text in another language than its edition, a broken verse range, a stale division, an unsupported execution structure … stop the import, and the preview names each one. Then it is saved in one go — all or nothing — and recorded in the import history.
- What a text still lacks is listed in "missing"; such a text is "incomplete" until it is checked.

type.canonical_work: A work as such — a psalm, canticle, hymn or reading — independent of any translation; its numbers in each numbering are written out.
type.text_edition: An edition or translation: language, publisher, licence and what the licence permits. Every text belongs to one.
type.text_resource: One actual text in one edition — psalm, canticle, antiphon, hymn, reading, responsory, dialogue, versicle, intercessions, response, prayer, doxology, blessing — as ONE wording ("text") with its structure ("layout", see „Wording and structure").
type.passage_definition: A part of a psalm or canticle by verse ranges (internal verse numbers of its text); it copies nothing. Parts with the same "division" form a named division ("two parts", "Ps 119 — 22 parts") in their "order"; reading the whole text or one division needs no second copy.
type.liturgical_template: The parts (slots) of an hour or of Mass, in order, with where their texts are looked for. Built-in templates exist for every hour and Mass (see „Built in”).
type.calendar_observance: A celebration in a calendar: its date rule, rank, colour and precedence.
type.liturgical_assignment: Which text fills which slot, and when (conditions).
type.liturgical_rule: A rule of a calendar: another date, a transfer, another text in a slot, or a slot left out.
type.calendar_profile: A combination of calendars (e.g. Roman + Poland + a diocese) with time zone and language — chosen when reading.

builtins.title: Built in
builtins.intro: The app brings a basic calendar and a template for every hour and Mass. Refer to them by "id"; to change one, name its "id" with the fields to change; {"id", "remove": true} returns it to the default. They are not a complete Roman or Polish calendar.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- Storage: each entity is one entry of this collection, sealed in the browser with the key of its area; every import adds an entry to the import history. The area decides who reads: its members — everyone only when the area is public and its rule for collections is confirmed.
- In the collection: Resources (each text in the continuous and the liturgical view, with its divisions, references, everything that uses it and its revisions) and Calendar and reading — the liturgical day and the hours and Mass composed when they are read, in either view; print/PDF, the composition as JSON and an HTML file to read offline.
- Elsewhere: a knowledge base (Cogita) that adds the collection under Settings → Sources sees its entities as read-only material — the wording, passages with their verses; other Library collections can refer to them; an AI link that includes the collection carries the exact entities in this format (MCP get_liturgy_library) and the wordings (search_entries).
- The import does not delete what the document leaves out, never fetches texts from outside and writes nothing into Cogita or another collection; in a public area it is refused while an edition lacks "share" in "permitted_usage".

wording.title: Wording and structure
wording.intro: A text has one "text". Its structure is written as units — pieces of that wording in order, with what each one is in the performance. Stored as positions; the export writes the pieces again.
wording.unit: "layout" (and "units" of an attested division) — a list of units:
wording.performance: "performance" — steps in order (each with exactly one of "say", "resource", "rubric"):
wording.notes: "notes" — shown in the liturgical view only:
wording.types: "resource_type": {types}. Psalms, canticles and the doxology are shown in verse lines, hymns in stanzas, everything else as prose with its marks.
wording.checks: Checked: the pieces follow the wording; units neither overlap nor leave text out; ids are unique; steps, notes, incipit and variants point to existing units; a division was made for the current version; ranges of a passage exist in its text.

unit.text: The piece of the wording (exactly as in "text", spaces may differ)
unit.id: Its name, for steps, notes, incipit and variants (e.g. "R", "conclusion")
unit.verse: Internal verse number (1, 2, …) — stable, used by passage ranges
unit.label: The number as printed by the edition ("2a", "116"); a stanza number in a hymn
unit.end: How the unit ends: {values} — mediant shows *, flex shows †; verse, stanza and part break the line
unit.cross: true: a sign of the cross ✠ before it

step.say: Units of this text (ids) — a unit already said is a repetition: the wording is not written again
step.resource: Another text (its id), e.g. the common response or the doxology
step.units: With "resource": only these of its units
step.rubric: A rubric line of the edition

note.at: "start", "end" or the id of the unit it stands before
note.source: Where it comes from (e.g. the source of a sentence)

variant.replaces: The id of the unit it replaces (with the following units of the same kind); absent: the whole text
variant.when: Conditions under which it is used (as in "conditions")

hours.title: How an hour is composed
hours.text:
- A slot takes the text of the best assignment (layers in "source_order", then priority); a passage reads only its verses.
- The antiphon of an assignment ("antiphon_ref", division "antiphon_layout") comes back as "antiphon_repeat" says: {repeats}. When repeated, its mediant is shown as "/".
- Glory be follows a psalm or canticle (and each part of a divided psalm) where the slot or the assignment asks for it ("doxology"), unless the text says "doxology": "none" or the assignment says false. The psalm's own view never shows it.
- A prayer takes the variant whose "when" matches (e.g. the short ending); its conclusion and the Amen stay distinct units; a blessing or dismissal is its own text in its own slot.
- Responsories, dialogues and intercessions follow their "performance"; the common response is said where the steps say.
- The opening dialogue, versicles, the blessing and the dismissal are single reusable texts referred to by assignments.

migration.title: Earlier formats
migration.text:
- Version 1 ("recreatio/liturgy", 1) and the first format ("recreatio.liturgy" 1.0/1.1 with "operations") are read and written as version 2.
- Blocks ("structured_content") become one wording: stanzas and paragraphs as paragraphs, responses as lines; rubric and heading blocks become "notes". " * " and " † " inside a text become unit ends and leave the wording.
- "metadata.performance_markers" ({"at", "mark"} per block) become units: * mediant, † flex, / mediant (shown on repetition), ✢ ✣ a sign of the cross; other attested positions ("recitation_mark_variants") become "layouts".
- Speakers P/K/V become V. (cantor), W/R become R. (all); repeated lines become steps of "performance" instead of a second copy.
- Psalms without verse boundaries get verses inferred from the pauses; hymns get lines from capital letters when their number matches the print — both marked in "missing" until checked.
- Intercessions "A, — B." become introduction, petition and second part; the refrain (refrain_resource_id) becomes "response_ref". Prayers get body, conclusion and Amen; "introduction_formula" becomes "intro_formula". Readings get "origin", "reference", the title as a heading and heading lines that continue into the text as incipit.
- Kinds: psalm_fragment → psalm, gospel_canticle → canticle, intercession_refrain → response, blessing_and_conclusion → blessing, office_rubric → dialog (with speakers) or rubric.
- "metadata" stays unchanged (sources, usages, attested differences). A stored record of version 1 is read as version 2; an import that names it writes it as version 2.

desc.intro:
Masses, devotions and confession of one calendar (group schedule) with Mass intentions — day by day. The import first shows the list of changes: which Mass on which day gets which intention; it saves only after “Import”.
What the import does (Masses and devotions → “More” → “Import and export (JSON)”):
- An entry with "id" from the export is changed in place — only what the document gives; what it does not give stays. An entry without "id" in "masses" is created new (single or series).
- An intention belongs to a Mass on a SPECIFIC DAY. That Mass is looked up by "mass" (id from the export or "@name" from "masses") and "date" — or by "date" and "time" among the calendar's Masses.
- An intention without "id" is added to its Mass, unless this Mass already has the same text — then nothing is duplicated.
- A Mass that already has ANOTHER intention in the calendar than in the document is a conflict: by default new intentions are not added to it (the warning says which); in the preview you can choose “add beside”.
- Nothing is deleted. "status": "cancelled" withdraws an intention, "until" ends a series, "cancelled": true cancels a Mass on one day.
- The donor and the offering are encrypted in this browser with the key of the calendar's group, the place — with the key of the group that sees the Masses (as for every date). The intention text and the Mass name are public: they are read at Mass and hang on the notice board.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments: at most {masses} entries in "masses", {occurrences} items in "occurrences", {intentions} intentions at one Mass, a period of up to {days} days.

desc.bookText:
The most common work: the parish office copies a month from the book of intentions (e.g. AI from photos of the pages).
1. Easiest to start from the export of that month: every Mass stands in "occurrences" with "date", "time" and "mass" — with the intentions it already has, or with "free": true. Write the intentions into these items (instead of "free": true — "intentions"); do not add or remove items.
2. Without the export: one item for every Mass in the book, with "date" and "time" (the Mass must already be in the calendar or in this document's "masses").
3. “wolna” (free) → "free": true. Several intentions at one Mass → several items in "intentions", in the order of the book. Collective Mass → "collective": true and all its intentions.
4. Copy the text exactly as in the book (“Za śp. …”, “O zdrowie i Boże błogosławieństwo dla …”), without ordinal numbers. An illegible word: the best reading and “[?]” at the end of the text — the office will correct it.
5. Write the donor and the offering only when they are in the book ("giver", "offering"); do not guess.
6. The same text at the same Mass is not added a second time. Another text at a Mass that already has an intention is a conflict — the preview shows it before anything is saved.
Example — the 7:00 and 18:00 Masses are already in the calendar:
{sample}
desc.usage:
- Masses, devotions and confession are calendar dates: they appear in the Calendar (with the number of intentions at a Mass, e.g. “2 int.”) and in “Now” for everyone who has the key of an area that sees the calendar. People in "celebrants" and "celebrant" find them under “Assigned to me”.
- The parish office works on them in “Masses and devotions”: Intentions, Plan and changes (two weeks), Print.
- The public plan — the page module “Masses and devotions” (also as a widget on another website) — shows without an account the time, name, cancellation, public scheme fields and intention texts (collective ones folded, with their number). It takes Masses only from calendars seen by a public area (“everyone reads”).
- The print for the notice board (Print → “Print intentions (A4)”) is a week of Masses from the same public plan.
- Never in the plan or on the print: donor, offering, place or celebrant; withdrawn intentions ("cancelled") neither — they stay in the office.
- “Celebrated” is not set by itself: the office marks it after Mass (“Mark as celebrated”) or the import does ("status": "celebrated").
- When a Mass gets another time, its intentions stay on the same day; if a day with accepted intentions would disappear, the change is not saved.
- The app does not remind of Masses, and the import notifies nobody — its intentions have their "status" at once and do not wait in “Entries to accept”.

prompt.answer: Return ONE JSON object (without comments): this export with the intentions from the book written into the right items. Do not add or remove items; describe a Mass from the book that is not in the export separately, outside the JSON.
prompt.exact: Copy the text exactly; an illegible word — the best reading and “[?]” at the end of the text. Write the donor and the offering only when they are in the book.

hero.showsAll: Badge, headline with subtitle, description and buttons.
hero.badgeKicker: Overline — capitals in the accent colour
hero.headline: Headline
hero.actionHrefHint: #slide-name (e.g. #zapisy), a page address or a full address https://…

facts.label: Key facts
facts.use: A row of the most important facts — date, place, distance, cost.

key.label: Label, e.g. "Date"
key.detail: Detail below the value (or null; not shown in the strip)

facts.showsStrip: Facts in one row, without details.
facts.showsAll: Facts with details and a note below.

image.label: Image
image.use: One photo, logo or graphic — with a caption and a link; on request a short silent film in place of the photo.
image.urlHint: choose above or an address: https://… or /logo.svg
image.caption: Caption

key.fit: "contain" — the whole image fits in the space (usual), "cover" — fills the space and crops the edges
key.at: With "cover": where the centre of the crop is, e.g. "center", "top", "57% 50%". In a presentation the place on the scene can have its own "crop" (also in frames and on the phone) — then that counts
key.video: A short silent looping film instead of the photo (MP4 or WebM): a page file "page-image:<id>" or "https://…". "url" is its poster — it stands until the film has loaded, with „reduced motion” and when saving data; the film plays only while it is visible

image.missing: Choose an image or enter its address.
image.showsFilm: A film in place of the photo.
image.fitCover: Crop — fills the space, trims the edges
image.video: Film instead of the photo — a few seconds without sound, looping; the photo is its poster (optional)

gallery.label: Gallery
gallery.use: A carousel of photos; a click opens the whole gallery full screen, with zoom.

key.url: Address https://… or a page file "page-image:<id>" (uploaded in the editor)
key.caption: Caption (or null)
key.alt: Description of the photo for screen readers
key.shuffle: true — random order on every visit, false — as in the list

gallery.showsStrip: A button that expands the gallery.
gallery.showsCarousel: Carousel — {photos}; a click opens the whole gallery.
gallery.privacy: Photos are shrunk before uploading (long side up to 2048 px), and EXIF data — including where they were taken — is not sent.
gallery.caption: Caption
gallery.altHint: For people using a screen reader.

layers.label: Layered image
layers.use: A sign or illustration made of several stacked layers, each with its own motion — e.g. a logo whose letters assemble while bubbles float.
layers.intro: The first layer sets the size; the next ones lie exactly on top of it (images of the same size with a transparent background).

key.layers: Layers from the first (it sets the size) — a list; each: { "url", "z", "shadow", "motion" }
key.url: Image address (e.g. "/cogita/logo/Cogita00.png") or "page-image:<id>" — an image of the page
key.z: Stacking order: higher — in front (−10…10; omitted — 0)
key.shadow: Layer shadow: "offset-x offset-y blur colour", e.g. "0 26px 60px rgba(8, 20, 38, 0.6)" (omitted — no shadow)
key.motion: Motion of the layer (described below: Motion) — e.g. { "name": "float", "x": 4, "y": 6 } or { "name": "assemble", "delay": 90 }; a list of up to three
key.motionX: Motion setting (here: sideways swing, px) — each motion has its own, described below
key.motionDuration: Duration of one run in ms (omitted — as in the dictionary)
key.motionDelay: Delay in ms — grows with each following letter (0, 90, 180 …)

showsAll.one: {count} layer, each with its own motion.
showsAll.other: {count} layers, each with its own motion.

shape.label: Shape
shape.use: A circle, rectangle or line in colour — a background, an accent, an element of a presentation.
shape.fillHint: #14180f, a pair „light|dark” or accent, ink, ground, muted

map.label: Map
map.use: GPS points and a route track on an OpenStreetMap map; the track can be loaded from a GPX file.
map.noTracks: No tracks — the map will join the points below with a line.
map.name: Name
map.gpxHint: You can pick several files at once — each becomes its own track. Long tracks are simplified so the page does not load tens of thousands of points.

key.points: Points on the map — a list
key.label: Point name
key.isStop: true — a stop (shown in the legend), false — an ordinary point
key.tracks: Routes — a list (easiest: load a GPX file in the editor)
key.trackColor: Line colour, e.g. "#d9480f" (or null — from the palette)
key.trackPoints: Route points: a list of pairs [latitude, longitude]; at most 2000 points in total
key.showTrack: true — draw the routes, false — points only

map.showsStrip: A button that expands the map.
map.showsSide: A map with the legend of points beside it.
map.showsBelow: A map with the legend below — {points}, {tracks}.
map.zoomHint: 2–18. The map fits its view to all points and tracks anyway.

scene.world: World: gravity, air resistance, body thickness, ground, pace
scene.worldGravity: Gravitational acceleration in m/s² (Earth 9.81, Moon 1.62, 0 — weightlessness)
scene.worldAir: Air resistance: 1 — normal, 0 — vacuum, more — denser air
scene.worldDepth: Body thickness in metres (with density and area it gives the mass); usually 0.1
scene.worldGround: false — no ground (a table seen from above, space)
scene.worldSpeed: Pace of time at the start (1 — as in reality)
scene.vars: Values drawn at every opening (and with „New draw”) — used in expressions "=…" and in texts as "{nazwa}" (nazwa = the value’s name)
scene.varsPick: Instead of a number: a list of texts to draw from (e.g. liquids)
scene.bodies: Bodies: balls, blocks, polygons — of a material or with their own density
scene.bodiesId: Body name (letters, digits, - _) — in joints, goal and graph
scene.bodiesX: Position of the centre (poly: of the origin of its points) in metres
scene.bodiesPoints: Polygon points [[x, y], …] relative to x, y
scene.bodiesMaterial: Material: wood, oak, cork, steel, aluminium, lead, gold, rubber, ice, stone, plastic, glass, paper, foam, ball, egg
scene.bodiesDensity: Own density in kg/m³ (instead of the material’s)
scene.bodiesTrace: true — draws a trace of its motion
scene.joints: Joints: pivot, rod, rope, spring, pulley
scene.jointsB: Second body (id) — omitted: attached to the world
scene.jointsAt: Point in the world (without "b") or on body "b"; for a pulley — the first wheel
scene.jointsOn: Point on body "a" relative to its centre (default: the centre)
scene.jointsLength: Length (default: how far apart the ends are)
scene.fluidsLayers: Layers of liquid from the bottom (a lighter one rises to the top by itself)
scene.fluidsLayersLiquid: Liquid: water, saltwater, sea, oil, alcohol, glycerin, honey, mercury, milk
scene.fluidsLayersHeight: Height of the layer in an empty tank (m)
scene.fluidsHoles: Holes in the walls (a jet following Torricelli’s law)
scene.fluidsHolesAt: Height above the bottom (with "bottom": distance from the left wall)
scene.show: What is visible: arrows, traces, grid, pressure, values
scene.showPressure: true — pressure in the liquid as a darker shade in the depth
scene.showValues: false — no labels of masses and forces
scene.graph: A graph over time for one body
scene.allowPalette: What can be added: ball, box, plank, wedge, ramp, wall, pendulum, spring, pulley, seesaw, basin
scene.allowTools: Tools: pin, rope, rod, link (spring), ruler, probe (pressure), delete
scene.allowEdit: false — no changing of materials and body settings
scene.goal: Goal: a body in an area for a while — then a message appears
scene.goalArea: Area [x0, y0, x1, y1] (numbers or expressions)
scene.goalFor: How many seconds it has to stay there
scene.goalSay: What to say when it succeeds
scene.steps: Steps of the experiment — „Show” performs them one by one
scene.stepsSay: What to do in this step
scene.stepsWait: How many seconds the step lasts with „Show”
scene.view: What is visible at the start: [x0, y0, x1, y1]

physics.label: Physics lab
physics.use: A 2D physics lab: bodies of real materials, slopes, pendulums, springs, pulleys, collisions, liquids (pressure, buoyancy, communicating vessels, jets) — a sandbox or a ready school experiment; full screen.
physics.title: Physics lab
physics.showsStrip: {title} — a card with a button: the lab opens full screen.
physics.showsSandbox: Sandbox „{title}” — the scene, controls beside or below it, a full-screen button.
physics.showsExperiment: Experiment „{title}” — the scene, controls beside or below it, a full-screen button.

key.title: Title of the experiment (above the scene)
key.text: Text for students — what they should do and observe (paragraphs)
key.mode: "experiment" — exactly this scene (with „Show”), "sandbox" — everything is allowed, ready experiments to load, saving and JSON export
key.scene: Scene: world, bodies, joints, tanks of liquid, pipes, what is visible, what is allowed, goal and steps — the engine is built in, the scene says what stands in it
key.question: in a story with a knowledge base: reaching the scene’s goal ("goal") counts as a correct answer to this question of the base — id or @name (empty: its own goal card)
key.about: in a story with a knowledge base: for which entries of the base the reached goal counts — id or @name, each on its own line

scene.seed: Random seed — the same number, the same run (e.g. the pits in the walls where bubbles are born)
scene.box: Inside of the box in metres and the thickness of the 2D layer
scene.boxDepth: Layer thickness (m), usually 0.01 — masses and energies follow from it
scene.ambient: Surroundings: pressure, temperature, humidity, gravity, air composition
scene.ambientP: Pressure in kPa (101.325 — sea level; 70 — a high mountain; 200 — a pressure cooker)
scene.ambientRh: Relative humidity of the air, from 0 to 1
scene.ambientG: Gravitational acceleration in m/s², from 2.45 (1/4 g) to 19.6 (2 g)
scene.ambientAir: Composition of dry air — mass fractions, e.g. { "N2": 0.7676, "O2": 0.2324 }
scene.ambientAirN2: Mass fraction of nitrogen in the air
scene.ambientAirO2: Mass fraction of oxygen in the air
scene.sides: Each side of the box: "wall" or "open" (open to the room)
scene.quality: Cell size: "high" (2 mm, normal), "very-high" (1 mm, a strong computer), "medium" (3 mm, a weaker computer); a device on which someone chose another one keeps its own
scene.extremes: Violent phenomena (explosive boiling of superheated water, very fast water motion): "ask" (default — the lab stops and asks how to continue computing), "compute" (compute exactly, as in reality — water may fly out of the vessel), "normalize" (soften: bubbles at most 4 mm, no superheating, water stays in the vessel)
scene.ops: Build steps in order — the starting setup, not the run
scene.opsOp: "fill" (water or air), "erase" (remove — air comes back), "solid" (a fixed structure of cells), named objects with settings: "body" (a block, ice cube, stone — an exact rectangle: falls, floats, sinks, tips over; ice melts and freezes on with whole faces), "beaker", "hotplate"; "grains" (a handful of salt crystals: falls, sinks, piles up, dissolves); "move" (move object "id" together with its contents, or everything solid in an area), "remove" (take away object "id"); "pin" (older scenes: pin or unpin a body at point x, y — today "pinned" on the object)
scene.opsId: Object name ("body", "beaker", "hotplate"), e.g. "cube" — under it the lab selects the object and changes its settings in the object itself; in "move" and "remove" steps the name of the object they concern; without a name the object gets "body-1", "beaker-1" …
scene.opsDx: Horizontal shift (m) — in a "move" step; objects move exactly, painted structures by whole cells
scene.opsRegion: Area: rect, circle, poly or line with width; a body ("body") is always a rectangle — a circle becomes a square of the same area, a polygon the rectangle enclosing it, a line with width a rotated rectangle
scene.opsComposition: Composition (mass fractions): { "H2O": 1 } for water, { "oil-rapeseed": 1 } for rapeseed oil, { "H2O": 0.9, "NaCl": 0.1 } for 10 % brine (saturated is about 26 %), { "N2": 0.7676, "O2": 0.2324 } for air
scene.opsMaterial: Material: "glass" (borosilicate glass), "steel" (stainless steel), "ceramic" (boiling stones), "wood" (pine), "ice" (as a body it melts and freezes on, as a structure it does not), "stone" (granite); in a "grains" step: "NaCl" (table salt)
scene.opsD: Crystal diameter in a "grains" step (m): 0.0005 (default, table salt), from 0.00005 to 0.005 — finer ones sink more slowly and dissolve faster
scene.opsPinned: Object pinned (stays in place, does not fall) or free (false: falls under gravity); a block is free unless true; a beaker and a plate are pinned unless false — in the lab: the object’s „Pinned” field
scene.opsAngle: Rotation of the body in degrees anticlockwise (beaker and plate around the centre of the bottom, a body around the centre of its area)
scene.opsX: Centre of the apparatus (m); in a "pin" step the point of the body
scene.opsY: Bottom of the apparatus (m) — 0 is the bottom of the box; in a "pin" step the point of the body
scene.opsWall: Wall thickness of the beaker (m) — exact, the beaker is a body made of rectangles
scene.opsLid: true — a beaker with a tight lid (a closed gas region)
scene.opsPower: Plate power in W per layer thickness (with a thermostat: the maximum power)

lab2d.label: 2D lab
lab2d.use: 2D lab (engine v2): a box full of air in which you place beakers and hotplates and paint water — heat, convection, evaporation, boiling with bubbles, condensation and fog follow from the laws of physics and the materials database. Tools: probing a point, a bubble view with forces, overlays (temperature, pressure, velocity with arrows, humidity, vapour, phase map), a particle view, graphs, two levels. Full screen.
lab2d.title: 2D lab
lab2d.showsStrip: {title} — a card with a button: the lab opens full screen.
lab2d.showsAll: „{title}” — a box with water and apparatus, tools beside or below it, a full-screen button.

choice.startButton: Waits for a button (run live or bake)
choice.startBake: Bakes a recording right away (a ready one plays at once)

key.title: Title of the lab (above the box)
key.text: Text for students — what they should do and observe (paragraphs)
key.mode: "sandbox" — all tools, "experiment" — reserved for experiments with steps
key.scene: Starting setup: box, surroundings, sides, seed and build steps (water, air, solid, beaker, hotplate, remove) — the engine is built in, the scene says what stands where at the start
key.start: What the lab does after opening: "button" (default) — nothing is computed, it waits for the „Run live” or „Bake” button; "bake" — bakes a recording right away (the scene is computed once, as fast as possible, and saved in this browser; a ready recording plays at once)
key.seconds: Recording length in seconds of simulation time: 10, 30 (default), 60, 120 or 300
key.scenarios: Further scenarios to choose in the lab (the first is the scene from the key scene): a list { title, text, scene }
key.scenarioTitle: Scenario title (in the choice list and above the box)
key.scenarioText: Text for students for this scenario — a list of paragraphs
key.scenarioScene: Scene of the scenario — like the one in the key scene

scene.seed: Random seed — the same number, the same run
scene.box: Inside of the box in metres and the thickness of the 2D layer
scene.boxDepth: Layer thickness (m), usually 0.01 — masses and energies follow from it
scene.ambient: Surroundings: pressure, temperature, gravity, air composition
scene.ambientP: Pressure in kPa (101.325 — sea level; lower in the mountains)
scene.ambientAirN2: Mass fraction of nitrogen in the air
scene.ambientAirO2: Mass fraction of oxygen in the air
scene.sides: Each side of the box: "wall" or "open" (open to the room)
scene.quality: Resolution: "very-high" (2 mm particles, normal), "high" (2.5 mm), "medium" (3 mm, for a weaker computer); a device on which someone chose a lower one keeps its own
scene.ops: Build steps in order — the starting setup, not the run
scene.opsRegion: Area: rect, circle, poly or line with width
scene.opsCompositionH2O: Mass fraction of water (H₂O) — other substances from the database likewise: N2, O2
scene.opsY: Bottom of the apparatus (m) — 0 is the bottom of the box
scene.opsWall: Wall thickness of the beaker (m) — at least two particles
scene.opsPower: Plate power in W per layer thickness

particles.label: Particle lab
particles.use: A 2D particle lab: a box full of air into which you paint water and place apparatus (beaker, hotplate) — the engine computes everything from local rules and the substance database. Stage M1a: mechanics (liquid and gas, walls, surface tension, buoyancy); heat and boiling in later stages. Full screen; the „All cores” button opens it in a new tab that computes on all cores.
particles.title: Particle lab
particles.showsStrip: {title} — a card with a button: the lab opens full screen.
particles.showsAll: „{title}” — a box of particles, tools beside or below it, a full-screen button.

key.title: Title of the lab (above the box)
key.text: Text for students — what they should do and observe (paragraphs)
key.mode: "sandbox" — all tools, "experiment" — reserved for experiments with steps
key.scene: Starting setup: box, surroundings, sides, seed and build steps (fill, remove, solid, beaker, hotplate) — the engine is built in, the scene says what stands where at the start

shape.x: Position in drawing units (in a frame — world units): rect, image — top left corner (in a frame: bottom left); circle, ellipse — centre; text — anchor point; line, arrow — start; group, use — offset; frame — top left corner of the frame. A number or an expression "=…"
shape.r: circle — radius; rect — corner rounding (always in drawing units)
shape.d: path — an SVG path ("M10 10 L50 40 Z" …); in a frame it is not converted — use "poly" there
shape.text: text — the text; with values in {…}: "Angle: {fmt(kat, 0)}°"
shape.use: use — name of a part from "symbols"
shape.fill: Fill: a colour ("#rrggbb", "rgba(…)", "accent", "muted/35" …), "none", a glow "radial(rgba(120, 190, 255, 0.25), transparent 70%)" or an expression "=trafione ? 'ok' : 'accent'"
shape.glow: Glow/shadow: "x y blur colour", e.g. "0 0 10px rgba(160, 220, 255, 0.75)"
shape.origin: What it rotates and grows around: "center" (usual), "25% 75%" (part of the element), "170 225" (drawing units)
shape.rotate: group, use — rotation in degrees (in a frame: anticlockwise)
shape.children: group, frame — elements inside (the same keys)
shape.shift: group, use — the elements inside start moving this many ms later (e.g. successive cards 120 ms apart)
shape.motion: Motion of the element (described under: Motion) — an object or a list of up to three
shape.show: When the element is visible: an expression, e.g. "step >= 1" (second step of the scene) or "sily == 1"
shape.drag: Dragging: { "x": "variable" } — variable = finger position; { "set": { "kat": "deg(atan2(py, px))" } } — from the finger position (px, py); "label" — name of the handle
shape.dragX: Variable that receives the horizontal finger position
shape.dragY: Variable that receives the vertical finger position
shape.dragSet: Variables computed from the finger position: { "name": "expression with px, py" }
shape.dragLabel: Name of the handle for screen readers
shape.tapGo: In a presentation: where to — "next", "back", a scene key, "link:<id>"
shape.tapLabel: Name of the button for screen readers
shape.repeat: How many copies of the element (in each "i" = 0, 1, … and "n" = how many) — e.g. particles, a scale
shape.label: Name of the handle or button (dragging, clicking)
shape.head: arrow — size of the arrowhead (drawing units)
shape.points: poly — points [[x, y], …]: numbers or expressions "=…"
shape.fn: plot — y as an expression of "u" (e.g. "A*sin(2*pi*u/l)")
shape.fx: plot — x of the path from "u"; trace — what to follow horizontally (e.g. "x")
shape.fy: plot — y of the path from "u"; trace — what to follow vertically (e.g. "y")
shape.var: plot — name of the curve parameter (usually "u"; e.g. "i" for the zigzag of a spring)
shape.from: plot — from which parameter value (a number or "=…")
shape.to: plot — up to which parameter value (a number or "=…")
shape.samples: plot — from how many points (up to 600)
shape.keep: trace — how many of the latest points remain
shape.every: trace — a new point every this many seconds of simulation
shape.view: frame — which part of the world is visible: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (numbers or "=…"; y grows upwards)
shape.clip: frame — true: whatever leaves the frame disappears
shape.camera: frame — true: you can zoom (+, −, Ctrl+wheel, two fingers) and pan the view; "view" is then the „Fit” view
shape.typeMore: "group" gathers "children", "use" inserts a part from "symbols", "frame" is a frame with a world (y upwards), "world" — this is where the things of "world" stand (in a frame)

motion.delay: Delay (ms; in a loop it may be negative)
motion.from: From (a number, a point [x, y] or a colour)
motion.to: To (a number, a point [x, y] or a colour)
motion.path: move — the path: a list of points [x, y]
motion.length: draw outside a drawing — length of the stroke
motion.by: "scene", "enter" or "leave" — in a presentation the motion follows scrolling (the progress of the scene, its arrival or departure) instead of the clock

frame.draw: How much of the line is drawn (0–1)
frame.color: Colour of the fill or text
frame.reveal: How much is visible from the left (0–1)

vars.name: Name (letters, digits, _; does not start with a digit) — used in expressions
vars.step: Step of the slider and dragging
vars.label: Label at the slider
vars.random: At every opening (in Cogita: at every attempt) a random value from [from, to]

sim.stateRate: Rate of change — derivative over time (expression; e.g. "vy" for y, "-g" for vy)
sim.events: Events: when a condition BECOMES true
sim.eventsSetVy: e.g. the new velocity after a bounce — the key is the name of a quantity or variable
sim.speed: Pace relative to the clock (1 — as in reality)
sim.auto: true — starts by itself when the drawing is visible
sim.loop: true — starts again after the end
sim.sleep: true — when nothing moves any more, computing goes to sleep (saves battery) and wakes up at every change

controls.var: The variable it sets (slider, number, toggle, choice)
controls.label: Label (default: the variable’s label)
controls.go: button — in a presentation: "next", "back", a scene key, "link:<id>"
controls.show: When the element is visible — an expression (e.g. "solved": the „Next” button only after solving)

rules.when: Condition — the rule fires when it BECOMES true
rules.go: In a presentation: where next — "next", "back", a scene key, "link:<id>"
rules.goal: true — this is the goal of the task (in Cogita: a correct answer)
rules.for: How many seconds the condition must hold without a break before the rule fires (e.g. 1 — „steadily”)

predict.start: true (usual) — a task: the drawing starts paused, and every change after checking pauses it again; false — it runs at once, and the „Predict” button pauses it on request
predict.say: What is visible below the drawing while it is paused (e.g. „Set it as you think — then check”)
predict.check: Label of the button that lets it go (usually „Check”)
predict.again: Label of the button after checking that pauses it again (usually „Adjust”)
predict.hold: Label of the button that pauses on request (with "start": false; usually „Predict”)

task.require: Conditions of every drawn task (expressions) — e.g. "onstep(s, 0.5)" (result on the slider grid), "abs(s - r0) >= 1" (far enough from the start), "a != b"; the conditions alone decide on comparable difficulty
task.solve: The solution as expressions of the drawn values: "w2.pos = 3 + s; kat = 45" — it must be settable by hand; in Cogita the solution of the question, unless the question gives its own
task.new: Label of the „New task” button (false — no button); in Cogita every attempt draws anew anyway
task.tries: How many times at most to draw (usually 200); when nothing fits — the task from the values "value"

world.kinds: Kinds of things (up to 12): what each has, what follows from it, how it moves, how it looks and what may be done with it
world.kindsName: Name of the kind (like a variable name) — also a set in summaries: count(belka, !ok)
world.kindsLabel: Name for people („Beam”) — in the panel and on buttons
world.kindsProps: Properties (up to 24): numbers with limits — set in the panel, dragged, saved in the answer
world.kindsPropsName: Property name — in expressions of the thing „pos”, of the parent „parent.pos”, of the thing with a given id „w2.pos”
world.kindsPropsMin: Minimum — a number or an expression computed in the thing
world.kindsPropsMax: Maximum — a number or an expression, e.g. "=parent.length" (at most to the end of the beam it hangs on)
world.kindsPropsApart: Smallest distance from siblings in this property (two weights do not hang at one spot)
world.kindsPropsNew: Where a newly added thing stands — an expression, e.g. "parent.pivot + 1" (a free spot is found automatically)
world.kindsPropsWhen: When the property applies to this thing — an expression, e.g. "!isroot" (only when it hangs) or "isroot"
world.kindsPropsQuiet: true — do not show it among the data of the selected thing (e.g. the length of a string: it only changes the picture)
world.kindsLet: Values computed in every thing — the order follows from what they read (children first, then the parent, or the other way round)
world.kindsLetValue: Expression: own names, parent.x, root.x, sum(children, total*arm), count(…), names of the drawing (g, tol) and built-ins (isroot, depth, index, selected, nchildren)
world.kindsState: Simulation quantities of every thing — computed with the same Runge-Kutta as "sim" (then "dt", "speed", "auto", "sleep" are enough for "sim")
world.kindsStateRate: Rate of change — derivative over time (expression in the thing)
world.kindsEvents: Events of the thing: when a condition BECOMES true (e.g. a swing limiter)
world.kindsEventsWhen: Condition in the thing, e.g. "angle > tilt"
world.kindsEventsSet: New values of properties or quantities: { "angle": "tilt", "omega": 0 }
world.kindsEventsSay: Text below the drawing ({…} — computed in the thing)
world.kindsShapes: How the thing looks: elements as in "elements", computed in the thing ("=x" is ITS x); in a frame — world coordinates
world.kindsDrag: What dragging the thing sets: { "property": "expression with px, py" } — px, py is the finger in the world; the grab ring stands at its "x", "y"
world.kindsDragPos: E.g. a place: "px" (along the ground) or the projection of the finger onto the parent’s beam
world.kindsCan: What may be done with a thing of this kind
world.kindsCanEdit: Properties to set in the panel of the selected thing (slider, number, ±)
world.kindsCanAdd: Which kinds may be hung onto it
world.kindsCanRemove: true — it can be removed (together with what hangs on it)
world.kindsCanCopy: true — it can be duplicated (together with what hangs on it)
world.kindsReadouts: Readouts in the panel of the selected thing
world.kindsReadoutsShow: When the readout is visible — an expression, e.g. "!held" (not while the person is predicting)
world.kindsChildren: How many things at most may hang on it
world.kindsBrief: What the thing is called in the panel — a text with {…}, e.g. "{m} kg" („Weight 2 kg”); omitted — kind and id
world.kindsMark: true (usual) — a thing that may be changed has a dashed ring (when there are also given things); false — the kind shows it itself (colour, arrows: "can", "can.pos")
world.thingsId: Name of the thing (letters, digits, _ -) — in expressions „s1.pos”, in answers and in the Cogita solution („s1.pos = 4”)

world.thingsLock: true — nothing may be changed or removed; a list — these properties may not be changed (a puzzle)
world.thingsPos: A property of the thing (any property of its kind, here "pos"): a number, { "random": [from, to] } (in Cogita drawn at every attempt) or an expression "=…" of the drawing’s values (random tasks: "=3 + s")
world.allow: What is allowed in this world at all — narrower than the kinds (a puzzle), never wider
world.allowEdit: true — properties may be set in the panel
world.allowRoots: Which kinds may be placed at the very top (e.g. a new stand)
world.keep: What must always hold — a change after which it no longer holds is undone
world.keepWhen: An expression, e.g. "edits <= 2" (at most two moves; edits — how many changes since „Start over”) or "nthings <= 6"
world.save: true — a workshop: „Save”, „Load” (in this browser) and the layout as JSON
world.hint: Hint below the drawing when nothing is selected ({…} — computed)
world.list: true — every property that may be changed as its own slider in the panel („You set”, without selecting a thing); false — select a thing first; omitted — rows, when nothing may be added or removed and there are at most 6 of them

Full description — with the page JSON import and in the AI prompt. Now: {sum}.

key.alt: Description of the drawing for screen readers (empty — the drawing is decorative only)
key.question: in a story with a knowledge base: the drawing’s goal (a rule with "goal": true) counts as a correct answer to this question of the base — id or @name (empty: its own goal card)
key.about: in a story with a knowledge base: for which entries of the base the reached goal of the drawing counts — id or @name, each on its own line
key.size: Size of the drawing in its own units: [width, height] — the drawing grows and shrinks as a whole with the module
key.max: At most this width in rem (a number); omitted — the full width of the module
key.panel: Where the controls go: "below" (below the drawing, usual) or "side" (beside it, when the drawing is wide; on a phone always below)
key.let: Values computed from others, in every frame, in this order: [{ "name", "value": "expression" }]
key.controls: Controls below the drawing: sliders, switches, choices, buttons, readouts
key.rules: Rules: when a condition becomes true — a text, the goal of the task, a setting, start/pause, onwards in a presentation
key.predict: Predict first, then see: the drawing stands still (simulation paused, rules silent, "held" = 1 in expressions — e.g. a colour that would give away the result waits) until the person clicks „Check”; "tries" — how many times they have checked. true or { "start", "say", "check", "again", "hold" }
key.task: A different task every time, equally hard: draws values from "random" (variables, properties of things, also as expressions of them) until the conditions hold, the task is not solved at the start, and the solution can be set. { "require", "solve", "new", "tries" }
key.world: A world of things to build (scales of beams and weights, gears): kinds, things at the start and what is allowed — every change goes through the rules of the world, with „Undo”; an element { "type": "world" } in a frame shows where they stand
key.symbols: Reusable parts: [{ "name": "fiszka", "shapes": [elements] }] — an element { "type": "use", "use": "fiszka" } inserts them
key.elements: Elements of the drawing, from back to front — each with position, look, motion ("motion") and — for moving — expressions, "drag", "tap", "show", "repeat"

landscape.label: Knowledge landscape
landscape.use: The knowledge landscape of a base (Cogita): “You” in the middle, around it fields of what you can learn now, further out mountains — the higher, the more is missing; what you know becomes land. Here the learner chooses how often questions come back — more often, standard, less often or “Once and done” (right once and finished) — unless the leader has set it for everyone in the base settings. Without a view — the whole base; with a view — only its entries; with several views the learner chooses above the map which landscape to look at. Clicking the house in the middle shows statistics and rewards, a double click — all at once. Visible to whoever can read the base.

path.label: Path
path.use: A learning path as a map (like a course path): from the bottom — from the basics — upwards, with forks and places where paths meet (“2 of 3 paths”); each step is a hexagon: known (sunken, ✓), now (highlighted), ready to learn (raised, glowing), locked (pale, padlock), due for review (marker). From the base’s learning order (“Must know first”) — for a story (its entries; “now” is the place in the story), one unit (its parts), a view or the whole base. Click a step: “Learn” with what must be known before. Next to a story it stands alone — in the “Course / story” module it is already built in.
path.exEntry: <id or @name of a unit or empty>
path.entryHint: id or @name of the entry — its parts; empty: nothing
path.showsStrip: One line: how many steps are done and what is next — a “See” button.
path.showsTall: The whole map with step names; click a step: state and “Learn”.
path.showsBlock: A small map (collapsible) — follows where the learner is; click a step: state and “Learn”.

pathView.noStory: This story is not in the knowledge base.

viewView.noCards: These entries produce no cards to learn.

viewPart.use: A saved view of a knowledge base (Learning → base → Entries → “Save as view”): chosen entries — also sermons and commentaries from the libraries the base uses — as a table, a tree with groups, a matrix (e.g. 20 mysteries × 12 periods; a cell opens its entries), a learning map, a progress map (tiles coloured by how well the visitor knows each entry — a click shows the text, questions and “Practise this”) or a landscape (in front of the visitor a ring of what they can learn now, further out mountains — the higher, the more steps are missing, behind them a valley of what they know; click: read, learn, revise, set a goal); a clicked entry opens below (commentary, the whole sermon), the path stays in the address. “Learn this” asks about the entries shown. Visible to whoever can read the base.
viewPart.modeHint: table, tree, matrix, map, quilt or landscape (also: tabela, drzewo, macierz, mapa, postepy, krajobraz) — empty: as saved
viewPart.switchHint: “yes” (or “tak”) — the visitor may change how it is shown and search in the view; empty or “no” — they see only what is chosen here
viewPart.missingView: Choose a view (saved in the base’s “Entries”).
viewPart.showsStrip: One line: name, how many entries, a “See” button.
viewPart.showsTall: The whole view: search, table, tree, matrix, map, progress map or landscape; a matrix cell, a tile and a clicked entry open below.
viewPart.showsBlock: The first entries of the view — the rest in full screen; progress map — up to 60 tiles; landscape — up to 24 fields.

question.label: Question
question.use: A question with an answer to check. In a presentation — a step of the flow: after a right and after a wrong answer it can lead to different places, and answers count in the browser or in Cogita. In a story with a knowledge base it can be a real question from the base ("question": its id or @name) — the answer then counts for what it is about, and together with revisions; an own question with "about" counts for the listed entries.
question.missValue: Choose whether the sentence is true.
question.missBack: Enter what is on the back.
question.answers: Right answers — each on its own line
question.exExplain: Baptism, confirmation, Eucharist, penance, anointing of the sick, holy orders, matrimony.
question.sPrompt: the question text (for a flashcard: the front)
question.sOptions: options, each on its own line (one, many)
question.sCorrect: numbers of the right options from 0, comma-separated, e.g. "1" or "0,2"
question.sAnswers: right answers, each on its own line (text, number); the back side (flash)
question.sValue: "tak" (yes) or "nie" (no) — whether the sentence is true (truefalse)
question.sUnit: unit of the right answers, e.g. "N·m" (number)
question.sQuantity: quantity (number) — e.g. "Torque", "Energy", "Mass", "Length"; then an answer in another unit of this quantity is converted, and a unit of another quantity is an error ("12 J" for a question about torque)
question.sTolerance: how far off an answer may be, in the question’s unit, e.g. "0,5" (number)
question.sQuestion: in a story with a knowledge base (a presentation with "story.base"): a real question from that base — its id or @name; then it shows itself (the fields above are not needed), and the answer lies on its card: it counts for what it is about (the question’s "about"), and together with revisions
question.sAbout: in a story with a knowledge base: for which entries of that base the answer to this (own) question counts — id or @name, each on its own line; knowledge of these entries grows with a right answer (landscape, path, conditions)
question.showsStrip: {form}: question and answer in one strip.
question.showsBlock: {form} — question, answer, rating and explanation; in a presentation then “Next” to wherever the result leads.
