fn.sin: sine (angle in radians — rad(30) converts degrees)
fn.asin: arc sine — result in radians (deg(...) converts to degrees)
fn.atan2: atan2(y, x) — angle of the vector (x, y) in radians
fn.floor: round down to a whole number
fn.ceil: round up to a whole number
fn.clamp: clamp(x, from, to) — x limited to the interval
fn.lerp: lerp(a, b, t) — from a to b: t = 0 gives a, t = 1 gives b
fn.exp: e to the power of x
fn.hypot: hypot(x, y) — length of the vector
fn.mod: mod(a, b) — remainder, always from 0 to b (also for negative numbers)
fn.step: step(edge, x) — 0 before the edge, 1 from the edge on
fn.smooth: smooth(from, to, x) — smoothly from 0 to 1 as x goes from “from” to “to”
fn.rand: rand(x) — a “random” number 0–1, always the same for the same x (e.g. rand(i) for each copy)
fn.onstep: onstep(x, step) — 1 when x lies on the step grid (onstep(2.25, 0.25) → 1): a condition for random tasks so that the solution can be set
fn.root: root(x, n) — n-th root (root(27, 3) → 3; of a negative number only for odd n)
fn.log: log(x) — base 10, log(x, b) — base b: log(8, 2) → 3
fn.sig: sig(x, n) — rounding to n significant digits: sig(0.012345, 2) → 0.012
fn.fact: fact(n) — factorial n! (n a whole number 0–170)
fn.binom: binom(n, k) — binomial coefficient: how many ways to choose k out of n
fn.isint: isint(x) — 1 when x is a whole number (condition: the result must be whole)
fn.fmt: fmt(x, digits) — number as text with a decimal comma: fmt(9.81, 1) → "9,8"
fn.fmtpi: fmtpi(x, digits) — number as a multiple of π: fmtpi(2.356) → "0,75π", fmtpi(3.1416) → "π" (up to 2 places, no trailing zeros)

listFn.len: len(x) — how many items a list has (or characters a text)
listFn.at: at(list, i) — the item at place i, counting from 0 (−1: the last); same as list[i]
listFn.take: take(list, k) — the first k items
listFn.drop: drop(list, k) — without the first k items
listFn.slice: slice(list, from, to) — a piece: from inclusive, to exclusive (from 0; negative counts from the end)
listFn.sort: sort(list) — ascending: numbers by value, texts alphabetically, entries by name (descending: reverse(sort(list)))
listFn.shuffle: shuffle(list) — randomly shuffled (the task’s draw: same task number, same order)
listFn.choose: choose(list, k) — k different items chosen at random (no repeats)
listFn.pick: pick(list) — one item chosen at random
listFn.contains: contains(list, x) — 1 when x is in the list (for a text: when the text contains x)
listFn.index: index(list, x) — the place of x in the list, from 0 (−1: not there)
listFn.range: range(from, to, step) — numbers from…to INCLUSIVE (range(1, 5) → [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]); step defaults to 1
listFn.join: join(list, separator) — the items in one text (comma by default)
listFn.concat: concat(a, b, …) — lists joined into one (a single value is added as an item)
listFn.list: list(a, b, …) — a list of these values (same as [a, b, …])
listFn.get: get(entry, "key") — a field of the entry by key (same as entry.key)
listFn.str: str(x) — as text; a number with a decimal comma, up to 12 significant digits
listFn.num: num(text) — a number from a text ("3,5" → 3.5)
listFn.sub: sub(x) — digits and the signs + − ( ) as subscript: "SO" + sub(4) → "SO₄"
listFn.plain: plain(x) — sub- and superscripts back to plain characters: "Al₂(SO₄)₃" → "Al2(SO4)3"
listFn.gcd: gcd(a, b, …) — greatest common divisor of whole numbers (lists too)
listFn.lcm: lcm(a, b, …) — least common multiple (lists too): lcm(3, 2) → 6

lazyFn.if: if(condition, a, b) — a when the condition holds, otherwise b (same as condition ? a : b)
lazyFn.filter: filter(list, condition) — the items for which the condition holds: filter(jony, it.ladunek > 0)
lazyFn.map: map(list, expression) — the expression for each item: map(wydarzenia, it.label)
lazyFn.sortby: sortby(list, key) — ascending by the expression: sortby(wydarzenia, it.data) — earliest first
lazyFn.find: find(list, condition) — the first item that meets the condition (none: "")
lazyFn.any: any(list, condition) — 1 when at least one item meets the condition
lazyFn.all: all(list, condition) — 1 when every item meets the condition
lazyFn.count: count(list) — how many items; count(list, condition) — how many meet the condition
lazyFn.sum: sum(list) or sum(list, expression) — the sum: sum(skladniki, it.masa)
lazyFn.avg: avg(list) or avg(list, expression) — the average
lazyFn.min: min(a, b, …) — the smallest number; min(list); min(list, expression)
lazyFn.max: max(a, b, …) — the largest number; max(list); max(list, expression)
lazyFn.minby: minby(list, key) — the item with the smallest key: minby(wydarzenia, it.data) — the earliest
lazyFn.maxby: maxby(list, key) — the item with the largest key

expr.unclosedText: unclosed text — a quotation mark is missing
expr.tooDeep: the expression is nested too deeply
expr.fieldAfterDot: a field name was expected after the dot
expr.breaksOff: the expression breaks off — something is missing
expr.needsEach: {fn}({set}, …) needs an expression after the comma
expr.listTooLong: a list in the expression has more than {n} items
expr.needsParens: “{name}” is a function — it needs parentheses: {name}(…)
expr.dotOnlyInWorld: “{path}” — a dot in a name only works in a world (“world”)
expr.afterDot: “{path}” — after the dot: parent, root, outer or self

exprHelp.intro: Expressions (values computed on the fly) — text, e.g. "v0*cos(rad(kat))":
exprHelp.numbers: numbers: 3, 0.5, 2e-3 (decimal point); texts in apostrophes: 'ok'; names: variables, computed values, simulation state and built-in names
exprHelp.compare: comparisons: < <= > >= == != — give 1 (yes) or 0 (no); logic: && (and), || (or), ! (not); condition: w ? a : b
exprHelp.text: text + number joins text (number with a decimal comma, up to 3 places); fmt(x, digits) — number with a chosen number of places
exprHelp.constants: constants: pi, tau (2·pi), e, true (1), false (0) — an own variable with such a name (e.g. "e" as the coefficient of restitution) takes precedence
exprHelp.angles: Angles: sin/cos/tan work in radians — rad(angle) converts an angle in degrees, deg(...) converts the result of asin/acos/atan2.
exprHelp.world: In a world ("world"): parent.x, root.x — value of the parent, of the root (parent.parent.x — of the grandparent); outer.x — of the thing that is summing up; name.x — of the thing with that "id"
exprHelp.can: can — 1 when the person may change something in this thing (drag, set), 0 when it is given; can.pos — when they may change "pos" in particular (e.g. colour for given vs changeable, arrows ↔)
exprHelp.end: An unknown name is an error (the editor shows where); division by 0 gives infinity — such a shape is not drawn for the moment.
exprHelp.aggregates: summaries: {list} — e.g. sum(children, total*arm), count(children), count(odwaznik, mass > 5), all(belka, abs(mom) < 0.05)
exprHelp.sets: sets: children, descendants (all below), siblings, others (others of this kind), things (all) or the name of a kind; the expression after the comma is computed in EACH thing of the set (its names, its parent), and outer.x reaches the one that asks
exprHelp.lists: lists (e.g. range(1, 10)): {list} — described in Cogita’s generated tasks; in filter/map/sortby… "it" is the item, "i" its place

genHelp.intro: Expressions in generated tasks — the same language as in drawings (numbers with a decimal point, texts in apostrophes, + - * / % ^, < <= > >= == !=, && || !, w ? a : b), plus:
genHelp.lists: lists: [1, 2, 3], [a, b]; item: list[0] (from 0; list[-1] — the last); list + list — joined
genHelp.entry: entry (drawn from the base): entry.field (e.g. kation.ladunek), entry.id, entry.label; a number field with a quantity: entry.field_si (in SI), entry.field_unit; date: entry.date (number yyyymmdd, for comparisons), entry.date_text (in words); reference: entry.period.label (one step further)
genHelp.each: an expression for each item (filter, map, sortby, count, any, all, find, sum, avg, min, max, minby, maxby): "it" — the item, "i" — its place (from 0), e.g. filter(jony, it.ladunek < 0), map(wydarzenia, it.label)
genHelp.compare: texts compare alphabetically ("Ala" < "Ola"); == also compares lists (item by item) and entries (by id)
genHelp.random: drawing at random in an expression (shuffle, choose, pick) uses the task number — the same number gives the same task
genHelp.listFns: functions for lists, texts and entries:
genHelp.limits: Limits: a list up to {items} items, up to {work} steps over lists in one expression — more gives NaN (the task is not drawn).

move.label: Moves
move.says: changes place: "to": [x, y] — to a point (from "from", usually [0, 0]), or "path": [[x, y], …] — along a way through the points ("times": when at each, 0–1)

size.says: grows or shrinks: "from" → "to" (1 — as it is; a number or [width, height])

turn.label: Turns
turn.says: turns: "from" → "to" in degrees (360 — a full turn)

reveal.label: Reveals
reveal.says: is revealed from the left: "from" → "to" (0 — nothing, 1 — all of it)

keys.label: Frames
keys.says: everything at once, frame by frame: "keys": [{ "at": 0–1, "x", "y", "scale", "sx", "sy", "rotate", "opacity", "blur", "draw", "color", "stroke", "glow", "reveal", "clip", "ease" }]

draw.label: Draws itself
draw.says: a line is drawn from start to end: "from" → "to" (0 — nothing, 1 — all of it; below 0 — nothing for a moment longer, above 1 (up to 10) — finished before the motion ends)

rise.label: Rises
rise.says: appears, rising a few pixels — slide text after arriving

assemble.label: Assembles
assemble.says: a layer appears, slightly raised and scaled down; the next ones, with growing delay, assemble the sign

focus.label: Comes into focus
focus.says: from a slight blur and from below into focus

float.label: Floats
float.says: sways gently by a few pixels and comes back

breathe.label: Breathes
breathe.says: grows and brightens, shrinks and fades

drift.label: Drifts
drift.says: moves slowly diagonally and grows, then returns — background, mist

sway.label: Sways
sway.says: waves up and down very slowly, stretching vertically — background threads

wave.label: Wave
wave.says: flows sideways and vertically along an irregular way — bands of waves

blink.label: Blinks
blink.says: dims and flares up — a warning, an error

desc.intro: Motion ("motion") — on a module on a slide and in a presentation scene, on a layer of a layered picture, on a background layer and on every element of a drawing ("animation"):
desc.shape: { "name": "move", "to": [40, -12], "duration": 900, "delay": 120, "repeat": "once", "ease": "inOut" } or a list of up to three of them (outermost first); the plain word "rise" is enough too
desc.times: "duration", "delay" — in milliseconds; for a looping motion "delay" may be negative (it starts mid-cycle)
desc.repeat: "repeat" — "once" (once, when the thing is reached; again on the next arrival — until then it stays at the first frame), "loop" (over and over while visible), "alternate" (there and back), or a number of repeats
desc.ease: "ease" — how it passes from frame to frame: "linear", "ease", "in", "out", "inOut", "step" or "cubic-bezier(a, b, c, d)"
desc.unit: "unit" — "px" (usually; in a drawing — drawing units) or "%" (percent of its own size)
desc.by: "by" — only in a presentation scene: the motion follows not the clock but the PROGRESS of the scene — "scene" (inside the scene: from the first to the last step), "enter" (the scene coming in), "leave" (the scene going out); 0 — the first frame, 1 — the last. Scrolling back reverses the motion, stopping stops it; "duration", "delay" and "repeat" then play no role
desc.verbs: Basic words (any motion can be built from them):
desc.frame: Frame ("keys"): "at" 0–1 — when; "x", "y" — shift; "scale" or "sx", "sy" — size; "rotate" — degrees; "opacity" 0–1; "blur" — blur in px;
desc.frame2: "draw" — how much of the line is drawn (0–1); "color" — fill or text colour; "stroke" — line colour; "glow" — a glow "x y blur colour" (e.g. "0 0 10px rgba(160, 220, 255, 0.75)");
desc.frame3: "reveal" 0–1 — how much is visible from the left; "clip" — a cut-out "inset(top right bottom left round 1rem)", a circle "circle(40% at 50% 50%)" or an oval "ellipse(60% 40% at 50% 50%)" (with "by" — a mask that grows with progress); "ease" — the passage to the next frame. What a frame does not give flows in one motion between the frames that give it; before the first such frame — as the thing is by itself, after the last — it stays.
desc.colors: Colours: "#rrggbb", "rgba(…)", theme names "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted", "ok", "danger" — with "/35" at the end: 35 % opacity.
desc.presets: Ready-made motions (from the old Cogita show) — entrances:
desc.reduced: With the system setting “reduce motion” nothing moves — everything stands as described without motion.

live.intro: A drawing to move ("animation" with the keys below) — a person sets something (slider, drag, button) and sees the effect at once; there may also be a simulation (motion from equations) and a goal to reach. Just like Brilliant lessons: first doing, then explaining.
live.vars: "vars" — values to set (up to {n}): [{ "name": "kat", "value": 45, "min": 0, "max": 90, "step": 1, "unit": "°", "label": "Angle", "random": [from, to] }] — "random": a different value from the interval each time it opens (in Cogita: on each attempt)
live.let: "let" — values computed from others, in this order, anew in every frame: [{ "name": "zasieg", "value": "v0^2*sin(rad(2*kat))/g" }]
live.events: "events": [{ "when": "y < 0 && vy < 0", "set": { "y": "-y", "vy": "-e*vy" }, "stop": false, "say": "Bounce!", "mood": "info" }] — when the condition BECOMES true (collision, bounce, end); "set" computes all values at once and only then assigns them,
live.until: "until": "t > 5" (end), "dt": 0.002 (step in s), "speed": 1 (pace), "auto": true (starts by itself when the drawing is visible; otherwise the "run" button), "loop": true (again after the end), "max": 600 (longest, s), "sleep": true (falls asleep when nothing moves any more and wakes on a change) }
live.rk4: Computed with the 4th-order Runge-Kutta method in fixed steps — on a slow phone the result is the same. Changing a value the start depends on restarts the simulation; changing a value in "rate" (e.g. gravity) takes effect at once.
live.slider: { "type": "slider", "var": "kat", "label": "Angle", "unit": "°", "digits": 0 } — a slider (range and step from "vars"); "number" — a number field;
live.rules: "rules" — rules (up to {n}): [{ "when": "abs(x - cel) < 0.5 && y <= 0", "say": "Hit at {fmt(kat,0)}°!", "mood": "ok"|"miss"|"info", "goal": true, "once": true, "set": {…}, "do": "pause", "go": "next" }]
live.rules2: acts when the condition BECOMES true (checked after every simulation step — flying through a hoop counts too); "say" appears below the drawing ({…} — computed);
live.goal: "goal": true — this is the goal: reached = task solved (in Cogita: a correct answer); "go" — in a presentation: "next" (onward), "back", a scene key or "link:<id>"; "for": 1 — the condition must hold this many seconds without a break (“steadily”)
live.show: every control may have "show": "solved" — it is visible only when the expression is true (e.g. a “Next” button after solving)
live.predict: "predict" — predict first, then see: true or { "start": true, "say": "…", "check": "Check", "again": "Adjust", "hold": "Predict" }; the drawing stands still (simulation stopped, rules silent, no goal) while the person sets their prediction; “Check” lets it run, “Adjust” (or any change after checking) stops it again; "start": false — runs at once, and “Predict” stops it on request.
live.held: In expressions "held" = 1 while it stands still — whatever gives away the result waits: "stroke": "=held ? 'ink' : (ok ? 'ok' : 'danger')", "show": "!held"; "tries" — how many times it has been checked (e.g. “first time!”). In Cogita the drawing stands until the card’s “Check”.
live.task: "task" — a different task each time, equally hard: { "require": ["onstep(s, 0.5)", "abs(s - r0) >= 1"], "solve": "w2.pos = 3 + s", "new": "New task", "tries": 200 }
live.task2: values with "random" are drawn (variables and properties of things; a property may be an expression of them: "m": "=a", "pos": "=3 - d") until every "require" condition is true, the task is not solved at the start (no "goal" rule holds) and the "solve" solution can be set by hand (within the limits, on something that may be changed);
live.task3: comparable difficulty comes from the conditions alone: the same steps, numbers from the same range, the result on the slider grid (onstep), far enough from the start. When nothing fits, the task from the "value" values stays. "new" — a “New task” button (false — none); in Cogita every attempt draws the same way and remembers the numbers, and "solve" is the solution of the question unless the question gives its own.
live.panel: "panel" — "below" (controls below the drawing, usual) or "side" (beside it, when the drawing is wide; on a phone always below)
live.elements: In the elements of the drawing:
live.anyNumber: every number (x, y, w, h, r, x2, y2, rotate, scale, opacity, width, size) and colour (fill, stroke) may be an expression: "x": "=x0 + v*t", "fill": "=trafione ? 'ok' : 'accent'"
live.showStep: "show": "step >= 1" — visible only when the condition is true
live.drag: "drag": { "x": "cel" } — dragging sets the value to the finger position (x, y); or { "set": { "kat": "deg(atan2(py, px))" }, "label": "Direction" } — from the finger position (px, py); "label" for screen readers. The handle can be grabbed from 44 px and works with the arrow keys
live.tap: "tap": "run" or { "set": { "widac": "1 - widac" }, "do": "toggle", "go": "next", "label": "Flip" } — a click on the element (also Enter/space)
live.repeat: "repeat": 20 — this many copies of the element; in each "i" (0, 1, …) and "n" (how many) — e.g. gas particles, a scale (up to {n})
live.kinds: new kinds: "arrow" (a vector from x, y to x2, y2; "head" — arrowhead size), "poly" ("points": [[x, y], …] — numbers or "=…"; "closed": true — a polygon),
live.plot: "plot" (a curve: "fn": "A*sin(k*u)" — y of u, or "fx", "fy" — a way; "var" (usually "u"), "from", "to", "samples" (up to {n})),
live.trace: "trace" (a trail: "fx": "x", "fy": "y" — a point every "every" s of simulation, the last "keep" points; cleared on restart),
live.frame: "frame" (a frame with a world: the rectangle x, y, w, h shows a part of the world "view": [x0, y0, x1, y1] — y grows UPWARD, units are e.g. metres; "axes": { "x": "x [m]", "y": "y [m]", "grid": true }, "clip": true — what goes outside the frame disappears;
live.frame2: in a frame positions are in world units and sizes (r, width, size, head) in drawing units; a "rect" stands with its lower-left corner at (x, y); a group in a frame shifts by world x, y and rotates counter-clockwise)
live.world: A world of things ("world") — when the drawing is a set-up of things that are added, moved, hung and removed (a balance of beams and weights, a mobile, gears). You do not write a game, you describe kinds of things, the things at the start and the rules:
live.props: "props": [{ "name": "pos", "value": 1, "min": 0, "max": "=parent.length", "step": 0.25, "unit": "m", "label": "Place", "apart": 0.25, "new": "parent.pivot + 1", "when": "!isroot" }] — properties with limits (limits may be expressions; "apart" — distance from siblings; "new" — where a new thing stands; "when" — when the property applies to the thing),
live.thingLet: "let": [{ "name": "total", "value": "bm + sum(children, total)" }] — values computed in each thing (the order follows from what they read),
live.thingState: "state": [{ "name": "angle", "value": 0, "rate": "omega" }] and "events" — the motion of each thing (the same Runge-Kutta; "sim" then gives only "dt", "speed", "auto", "sleep"),
live.shapes: "shapes": [elements as in "elements"] — the look of one thing, computed in it ("=x" is ITS x; in a frame — world coordinates),
live.thingDrag: "drag": { "pos": "parent.pivot + (px - parent.x)*cos(parent.angle)" } — what dragging sets (the finger in the world: px, py; the handle lies at its "x", "y", radius "hit"),
live.can: "can": { "edit": ["m", "pos"], "add": ["ciezarek"], "remove": true, "copy": true }, "readouts": [{ "label", "value", "unit", "digits" }] (the panel of the chosen thing), "children": 8,
live.brief: "brief": "{m} kg" — what the thing is called in the panel (“Weight 2 kg”); "mark": false — no dashed ring around things that may be changed (when the kind shows it itself: by colour and arrows from "can", "can.pos") }
live.things: "things" — the things at the start: [{ "id": "w1", "kind": "ciezarek", "parent": "b1", "m": 4, "pos": 1.5, "lock": ["m"] }] — properties directly; { "random": [from, to] } — at random (in Cogita on each attempt); "=a + 1" — an expression of the drawing’s values (random tasks); "lock": true — nothing may change, a list — these properties may not
live.allow: "allow" — what is allowed in this world: { "add", "remove", "copy", "edit", "drag" (true/false), "roots": ["belka"] (what may be placed at the top) }; "limits": { "things": 40, "depth": 6 }
live.keep: "keep": [{ "when": "edits <= 2", "say": "Only two moves!" }] — must always hold: a change after which it does not hold is undone; "save": true — a workshop (save, load, JSON); "hint" — a hint when nothing is chosen ({…} — computed)
live.panelGiven: The panel shows what is given (“Given”: things that may not be changed) and what the person sets (“You set”: in a puzzle each changeable property as its own slider, without choosing a thing); "list": true/false forces or turns off these rows (by default: when nothing may be added or removed and there are at most 6).
live.worldEl: In the elements: { "type": "world" } in a frame — the things stand here; frame "camera": true — zooming (+, −, Ctrl+wheel, two fingers) and panning; "view" computed from the things, e.g. "=min(things, bx0)".
live.worldExpr: In the expressions of things: parent.x, root.x, w1.x (a thing by id), outer.x (the one summing up); summaries sum/avg/min/max/count/all/any over a set: children, descendants, siblings, others, things or the name of a kind; built into things: isroot, depth, index, selected, nchildren; in the whole drawing: edits (how many changes since “Start over”), nthings.
live.worldUndo: Every change (drag, panel, adding) goes through the rules of the world and has “Undo” (Ctrl+Z); in Cogita the answer is the arranged world — replayed by the same rules and checked by simulating to the end; solution: "w2.pos = 5". Pattern: the example “Balance — workshop”.
live.builtins: Built-in names: {list} — t: simulation time (s), time: time since the drawing was shown (s; motion without a simulation, e.g. "y": "=sin(2*time)"), step: the place in a presentation scene (0 at its start, 1 after the first step, smoothly in between — for revealing), i/n: copy number and how many copies, u: the course of a curve, px/py: the finger while dragging; edits: how many changes in the world, nthings: how many things; held: 1 while the drawing stands still for a prediction, tries: how many times it was checked; in a thing can: 1 when the person may change it.
live.light: To keep the drawing light (phone): up to about 300 elements, no "blur"/"glow" on many elements, "dt" 0.001–0.005, always "until" or an event with "stop", at most 4–6 controls. The drawing computes only when something changes and stops when it is not visible.
live.physics: Physics — patterns: projectile (x, y, vx, vy; "rate" vy: "-g"), pendulum (th, om; om: "-g/L*sin(th)"), spring (x, v; v: "-k/m*x - c*v"), incline (a = g*(sin − μ·cos)), collision (an event, "set" both velocities at once), refraction (let: angle from asin(n1/n2*sin)), wave ("plot" with "fn" of u and time).

prompt.intro: Prepare the JSON of a drawing to move for the “Animation” module in REcreatio (a page or a presentation; the same drawing can be a question in Cogita).
prompt.topic: Topic: [describe the phenomenon, e.g. “projectile motion — the learner sets the angle and hits the target”].
prompt.rules: Rules: first the person does something (slider, drag, button), then sees the effect; one idea per drawing; labels in English; a goal ("goal") only when it is a task.
prompt.return: Return ONE JSON object with the keys "alt", "size", "elements" and — as needed — "vars", "let", "sim", "controls", "rules", "predict", "task", "panel", "symbols", "world". No comments.

world.givenGroup: Given — you do not change this
world.notLayout: This is not a layout (JSON with a “things” list).

model.predictSay: Predict first: set everything the way you think — then click “Check” and see what happens.

run.nameTaken: this name is already a variable or a computed value
run.notSettable: “{name}” is neither a variable nor simulation state — it cannot be set
run.infinite: the simulation gave infinity or NaN — check “rate” (division by 0?)
run.notAllowed: That is not allowed in this task.

task.unknownKey: “{key}” — there is no such variable or property of a thing (thing.property)

things.notOwn: “{name}” is neither a property nor state of the kind “{kind}”
things.notProp: “{name}” is not a property of this kind
things.cycle: computed values depend on each other in a circle — computing them in list order

drawing.saveFailed: Could not save — the browser does not allow it.

balance.solved: Balanced! On every beam, mass × arm on the left equals mass × arm on the right.
balance.stillBad: Beams still out of balance: {bad}. Compare mass × arm on both sides of the pivot.
balance.hint: Tap a beam or a weight to choose it; drag to move it.
balance.title: Balance — workshop
balance.says: A world of things: beams and weights that you hang, move and change; each beam computes its moment and tilts until you balance it.
balance.alt: A balance of beams and weights — workshop
balance.predict: The world stands still: build or change what you like and predict what will happen — then “Check”.
balance.workshopHint: Tap a beam to hang a weight or another beam on it; drag a weight along the beam. Undo: Ctrl+Z.

gears.title: Gear train
gears.says: Gears as a world of things: each gear meshes with the gear it hangs on; the number of teeth decides the speed. Add a gear, change the teeth, drag it around its neighbour.
gears.alt: A gear train: the driving gear and the gears meshing with it
gears.hint: Tap a gear: change its number of teeth or add the next one. Drag a gear around its neighbour.

projectile.title: Projectile motion
projectile.says: Angle and speed, a short sight, the flight trail, a draggable target; hitting it is the goal of the task.
projectile.alt: Projectile motion: angle and speed decide where the ball lands
projectile.short: Short by {fmt(cel - x, 1)} m. The longest flight is at an angle of 45°.
projectile.dragArrow: Direction and speed — drag the arrowhead
projectile.caption: angle {fmt(kat, 0)}° · speed {fmt(v0, 1)} m/s

pendulum.title: Pendulum
pendulum.says: A draggable bob (deflection and length), Earth / Mars / Moon, the period from the formula and a trail.
pendulum.alt: Pendulum: the period depends on length and gravity

spring.title: Oscillation on a spring
spring.says: A block to pull out, stiffness, mass, damping; an x(t) graph and energy bars.
spring.alt: A block on a spring: oscillation and exchange of energy

incline.title: Inclined plane with friction
incline.says: Slope, friction, forces as arrows; the block starts only when tan α > μ.
incline.alt: Inclined plane: the forces acting on the block
incline.stays: The block stays: friction μ·cos α is at least sin α (tan α ≤ μ).
incline.slides: The block slides down with an acceleration of {fmt(a, 2)} m/s².

collision.title: Collision of carts
collision.says: Masses, speed, elasticity; momentum stays the same, energy — only at e = 1.
collision.alt: Collision of two carts on a track
collision.hit: Collision! Momentum before and after: {fmt(p, 2)} kg·m/s.

refraction.title: Refraction of light
refraction.says: A draggable source, media to choose; Snell’s law and total reflection.
refraction.alt: A ray of light at the boundary of two media
refraction.total: Total internal reflection: sin α₂ would come out greater than 1, so the light does not pass.
refraction.denser: Into a denser medium: the ray bends towards the normal.
refraction.thinner: Into a less dense medium: the ray bends away from the normal.
refraction.dragSource: Light source — drag along the arc

waves.title: Superposition of waves
waves.says: Two travelling waves and their sum; wavelength and phase shift; in a presentation the sum appears in the second step.

orbit.title: Orbit
orbit.says: The launch speed as a draggable arrow: too slow — it falls, just right — a circle, faster — an ellipse, too fast — it escapes.
orbit.alt: A satellite in orbit around a planet
orbit.fell: Too slow — the satellite fell onto the planet.
orbit.escape: Escape speed: √2 ≈ 1.41 times the circular speed — the satellite flies away.

ball.title: Bouncing ball
ball.says: Moves on its own from the start: the ball falls and bounces; drag it to change the height.
ball.alt: A ball falls and bounces off the ground

sceneChange.fade: Crossfade — the previous one fades, this one appears
sceneChange.build: Build — the scene is there at once, its modules enter each in its own way
sceneChange.fly: Fly-through — the camera flies through the previous scene (its depth and word cloud)
sceneChange.rise: Rise — this one rises slightly from below
sceneChange.zoom: Zoom — the previous one grows and disappears, this one emerges from the depth
sceneChange.cover: Cover — this one slides up over the previous one
sceneChange.reveal: Reveal — the previous one slides up and reveals this one
sceneChange.side: From the side — this one slides in from the right, the previous one moves left
sceneChange.dissolve: Dissolve — the previous one fades, blurs and sinks, this one sharpens while rising (like the Cogita show)

arrival.fromLeft: Comes in past the left edge
arrival.fromRight: Comes in past the right edge

A dashed line — “next” leads to the next one in the list; delete it (Delete) to make this the end. Click a scene to choose targets from the list and make buttons; double-click opens the scene.

story.browserOnly: Only in the browser — an example; nothing leaves the device
story.inCogita: In Cogita — signed-in people (and people from a form) learn on their own account

settings.widthHint: The places of modules count within this width — on a wide screen the picture stays together (80 rem — like the Cogita show). The background stays on the whole screen.
settings.backdropHint: It stands behind all scenes. When there is one, the scenes are transparent and their own backgrounds (scene colour, its layers) lie in it and pass smoothly into each other — threads, waves and mist stay.
settings.soundHint: Plays only when the visitor clicks this button in the bar at the bottom — on a loop, quiet when the tab is hidden.
settings.volumeHint: Each scene can be quieter (scene settings).
settings.night: Other colours when the visitor’s device is in dark mode
settings.colorHint: A module’s colour can also be a pair “light|dark” (e.g. #ece0c9|#2a2113) or a name: accent, ink, ground, muted — then it follows the scene’s colours.
settings.sceneName: Name (in the scene bar; a link “#name” in a text leads here)
settings.change: How this scene replaces the previous one
settings.firstScene: This is the first scene — its transition is not visible.
settings.keep: The previous scene stays underneath until the transition ends
settings.jumpHint: How long the transition takes when an arrow or one turn of the wheel starts it.
settings.stepsHint: How many stops the scene has. A module with a step is then highlighted.
settings.branches: Branches, buttons and links outside — in the “Transitions” view.
settings.emphasis: Steps highlight their modules (the others fade and move back)
settings.grow: The scene grows as you go through it
settings.sceneVolumeHint: 1 — as in the whole presentation, 0 — silence on this scene; it changes smoothly between scenes.
settings.colorsEmpty: Empty — like the whole presentation. Also “light|dark”.
settings.depthHint: Modules with depth (z below zero) stand in the space of the scene. When the NEXT scene has the “Fly-through” transition, the camera flies through this scene — the nearer ones pass first, the deepest stays alone for a moment.
settings.flown: The next scene flies through this one.
settings.linger: Slow down at the deepest (the sentence stays alone for a moment)
settings.words: Word cloud — words (one per line; empty — no cloud)
settings.isButton: On this scene it is a button — a click leads on
settings.linksOutside: You add links outside in the “Transitions” view.
settings.everyHint: E.g. a fixed “Contact” button that stands on all scenes (with “Also stands before its first and after its last”). A target set separately for a scene takes precedence.
settings.sameTarget: The same target on every scene it stands on
settings.tallSame: On the narrow screen: as on the wide one — a change here makes a separate place.
settings.tallOwn: On the narrow screen: a separate place.
settings.maxWidth: At most this width (rem) — on a large screen it does not grow further
settings.zHint: 0 — flat. Below zero — into the depth of the scene (visible in a camera fly-through).
settings.motionHint: When the scene is reached (once) or over and over while visible — moves, grows, turns, fades in, draws; or a ready-made motion from the Cogita show.
settings.delayHint: The part of the transition after which it starts (0 — at once, 0.5 — halfway).
settings.spanHint: What part of the transition its appearance takes.
settings.travelHint: Tick the scenes on which the module has its place — when the scene changes it passes smoothly from one to the other (also through scenes without a place).
settings.hold: Also stands before its first and after its last place
settings.betweenHint: “Leaves and returns” — the same picture at the start and at the end of the story, and none in the middle; it then stands in the scene it is on, like its own module.
settings.leave: leaves with its scene and returns with the next
settings.layerHint: Higher — in front. A travelling one with a negative value (−1…−5) stands in front of the scene background but behind its texts; from 10 up — above all scenes.
settings.removeModule: Delete the module from the page
settings.cropHint: This point of the picture stays in view when the panel changes size (e.g. “50% 58%” — the focus). Empty — the point set in the picture module.
settings.radiusHint: 71 — reaches the corners when the centre is in the middle.
settings.frames: Frames — change with the scene’s progress
settings.progressHint: Scrolling (also backwards), the keyboard and the show move the same progress — stopped progress is a stopped picture.
settings.oneStep: The scene has one step — progress stays at 0. Add a step in the scene settings.
settings.framesHint: [{ "at": 0.4, "x": 30, "w": 40, "h": 55, "crop": "50% 60%" }, { "step": 2, "opacity": 0, "tall": { "y": 20 } }] — "at" 0–1 or "step" (from 0); a frame changes only what it gives; "tall" — its values on a phone.
settings.notFrames: — this is not a list of frames
settings.frameHere: + Frame at the end: the place as it is now
settings.stillHint: With the setting “reduce motion” the frames stand at one point (0–1) — a still composition with the same content. Empty: at the end (on exit — at the start); frames with steps jump from step to step.

json.usageTitle: How the app uses this data
json.usage:
- An alias and a domain are just a second entrance: the service leads them to the target page and takes everything from there — title, introduction, modules, look. A change to the page is visible at once under every entrance.
- Under an own domain subpages have shorter addresses: on cogita.pl the page cogita/kursy is #/kursy.
- Access follows the target page: an access-only page (sealed too) stays so under an alias and under a domain, and one blocked after a report shows under no entrance.
- Nobody gets new rights: the page is still edited by those who run its address. An alias's "role" only says who manages it — not who sees the page.
- An alias is not a separate page: where a page is chosen (e.g. for access links) it doesn't appear — the target page is chosen. The dependency map shows the domain next to its page.
json.formatTitle: Addresses and domains as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
json.intro:
Aliases and own domains of the pages this account runs (Workshop → Settings → “Addresses and domains” → “Import and export (JSON)”, #/workspace/addresses). An alias is a second entrance to a page inside recreatio.pl (recreatio.pl/parafia/news shows parafia/aktualnosci); an own domain shows a page under another name (cogita.pl shows recreatio.pl/cogita). The content stays where it lies — the entrance only points to it.
What the import does:
- It first shows the plan of changes with warnings; it saves only after “Import”.
- An alias that doesn't exist yet is created. An alias that exists is recognised by "path": the same target — no change; a different target — a warning (an alias's target can't be changed nor an alias removed — in the app either).
- It connects a domain to the page "path", swaps it for another or — only with "host": null — disconnects it. Moving a domain to another page: at the old page "host": null (or another domain), at the new one this domain — the import first disconnects, then connects.
- Pages not in "domains" and aliases not in "aliases" stay unchanged. It removes nothing else.
- It doesn't take addresses: a top-level address (e.g. recreatio.pl/cogita) is issued by the server with a code — “Pages” → “Take an address”.
What remains outside the app — for each new domain (the plan reminds of it on import):
{outside}
Signing in under an own domain also needs api.{host} (a CNAME to the same service, with a certificate) — also work on the server; public pages work without it.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.

how.title: How it works
how.root: An address taken with a code is a root. parish is taken once, with a code from the server. Everything below it — parish/grzegorzki — is opened by whoever runs it, in the workshop and without a code. Such routes can't be taken separately, and that's on purpose: otherwise one address would have two people responsible, and which page a visitor sees would depend on the order of rows in the database.
how.local: Sub-routes are local. If cogita.pl shows recreatio.pl/cogita, the page cogita/kursy is available under that domain as cogita.pl/#/kursy — without repeating the root name. That's why links on a page are written locally: the same link works both under recreatio.pl and under the own domain. If it contained the full path, one of the two versions would always be broken.
how.alias: An alias is a second entrance, not a second page. Nothing is saved under an alias — title, introduction and modules change where the content lies. The service refuses to save to an alias whether or not someone took it: two versions of the same thing would mean that one of them is out of date.

out.title: What has to be done outside the platform
out.lead: Connecting a domain here saves only one thing: that this name means this page. For a browser to get here at all, three more things are needed that aren't in the database.
out.hostTitle: 2. The same site under the new name
out.host: GitHub Pages accepts one own domain per repository, and that one is already recreatio.pl. A second domain therefore needs its own place: a separate repository with its own CNAME file or any static file hosting. An entry in the registry alone won't do it.
out.originTitle: 3. The service's consent to the new name
out.origin: A browser won't let a page from cogita.pl read answers from api.recreatio.pl until the service lists that name (Api:Origins). That takes someone with access to the server — it isn't set in the workshop, and that's how it should be: the list of allowed names is part of the security, not of the content.
out.loginTitle: Signing in under an own domain
out.login: Public pages work without signing in — the visitor needs nothing, point 3 is enough. But signing in under an own domain is harder: the session cookie is issued by api.recreatio.pl, so on cogita.pl it is a third-party cookie, and Safari and Firefox block or partition those. The session simply won't come back.
out.ways: There are two ways. The simpler: under the own domain only show the page, and manage it on recreatio.pl — there the cookie is first-party. The full one: point api.your-domain (a CNAME record) to the same service and build the software there with VITE_APP_API=https://api.your-domain. Then service and page are under one name, the cookie is first-party and signing in works. It needs a certificate for that subdomain — also work on the server.

text.layers:
Background layers (the page's "cover", a module's "slide.layers", "deck.backdrop").
ORDER = DEPTH: the first layer of the list lies deepest (at the very bottom), each next one lies ON the previous one, the last is on top — right under the slide's content. An opaque layer (a gradient, an image with "opacity" 1 or without transparency in the file) covers everything before it in the list. A large text ("bigtext") must therefore come AFTER an image if it should be visible on the image; an image with "blend": "multiply" needs a light layer before it in the list (underneath) or a light shared background (during a transition other than scrolling it blends only with its own slide's layers). The shared background ("deck.backdrop") lies under all layers of all slides; a slide's layers are visible only in its rectangle — they travel with it and vanish with it. In the editor the list is shown as on the screen: at the top what is on top (i.e. the reverse of the JSON).
Kinds, from those one usually starts with (deepest) to those on top:
  { "kind": "gradient", "speed": 0.12, "angle": 168, "from": "#12203a", "via": null, "to": "#060a12" }
  { "kind": "image", "speed": 0.34, "url": "https://…/tlo.jpg", "opacity": 0.45, "blend": "normal"|"multiply"|"screen"|"overlay"|"soft-light", "position": "center" }
  { "kind": "bigtext", "speed": 0.95, "lines": ["TRASA"], "opacity": 0.1, "color": null }
  { "kind": "glow", "speed": 0.12, "color": "rgba(120, 170, 220, 0.18)", "x": 58, "y": 42, "size": 60, "opacity": 1, "blend": "normal" } — glow: a soft patch of light; "x", "y" — centre in %, "size" — where it fades (% of the distance to the nearest edge)
  { "kind": "vignette", "speed": 0, "strength": 0.35, "reach": 55, "color": "#000000" } — dark corners: darker from "reach" % of the way to the corner, "strength" in the corner
  { "kind": "haze", "speed": 0.08, "color": "rgba(120, 170, 220, 0.08)", "depth": "rgba(30, 60, 100, 0.1)", "blur": 60, "opacity": 0.35, "motion": { "name": "drift" } } — haze: two dark patches ("depth") and a light streak ("color"), strongly blurred, drifting
  { "kind": "mesh", "speed": 0.05, "seed": 7, "count": 4, "color": "rgba(143, 208, 255, 0.25)", "glow": "rgba(167, 224, 255, 0.35)", "center": 0.82, "amplitude": 1, "opacity": 0.9, "dust": true, "motion": { "name": "sway" } } — threads: glowing wave lines above the bottom edge with dust; "count" layers, each waving its own way ("sway": 180–400 s); "center" — wave height (0 top, 1 bottom)
  { "kind": "waves", "speed": 0.05, "seed": 7, "count": 6, "hue": 188, "spread": 32, "opacity": 1, "blur": 1, "motion": [] } — waves: blurred bands near the bottom with light edges (hue "hue"…"hue"+"spread"); in the Cogita show they stand still — with "motion": { "name": "wave" } they flow
  "speed" 0–1 — how slowly the layer moves when scrolling; "opacity" 0–1. An image can be a page file: "page-image:<id>".
  Layer colours can be names: "ground", "accent", "ink", "muted" — then they follow the slides' colours. "seed" — the same number gives the same picture every time; "motion" — the layer's motion (below: Motion), "[]" — stands still.

A module's slide ("slide") — everything except "label" and "layers" is optional:
  "transition" — how this slide replaces the previous one: "scroll" (comes in from below, the default), "flow" (flow: the content moves up with the scrolling and blends at the same time — the previous one moves up and fades with its layers, this one comes in from below and appears; the layers move slower than the content, each at its own pace), "fade" (crossfades in place: the content stands; when the new slide is transparent, the previous one fades meanwhile), "cover" (covers the previous one, which dims), "reveal" (the previous one moves away and reveals it), "zoom" (zoom), "side" (from the right), "dissolve" (dissolve: the previous one fades, blurs and sinks by 12 px, this one sharpens while rising — like the Cogita show). It follows the scrolling, not a clock
  "enter" — how the content appears: "none", "rise", "fade", "zoom", "left", "right"
  "colors" — the slide's own colours, changing smoothly between slides: { "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted" } ("#rrggbb"; left out — like the page)
  "stage" — the module has NO slide of its own: it stands above all and, when the slide changes, moves to its place on the next one:
      { "frames": { "<id of the module-slide or "cover">": { "x": 50, "y": 50, "w": 30, "scale": 1, "rotate": 0, "opacity": 1 } }, "bare": false }
      "x", "y" — centre in percent of the stage; "w" — width in percent; between slides with a place it moves smoothly, before the first and after the last it stands; "bare": true — without a frame (logo, image)
      "max" — at most this width in rem (a logo stays a logo on a large screen); "tall" — other values on a screen taller than wide (phone): { "x", "y", "w", "scale", "rotate", "opacity" } — only those that differ; with its own "w" on a phone exactly that counts
  "motion" — the module's motion on its slide or on the stage (below: Motion), e.g. { "name": "rise", "delay": 220 } — the text rises once the slide is reached
  "layout" — where the slide's content stands: { "align": "start"|"center"|"end", "valign": "start"|"center"|"end", "width": 68, "tall": { "align", "valign", "width" } } — "width" in percent of the stage (stage width — "deck.width"); "tall" — on a phone; left out — in the centre, a comfortable text width
  "with" — the module has NO slide of its own: it stands beside another on its slide, in one row: { "slide": "<module id>", "side": "end"|"start", "share": 42, "tallSide": "start"|"end" } — "side" on the right / on the left, "share" — % of the row width, "tallSide" — on a phone above / below it (an image, an animation beside a text); "with": "<id>" is enough too
text.presentation:
Scenes are screens; modules stand on them anywhere. A scene can have several steps — then the highlight moves from module to module, and the scene follows the highlighted one. A module with a place on several scenes travels: when the scene changes it moves smoothly to its next place. Everything follows the scrolling (wheel, finger, arrows), in the “Show” — the keyboard and clicks.
Inside a scene a module can change with its PROGRESS ("frames" of a place): a large photo shrinks to a frame, moves, is revealed through a mask — scrolling back undoes the change, stopping stops it, and wheel, finger, keyboard and show move the same progress. The more "steps" a scene has, the longer its way.
Scenes don't have to go in order: each has one entrance and exits — “next” (arrows, scrolling: "next") and buttons (modules with "go"). An exit leads to a scene, to the end ("end") or outside ("link:<id>" from "links"). Whoever presses a button goes on that way; back — the way they came.

The page's "show":
  "format" — "screen" (full screen, like a home page; on a phone upright — with "tall" places), "wide" (16:9), "classic" (4:3)
  "fonts" — typeface: "app", "spectral" (Spectral + IBM Plex Sans), "cormorant" (Cormorant Garamond + Source Sans), "plex" (IBM Plex Sans)
  "nav" — the scene bar: "labels" (names at the top), "dots" (dots on the right), "none"
  "links" — ways out: [{ "id": "zapisy", "label": "Zapisz się", "href": "https://…" | "#/strona" | "mailto:…" }] — the exit of a scene or a button leads there through "link:<id>"
  "width" — at most this many rem of stage width: the module places count within it (x, y in percent), the background stays on the whole screen (e.g. 80 — like the Cogita show); left out — the whole window
  "sound" — ambient sound (fire, leaves), only at the viewer's request: { "url": "page-image:<id>" | "https://…/ogrod.mp3", "label": "Odgłosy ogrodu", "volume": 0.6 } — the bottom bar has a button with "label"; nothing plays without a click; it loops, goes quiet when the tab is hidden. File: MP3, M4A, OGG or WAV (a page file up to 30 MB). Volume on a scene — the scene's "volume"
  "backdrop" — shared background: layers (as for slides: "gradient", "image", "glow", "vignette", "haze", "mesh", "waves" …) standing behind all scenes; scenes are then transparent, and their own background (colour "ground", layers "layers") lies in it and changes smoothly into the next one's
  "map" — where the scenes stand on the transition map in the editor: { "<scene key>" | "link:<id>" | "gate:{keyTag}" | "end": { "x", "y" } } — for the editor only
  "story" — a RUN (as in Cogita): questions, conditions, values; a presentation with the "question" module always has one (then the answers stay in the browser). { "base": "<knowledge base id>", "storage": "<area id>", "values": [...], "gates": [...] }
    "base" — the knowledge base (Cogita) in which the answers of signed-in people (and people from a form) count; left out — an example: answers, values and the place where someone stopped stay only in the browser
    "storage" — the area (with intake) the answers go to; left out — the person's private area
    "values" — [{ "id": "pkt", "label": "Punkty", "start": 0, "min": 0, "max": 10 }] — values of the run (points, closeness to a character)
    in the knowledge base the same run is the run {"look": "scenes", "presentation": "<address of this page>"} (Presentation → Transitions → “Run in Learning”): in Learning it plays this presentation, answers and place count in the base — without a copy
    "gates" — gates between scenes; the exit of a scene, a button or a question leads to a gate through "gate:{keyTag}":
      { "key": "czy-umie", "label": "Umie?", "type": "condition", "when": { "type": "answered", "of": "<question module id>", "correct": true }, "yes": "<scene key>", "no": "<scene key>" } — a condition (as in Cogita: "answered", "value" { "value": "pkt", "op": "ge", "than": 3 }, "visited" { "of": "<scene key>" }, "knowness", "time", "and"/"or"/"not" with "items")
      { "key": "punkt", "type": "set", "actions": [{ "type": "add", "value": "pkt", "by": 1 } | { "type": "set", "value": "pkt", "to": 0 }], "next": "{targetTag}" } — changes values, then leads on
  "scenes" — the list of scenes in order:
    "key" — the scene key (short, unique, e.g. "start"); module places point to a scene by its key
    "label" — the name in the bar; a link "#name" in a text leads to this scene
    "steps" — how many steps (stops) the scene has; by default 1
    "change" — how it replaces the previous one: "fade" (crossfade), "build" (the scene is there at once, its modules arrive each their own way — "arrive"), "fly" (the camera flies through the PREVIOUS scene — its modules with depth and the word cloud), "rise", "zoom", "cover", "reveal", "side", "cut", "dissolve" (dissolve: the previous one fades, blurs and sinks by 12 px, this one sharpens while rising — like the Cogita show)
    "keep" — true: the previous scene stays underneath until the transition ends (with "fade", "build", "rise")
    "duration" — how long the jump to this scene takes in ms (by default 700, with "fly" 1700)
    "colors" — { "accent", "ink", "ground" (scene background), "muted" } — left out: like the whole presentation
    "layers" — background layers (as for slides, without moving)
    "grow" — { "from": 0.8, "to": 1.08 } — the scene grows from the entrance to the last step
    "follow" — { "wide": 0.45, "tall": 1 } — how strongly the scene moves so that the highlighted module stands in the middle (wide / narrow screen)
    "emphasis" — false: steps don't highlight modules (by default true: the non-highlighted ones fade and move away from the middle)
    "thread" — a thread through the modules with steps, in step order: "none", "line", "dots"
    "hint" — a small hint at the bottom (e.g. "Scroll"); it disappears when you move on
    "words" — a word cloud in the depth: { "list": ["colligere", …], "prefix": "RE", "count": 39, "seed": 7, "color": null }
    "depth" — { "perspective": 1000, "travel": 2200, "linger": true } — the scene's depth and how far the camera flies; "linger" — slows down at the deepest module
    "next" — where “next” leads (arrows, scrolling): a scene key, "end" (the end here) or "link:<id>"; left out — the next scene on the list
    "about" — in a story with a knowledge base ("story.base"): what the scene is about — entries of that base, ["@kurs/temat"] (id or @name); the story's path (module "path", Learning) places the scene next to them — so the introduction and the place where the ways meet stand on the map too, though they have no question (questions add what they are about themselves)
    "volume" — how loud the ambient sound ("sound") is on this scene, 0–1 (left out — 1; 0 — silence); it changes smoothly between scenes

A module's "show":
  "places" — { "<scene key>": place } — one place: the module belongs to that scene; several: it travels
    place: { "x": 50, "y": 50, "w": 30, "h": null, "max": null, "rotate": 0, "scale": 1, "opacity": 1, "z": 0, "step": null, "tall": null }
      "x", "y" — the module's point (usually the centre — see "origin") in percent of the scene; "w" — width in percent of the width; "h" — height in percent of the height (null — like the content)
      "max" — at most this width in rem (e.g. 22): on a large screen the module doesn't grow further, on a phone it takes "w" percent
      "z" — depth in pixels (0 flat, −980 far away); "step" — in which step of the scene it is highlighted (from 0)
      "tall" — other values on a narrow screen: { "x", "y", "w", "h", "max", "scale", "rotate", "crop", "mask" } (only those that differ)
      "crop" — the crop point of the image at this place: "57% 40%", "center", "left top" — with cropping ("fit": "cover" of the "image" module, an image in the "media" frame) this point stays in view when the field changes size (the focus stays the focus, on a phone too — "crop" in "tall"); left out — the image's "at"; it changes smoothly in frames
      "mask" — what of the module is visible: a circle { "shape": "circle", "r": 40, "x": 50, "y": 50 } ("r" — radius in %; 71 reaches the corners when the centre is in the middle), an oval { "shape": "ellipse", "rx": 60, "ry": 40, "x": 50, "y": 50 } ("rx" — % of the width, "ry" — % of the height), a rectangle { "shape": "inset", "top": 10, "right": 10, "bottom": 10, "left": 10, "round": 1.5 } (insets in %, "round" — corners in rem); null — the whole module; in frames masks of the same shape change smoothly, and a mask from null grows from the whole
      "frames" — FRAMES driven by the scene's progress (not a clock), at most 16: [{ "at": 0.4, "x": 30, "w": 40, "h": 55, "crop": "50% 60%" }, …] — "at" 0–1 of the progress or "step": the scene's step number (from 0) instead of "at"; a frame changes only what it gives ("x", "y", "w", "h", "max", "rotate", "scale", "opacity", "z", "crop", "mask"), the rest stays as in the frame before it; the place itself is the state at 0; the module moves smoothly to each frame with its "ease" ("inOut" — usual, "linear", "in", "out"); after the last one it stays; a frame without changes holds the state (e.g. { "at": 0.3 } — stands until 0.3); "tall" in a frame — its other values on a phone
      "by" — what the frames' progress is: "scene" (usual) — the inside of the scene: 0 at the first step, 1 at the last (the scene must have at least 2 "steps"; with 1 step it stands at 0); "enter" — the scene's entrance: 0 when the transition from the previous one starts, 1 when the scene is there; "leave" — the scene's exit: 0 at the last step, 1 when the next one is already there
      "still" — with “reduce motion”: at which progress (0–1) the frames stand — a still composition with the same headings, images and buttons; left out — at the end (with "leave" — at the beginning), and frames with "step" then jump from step to step, without the way between
  "skin" — the frame: "plain" (no background), "card" (a panel), "bubble" (a bubble), "pill" (a pill), "panel" (a field filling "w"×"h")
  "type" — only "text": "auto" (as on the page), "display" (a huge sentence — the page heading), "title" (capitals), "heading" (a heading with content), "kicker" (a heading in the accent colour with content), "body" (paragraphs), "close" (the punchline: italics in the accent colour, an empty line separates groups), "note" (a small note)
  "fill", "ink", "accent" — background, text and accent colour (links, punchline): "#rrggbb", a pair "light|dark" or a name: "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted"
  "origin" — which point of the module stands on "x", "y": "center" (default), "top-left", "top", "top-right", "left", "right", "bottom-left", "bottom", "bottom-right"
  "media" — an image in the frame: { "url", "at": "57% 50%", "fit": "cover"|"contain", "size": 60, "max": null, "opacity": 1, "fade": true, "side": "after"|"before"|"behind" } — with "contain": "size" in percent of the place, "max" at most this many rem
  "align", "valign" — "start", "center", "end"
  "arrive" — how it appears: "none", "fade", "rise", "zoom", "grow", "left", "right", "from-left", "from-right", "from-top", "from-bottom" (with "from-…" it comes in from beyond the edge)
  "delay", "span" — when in the transition it starts (0–1) and what part of it it lasts (0–1)
  "ease" — the travelling module's motion: "inOut", "linear", "in" (accelerates), "out"
  "hold" — true: it also stands before its first and after its last place
  "between" — a module with places on scenes NOT in a row: "glide" — glides through the scenes in between (usual), "leave" — leaves with its scene and comes back with the next one where it has a place (the same image at the beginning and at the end of a story, and not in the middle); it then always stands in the scene it is on — like its own module
  "layer" — higher is in front; a travelling one with a negative value (-1 … -5) stands in front of the scene background but behind its texts (a photo over the whole scene, and a caption on it) — in the scene of its first place, with "between": "leave" in the scene it is just on; a travelling one from 10 stands above all scenes
  "go" — the module is a button: { "<scene key>": target } — on this scene a click leads to the target (a scene key, "end", "link:<id>", "step" — to this module's own step on this scene: highlights it, the scene stays, "step:2" — to step 3 of this scene; "" — nowhere yet); instead of a scene key "*" — on every scene the module stands on (e.g. a fixed button “Contact” with "hold": true), a scene key takes precedence over "*"; a question ("question") has result exits instead: { "<scene key>:right": target, "<scene key>:wrong": target } — where “Next” leads after a right and after a wrong answer (left out — the scene's “next”); the target can also be a gate "gate:{keyTag}"
  "motion" — motion by the clock (description: Motion): once, when the scene is reached (e.g. { "name": "rise", "delay": 220 } — the text rises on arrival), or in a loop, as long as the module is visible; independent of "arrive", which follows the scrolling; with "by" ("scene", "enter", "leave") the motion follows the scene's progress instead of the clock — e.g. { "name": "keys", "by": "enter", "keys": [{ "at": 0, "clip": "circle(0% at 50% 50%)" }, { "at": 1, "clip": "circle(75% at 50% 50%)" }] } — the photo is revealed through a growing circle as the scene enters

Text ("text") in a presentation and on a page: "## " — a subheading, "# " — a large line, "> " — a small, quiet line, [caption](https://… | #/strona | #scena | mailto:… | tel:…) — a link; a line of only links is a row of links.
text.appointments:
A page can bring appointments (a retreat, a pilgrimage, a festival) together with their programme. The import ADDS them to calendars — each import anew (two imports are the same appointments twice). Appointments already in a calendar are shown by the page with a module through their id, not through "appointments".
Entrances ("calendars"): each entrance is a place the appointments go to; on import the importing person chooses for each entrance one of their calendars they can write in (like the area for the answers to a form's new questions).
  entrance: { "key": a short name (letters, digits, - and _), "label": how the importing person will see it, "calendar": calendar id — only a suggestion }
  An appointment without "calendar" goes to the entrance "{entry}"; an entrance without a description in "calendars" works too (its name is its "key").
Appointment (an entry in "appointments"):
  "key" — a short name by which modules point to this appointment: "@name" (e.g. "item" of the "program" module)
  "calendar" — the entrance (= "key" from "calendars"); programme points go to the calendar of their appointment
  "title" — the appointment's name (required)
  "start" — "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM" (local time) or "YYYY-MM-DD" (all day); in a programme point "HH:MM" is enough (the day of its appointment), and without "start" a point starts together with its appointment
  "end" — the same; "HH:MM" is the same day; for all day — the last day (inclusive); without "end": an hour, for all day — one day
  "allDay" — true: all day (also when "start" has a time)
  "location", "notes" — place and description
  "link", "linkLabel" — “More information”: an address https://… or #/path and the text on the button
  "repeat" — only an appointment (not a point): "none", "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "yearly"; "every" — every how many (1–99); "weekdays" — with "weekly": ["pn", "wt", "śr", "cz", "pt", "so", "nd"] (without them — the day of "start"); "until" — "YYYY-MM-DD" the last day (without it — no end)
  "points" — programme points: a list of appointments (the same keys, without "calendar" and "repeat"), also with their own "points" — at most {depth} levels; at most {max} appointments together with points
Modules point to appointments and entrances through "@name": "program" — "item": "@appointment name" (an empty "calendar" gets this appointment's calendar by itself, or "calendar": "@entrance"); "calendar" — "calendars": "@entrance" (also next to ids, separated by commas). After the import real ids stand there.

text.images:
A page can ask for files that don't exist yet — photos, a short video, a sound, a document to download. Describe each in "images", and where it should stand write "{prefix}key" instead of "page-image:<id>" — in a module, in a background layer, in a presentation scene, in the menu, wherever an image or file address stands. Before the import the importing person adds a file to each description (or chooses a file the page already has); the import uploads them to the page's files (public like the page) and puts them in every place with "{prefix}key".
File description (an entry in "images"):
  "key" — a short name (letters, digits, - and _), the same as in "{prefix}key"
  "label" — a short title the importing person will see (without it — "key")
  "description" — what the file should show: subject, framing, time of day, mood, landscape or portrait and what it will serve for — the importing person chooses the file by it
  "name" — the file name, if known (e.g. "IMG_3240.jpg"): files with this name are assigned by themselves, also those the page already has
  "kind" — "image" (usual: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF, up to 8 MB), "video" (MP4 or WebM, up to 30 MB), "sound" (MP3, M4A, OGG or WAV, up to 30 MB) or "file" (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, GPX or an image, up to 25 MB)
A description nobody added a file to: its places stay empty (a module without an image) — the import says so, and you add the file later in the editor. "{prefix}key" without a description in "images" works too — the importing person gets it without a description. At most {max} files.

text.intro:
What the import does:
- The document describes the whole page: title, text, look (a page with modules or slides), colours, menu, logic map and modules — each with its content. A key not in the document stays unchanged on the page.
- Export → change → import changes the page IN PLACE: a module with an "id" from the export stays the same module (with its registrations, people's links and place in the logic map). A module without "id" is created new.
- “Replace the page's modules”: the page's modules become exactly those from the document, the others disappear from the page. Without it the modules from the document are changed or added, and the rest stays.
- The import saves at once. An export before the import is a backup.
- An event document from the old system ({ "title", "pages": [{ "parts": [...] }] }) and a single module ("{module}") are accepted too — the latter is added to the page.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments.
text.keys:
"format" — "{format}"
  "version" — 1
  "path" — information only; the import always goes to the open page
  "title" — the page title
  "lead" — the text under the title (or null)
  "mode" — "page": modules on a grid; "slides": each module is a separate slide; "presentation": scenes with modules anywhere (below: Presentation)
  "lang" — the page language: "en", "de" or "pl" — every visitor sees the app's texts on this page in this language; left out or null — everyone in their own language (the content is written by the author and not translated)
  "theme" — colours: null (automatic — as in the app) or { "mode": "dark"|"light", "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted" } (colours "#rrggbb"); with "night": { "accent", "ink", "ground", "muted" } the page follows the device — light colours by day, these at night
  "cover" — the title slide background: a list of layers (below)
  "show" — presentation scenes (below: Presentation)
  "deck" — the slide show as a whole (only "mode": "slides"): { "backdrop": [layers], "nav": "labels"|"dots"|"none", "titleSlide": true|false, "width": 80 }
      "backdrop" — shared background: layers (as below) that stand behind all slides and lie UNDER their own layers — so the shared background's gradient doesn't cover the slides' images; the slides move over it transparent, and their own layers travel with their slide (in its rectangle): in a transition they move up with it, fade or get covered like it — nothing of the previous slide stays on the next one; a slide without its own layers is transparent (the shared background shows through)
      "nav" — the bar: slide names at the top (usual), dots on the right, no bar; "titleSlide": false — no title slide (the first module is the first screen)
      "width" — at most this many rem of stage width: the places of modules moving between slides and the slides' "layout" count within it (null — the whole window)
  "menu" — null (no menu), a list of items or { "from": "path" } (the same menu as on another of your pages)
      item: { "label", "kind": "abs" (path from the root, e.g. "parafia/zapisy") | "rel" (relative to this page) | "url" (full address) | "none" (heading only), "target", "children": [items], "image" }
      "image" — an image instead of the name (logo): "page-image:<id>" (an image of this page), "https://…" or "/logo.svg"; "label" stays — a screen reader reads it and it shows when the image is missing
  "subject" — choice on the page: at the top of the page one thing is chosen, and modules (e.g. "entry-panel") show it. {subject}
  "logic" — the page's logic map (when which module is visible, the person's steps) or null. It's easiest to build it in the editor; in JSON: { "version": 1, "nodes": [...], "edges": [...] }
      node: { "id", "kind", "x", "y", ... } — kind: {nodes}
      "part" has "partId" (= the module's "id") and "message"; "step" has "label", "help", "dueAt" (YYYY-MM-DD), "goto" (= the module's "id");
      "registered"/"confirmed"/"answer"/"mark" have "formId"; "answer" — "fieldId", "op" ("filled"|"empty"|"eq"|"ne"), "valueHash"; "mark" — "stepId", "markBy" ("office"|"person"); "date" — "when" ("after"|"before"), "date"
      edge: { "id", "from", "to", "port": "show"|"done"|"applies"|"in" }
  "modules" — modules in reading order
  "appointments" — appointments for the calendar, with a programme (points and sub-points): the import ADDS them to calendars the importing person chooses (below: Appointments for the calendar); the export doesn't contain them
  "calendars" — entrances for appointments: which calendars they should go to (the importing person chooses a calendar for each entrance)
  "images" — files the page needs that don't exist yet (photos, a video, a sound, a document), each with a description: the importing person adds them before the import, and the import puts them everywhere "{prefix}key" stands (below: Files to add); the export doesn't contain them
text.texts: A short text (a greeting, an announcement, a few sentences) stays in the module — e.g. "text". A longer text (a sermon, a conference, a meditation, a chapter) lives in the Scriptorium and is shown from there: the module "writing" (one text — with a plan, deliveries, footnotes) or "writings" (an archive of one scriptorium's texts). Then a correction in the Scriptorium is at once on every page, and the scriptorium's area decides who sees the text. Quotes are shown by the module "quotes" (from the Library). Texts in modules and on slides use the same markup as the Library, also colours: [words]{.red} — red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink, gray, mark ("mark" — highlighter).
text.usage:
- The page stands at recreatio.pl/#/<page path> (also under an alias or an own domain pointing to it) — as a grid of modules, slides or a presentation ("mode").
- The menu ("menu") stands on this page and on pages that take it through { "from" }; subpages don't inherit it.
- Modules read data live: calendars ("calendar", "program"), forms, Scriptorium texts, Library quotes, knowledge bases, the area's conversation ("chat"). Everyone sees as much of them as they themselves can read.
- A module standing on several pages is one: changed content changes on each of them. A module taken off the page (also through “Replace the page's modules”) disappears only from it — a form with questions or registrations stays in “Modules”.
- A personal link from a form opens the page on which the person's modules (“Person's registration”, “Person's steps”…) show their registration, steps and conversations. The logic map ("logic") only hides modules in the browser — it is not a protection.
- A module of a public page can be embedded on another site as a widget (“Embed on another site” in the editor); the widget won't show a page with access.
- A public page is seen by everyone, without an account. It saves only when an area with a data controller responsible for it is named (“Who is responsible for this page” in the editor); the page footer says who is responsible for the content and has “Report content”.
- A page with access is seen by the people of its areas (account, link, personal link) and those who run it. The server also knows its content — unless the page is encrypted (Address tree → Settings).
- The page's files (photos, videos, documents) are not encrypted: whoever knows a file's address will open it — also from a page with access.
- The page title is visible in “Your pages” of those who run it or have access to it; the cards “Events” and “Business card” lead to the area's main page (without a business card they take its title and text); a knowledge base run in Learning can play the presentation.
- The page document doesn't change its address, access, encryption or the area responsible for it (the access of an area's pages is set by "access" in the area document).
- The preview before the import (preview.html; for AI assistants — the MCP server recreatio-preview) draws the page the way the import will make it, and saves nothing.

usage.title: How the app uses this data
usage.text:
- Contacts live in your „Only me” area, each sealed separately: only you see them, on every device where you sign in. They do not go into areas, conversations or forms.
- Contacts (#/workspace/contacts): a list searchable by name, number, company, role, group and e-mail address; "groups" filter the list.
- In the „sms” edition the phone keeps a copy of them in a separate address book account „REcreatio” — thanks to it the name shows during a call. The copy is changed in recreatio, not in the phone's book; removing the „REcreatio” account from the phone removes only the copies.
- In the app's SMS the name from recreatio takes precedence over names from other phone accounts. The SMS archive in the browser labels numbers with names from your contacts, and „New message” suggests recipients from them.
- A group can have its own SMS number (SMS → „Numbers and groups”, #/workspace/sms/numery): whoever belongs to it gets SMS from that number, unless the conversation has its own choice. The number is tied to the group name — write it in "groups" the same as before.
- The import sends no SMS and does not change numbers assigned to groups.

json.title: Contacts as JSON ("{format}", version {version})
json.intro:
What the import does (Contacts → „More” → „Import and export (JSON)”):
- A contact with an "id" from the export is changed in place — only the fields in the document; the rest stays.
- A contact without "id" is looked up among existing ones: the same label (first and last name) and a shared number — then it is completed (new numbers, addresses, groups are added; what was there stays). Otherwise a new one is created.
- It deletes nothing. Before saving you see the list of changes and warnings.
- Everything is sealed in this browser — the service only sees that contacts exist. In the „sms” edition the phone gets a copy at the next save.
- For phones and Google keep using vCard („Load vCard”, „Save … as vCard”); JSON is for corrections by hand and by AI.
Return ONE JSON object, without comments, at most {max} contacts.

json.description:
Address registry as JSON — format "{format}", version 1.

Document fields:
- format: always "recreatio/registry"
- areaName: name of the area (information only — the import goes to the area opened here)
- addresses[]: list of addresses
- addresses[].id: identifier of the place (from the export) — ignored on import; an address is recognised by its parts
- addresses[].address: the address as one text ("ul. Długa 5/3, 31-147 Kraków") OR an object with parts:
  street (street, without "ul."), house (house no.), unit (flat no.), locality (locality), district (district/estate),
  postcode (code "00-000"), post (post office). Each part may be empty; without a locality, the post office's locality counts.
- addresses[].household: the family at this address (optional; fields you don't give stay unchanged):
  family (family name, e.g. "Kowalscy"), people[] ({name, born "YYYY-MM-DD", note}), phone, email, notes, tags[] (labels),
  kolenda: { "YYYY": { status: {statuses}, date "YYYY-MM-DD", priest, note } }

Import: the same address (after normalising: letter case, Polish characters, "ul.") is the same place — it isn't created twice.
A family at an address that already has a family is completed. Family details are encrypted with the area's key in the browser.

How the app uses this data:
- The area's registry (“Registry and pastoral visit”) has the tabs Addresses, Pastoral visit, Import and JSON. Whoever reads the area reads it; whoever writes in it changes it.
- Addresses: places with families; search by address, surname and label ("tags").
- Pastoral visit: the year's visits from "kolenda" — filters Year, Status, Street, Day, Priest; “Plan” for the selected (day, priest); a list in order of day and address, “Print list”.
- Families and visits open only in a browser that has the area's key — search and filters work there too.
- Addresses are not encrypted. Their parts (streets, localities, districts, codes, post offices) are shared by the whole app: they also suggest the address in address questions in forms, on the person card and for the data controller.
- The import creates no appointments in the Calendar (the visit stays in the registry), no persons or accounts, and deletes nothing.
